squat.variant: Goblet squat — one dumbbell at chest
squat.summary: A squat with one dumbbell held at the chest. The hips and knees bend together, then straighten to bring you upright.
setup: Set the dumbbell on a stable surface within easy reach. Leave space for your elbows and hips.
Check that adjustable dumbbell plates or selectors are locked before lifting it.
Hold the dumbbell upright. Cup the underside of its top end in both palms, with fingers around it.
Bring it close to your upper chest. Point your elbows down; keep the weight below your chin.
Set feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart. Turn toes slightly out if comfortable.
Spread pressure across each heel and forefoot. Brace your abdomen and look ahead.
execution: Bend your hips and knees together. Let your hips move down between your legs.
Keep knees pointing the same way as toes and the dumbbell near your chest.
Stop at the lowest point where your feet stay flat and your trunk stays steady.
Press through both feet. Raise your hips and chest together until standing.
finish: Finish upright with the dumbbell still close to your body.
Lower it with both hands to its stable surface; do not drop it or reach far forward.
breathing: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you stand while keeping your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Weight moves away from the chest: bring it close or use a lighter dumbbell.
Heels rise or knees fall inward: shorten the descent and reset your stance.
Bouncing out of the bottom: slow the lowering phase.
squat.easierOption: Use a lighter dumbbell or practice a separately logged bodyweight squat.
squat.safety: Use a depth you can control without pain. Stop if you cannot hold the dumbbell securely.
squat.loadConvention: Enter the weight of the single dumbbell, not twice its weight; one descent and return equals one rep.
squat.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

terms.meaning: Tighten the muscles around your middle to keep your trunk steady.

bench.summary: A flat-bench barbell press. Your head, upper back and hips stay supported as the bar lowers toward your chest and rises again.
setup: Center the flat bench inside the rack. Check it is stable.
Lie down with eyes under the bar. Set both J-hooks so a small elbow bend lets you lift the bar clear without lifting your shoulders.

Set matching safeties just below your lowest planned bar position. With an empty bar, test that they catch it above your neck and chest when you relax your arch. If this cannot work, use another setup.
Check all pins are locked. Add equal plates to both sides and fit collars.
Plant both feet. Keep head, shoulders and hips on the bench; a small natural back arch is acceptable.
Grip evenly, slightly wider than shoulders, with thumbs around the bar. Keep wrists over forearms.
Draw shoulder blades together against the bench. Agree on lift-off and help signals with your spotter.
Straighten arms to clear the hooks, then move the bar over your chest. Pause before lowering.
execution: Lower slowly toward the middle-to-lower chest, keeping forearms near upright.
Let elbows angle away from your sides without spreading straight out at shoulder height.
Stop at a comfortable depth. Do not bounce or let the bar rest heavily on you.
Press up and slightly back to the start. Keep hips down and both ends level.
finish: With arms steady at the top, move the bar back until it meets both rack uprights.
Lower into both hooks. Check both sides hold the bar before releasing your grip.
breathing: Inhale on the controlled descent; exhale during the press. Reset between reps without prolonged breath-holding.
commonErrors: Wrists fold back: place the bar lower in the palm.
Hips lift or bar tilts: end the set and reduce load.
Reaching for hooks before the last press is complete.
bench.easierOption: Use a light training bar and rehearse the full unrack, press and rerack.
bench.safety: Practice safety use in person before loaded work. Stop a set before control fails; a written guide cannot check your setup.
bench.loadConvention: Enter total barbell mass: bar plus plates on both sides. Record flat-bench variant consistently.
bench.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

terms.meaning: The two rack supports that hold the bar between sets.

row.variant: Standing one-arm dumbbell row — unsupported hip hinge
row.summary: One arm rows a dumbbell while you stand in a hip hinge. There is no bench support in this variation.
setup: Place the dumbbell where you can pick it up without twisting.
Hold it in your right hand with thumb around the handle and palm toward your body.
Place your left foot a little forward and right foot back, keeping room between your feet.
Bend knees slightly and send hips back. Tip forward from the hips while keeping your back in its natural shape.
Brace your abdomen. Let the right arm hang under its shoulder; keep your free hand clear of the moving weight.
Look at the floor ahead so your neck follows the line of your back.
execution: Bend the right elbow and move it back beside your ribs.
Bring the dumbbell toward your side without turning your chest toward the ceiling.
Stop when the elbow reaches your trunk and your shoulder can stay steady.
Lower until the arm is long again. Keep the same hip and back position.
Complete the planned reps, then repeat with the other arm and opposite foot forward.
finish: Let the arm lower, then stand upright before repositioning.
Set the dumbbell down with bent hips and knees before changing sides.
breathing: Exhale while rowing; inhale while lowering.
commonErrors: Torso twists to lift: use less weight.
Shoulder rolls forward at the bottom: stop the reach sooner.
Back rises with each pull: reset the hip hinge.
row.easierOption: Use less weight and a slightly more upright hinge. A bench-supported row is a separate variation.
row.safety: End the set if you cannot keep your trunk still or the hinge causes pain.
row.loadConvention: Enter one dumbbell's weight. Reps are per side; note unequal side results separately rather than adding them together.
row.sourceNote: Mayo describes the unsupported standing one-arm row. A small split stance is an app setup choice that matches the catalog cue; Mayo uses comfortably spaced feet. Logging rules are app definitions.

terms.meaning: Bend at your hips by moving them back, with a small knee bend.

rdl.summary: The dumbbell Romanian deadlift starts from standing. You move your hips back to lower two dumbbells, then bring your hips forward to stand.
setup: Check the dumbbells are secure and leave a clear place to return them.
Pick up one in each hand using bent hips and knees; stand upright before starting reps.
Place feet about hip-width apart with heels and forefeet on the floor.
Hold weights at the front or sides of your thighs, palms toward your legs.
Soften both knees and keep that small bend during the movement.
Brace your abdomen. Keep arms long and neck in line with your back.
execution: Push hips backward as if closing a door behind you. Your torso tips forward as the weights descend.
Keep the dumbbells close to your thighs and shins; do not reach them out ahead.
Stop when you feel a mild hamstring stretch or just before your back position changes. The weights need not reach the floor.
Press through your feet and bring hips forward to return upright.
Finish tall, with ribs over hips, without leaning back.
finish: Finish the last rep upright with arms at your sides.
Bend hips and knees further to set the dumbbells down on their clear resting surface.
breathing: Inhale while lowering. Exhale as you stand; keep your middle firm.
commonErrors: Knees bend more throughout: the hinge becomes a squat.
Back rounds to reach lower: stop higher.
Dumbbells drift away or hips push too far forward at the top.
rdl.easierOption: Practice an unloaded hip hinge or use light dumbbells and a shorter range.
rdl.safety: Stop for pain or loss of grip. Learn an unfamiliar loaded hinge with qualified instruction.
rdl.loadConvention: Enter weight per dumbbell, not the pair's total. One lowering and return equals one rep.
rdl.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

terms.meaning: A deadlift variation that starts upright and lowers mainly by bending at the hips.
The lowering phase here, when the working muscles lengthen under load.

pushup.summary: An incline push-up places your hands above your feet. A higher hand support usually makes the press easier.
equipment: Fixed rail, wall or stable bench
setup: Choose a support that cannot slide, fold or tip when pushed. Test it before leaning on it.
Clear space for your head and chest near the support.
Put hands slightly wider than shoulders. Spread fingers and press palms into the surface.
Step feet back, about hip-width apart, until your body forms one sloping line.
Brace your abdomen and keep your neck in line with your body.
execution: Bend elbows back and out at a comfortable angle, roughly halfway between your sides and straight out.
Lower chest toward the support. Let hips and shoulders travel together.
Stop before you lose the straight body position; your chest does not have to touch.
Press through both palms and straighten elbows to return.
finish: Finish with arms steady.
Walk feet toward the support before taking hands away.
breathing: Inhale down; exhale as you press away.
commonErrors: Hips drop or rise first: use a higher support.
Elbows point directly sideways.
Head reaches forward instead of chest moving toward the support.
pushup.easierOption: Raise the hand support or use a wall.
pushup.safety: Keep fingers clear of gaps and edges. Stop if the support moves or the movement hurts.
pushup.loadConvention: Log reps and support height. No added weight is required; do not enter your full body mass as external load.
pushup.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

plank.summary: A forearm plank holds your body still on your forearms and toes. The target is time in a controlled position.
setup: Lay the mat flat with enough room for your full body.
Start on hands and knees.
Put elbows under shoulders and rest both forearms on the mat.
Extend one leg, then the other. Place toes about hip-width apart.
Look down between your forearms and tighten the muscles around your middle.
execution: Lift knees so forearms and toes carry your weight.
Set hips in line with your shoulders and legs; avoid a dip or high peak.
Keep gentle pressure through your forearms and keep breathing.
Hold only while this position stays steady. End early if it changes.
finish: Lower both knees to the mat.
Relax, then sit back or roll to your side before rising.
breathing: Take regular breaths throughout the hold; do not hold your breath to extend the time.
commonErrors: Low back sags or hips rise.
Elbows slide far ahead of shoulders.
Timer continues after you lose position.
plank.easierOption: Keep knees on the mat, making a straight line from head to knees.
plank.safety: Stop for pain. A knees-supported hold must be recorded as that variation.
plank.loadConvention: Log actual seconds held, not repetitions. Record toe or knee support; no added weight is prescribed.
plank.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

terms.meaning: Muscles work while you hold a position without moving.

deadbug.variant: Dead bug — alternating opposite arm and leg
deadbug.summary: The dead bug moves an opposite arm and leg while your trunk stays still on the floor.
setup: Lay a mat where your arms and legs can extend without hitting anything.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet on the floor.
Keep your head down and lift both arms toward the ceiling.
Lift thighs over hips with knees bent about 90 degrees; shins are roughly level.
Gently brace your abdomen so your lower back stays steady against the mat.
execution: Move your right arm behind your head while slowly straightening your left leg.
Stop before your ribs lift or your lower back arches. Hand and heel can stay well above the floor.
Bring both limbs back over your body with control.
Repeat with left arm and right leg. Count each side on its own.
finish: Return arms and legs to the start.
Put one foot down, then the other. Roll onto your side to sit up.
breathing: Exhale as you reach; inhale as you return. Keep breaths easy.
commonErrors: Back lifts as the leg lowers: shorten the reach.
Arm and leg move too fast.
Head lifts to watch the feet.
deadbug.easierOption: Move one limb at a time or keep the moving knee more bent.
deadbug.safety: Do not force your heel or hand to the floor. Use a smaller range if your trunk cannot stay still.
deadbug.loadConvention: Reps are per side: right arm with left leg is one on that side. Log side differences; external load is not required.
deadbug.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.
quickCues: Reach only as far as controlled

bw-squat.variant: Bodyweight squat — both feet on floor
bw-squat.summary: A squat using bodyweight. The hips and knees bend while both feet remain on the floor.
setup: Clear space around and behind you.
Stand with feet a little wider than hip-width.
Turn toes slightly outward if that feels natural.
Keep heel, base of the big toe and base of the little toe in contact with the floor.
Reach arms forward for balance, brace your abdomen and look ahead.
execution: Move hips back and down while knees bend.
Keep knees moving in the same direction as toes.
Lower only while your feet stay planted and your trunk stays controlled.
Push through the floor and raise hips and chest together to stand.
finish: Return fully upright without pushing hips far forward.
Pause before stepping out of your stance.
breathing: Inhale down; exhale while standing.
commonErrors: Heels rise: shorten the range.
Knees collapse inward.
Chest drops sharply to reach a lower depth.
bw-squat.easierOption: Use a fixed support for balance or reduce depth.
bw-squat.safety: Depth depends on your control and comfort. Stop if the movement causes pain.
bw-squat.loadConvention: One descent and return equals one rep. Log support and depth changes; body mass is not entered as added load.
bw-squat.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

calf.variant: Standing calf raise — bodyweight, both legs
calf.summary: A standing calf raise lifts both heels together. This version starts on level ground and uses bodyweight.
setup: Stand beside a support that will not move when you touch it.
Place feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart.
Keep toes facing forward or slightly outward in a comfortable stance.
Rest one or both hands lightly on the support.
Stand tall with knees straight but not pushed backward.
execution: Press the forefeet into the floor and raise both heels.
Rise only as high as you can keep your ankles from rolling in or out.
Pause briefly with your body upright.
Lower heels slowly until they touch the floor.
finish: Set both heels down fully.
Check your balance before removing your hand support.
breathing: Exhale up and inhale down without straining.
commonErrors: Bouncing the heels.
Bending knees to help lift.
Rolling onto the outer edges of the feet.
calf.easierOption: Use more hand support and a smaller heel rise.
calf.safety: A step-edge calf raise has a different range. Keep this version on level ground.
calf.loadConvention: Log reps for both legs together. This version uses no added load; record support used.
calf.sourceNote: Bodyweight adaptation of Mayo’s two-dumbbell calf raise. The linked demonstration uses added weight, so it is not an exact media match. Logging rules are app definitions.

pulldown.variant: Lat pulldown — bar in front of chest
pulldown.summary: A lat pulldown brings a high cable bar down in front of your chest while you sit with thighs held under a pad.
setup: Read the machine’s adjustment labels. Make changes with the weight stack resting.
Check that the bar is clipped securely to the cable and the cable is on its pulley.
Set the seat so both feet rest flat. Set the thigh pad snugly over your thighs, close to the knees, without pinching.
Insert the selector pin fully at a light stack setting.
Stand to take the bar with palms forward, hands a little wider than shoulders and thumbs wrapped around.
Sit under the pad while controlling the bar. Sit tall with a small, steady backward lean.
execution: Pull elbows down toward your sides as the bar moves in front of your face.
Bring it toward your upper chest without rocking farther back.
Stop when elbows cannot move lower without changing your posture; touching the chest is not required.
Let arms extend slowly overhead while keeping control of the cable.
finish: Let the stack settle gently as arms lengthen.
Keep holding the bar as you rise, then return it to its resting position before letting go.
breathing: Exhale as you pull; inhale on the return.
commonErrors: Bar travels behind the neck.
Torso rocks back to start the pull.
Stack slams down between reps.
pulldown.easierOption: Use less stack weight and a comfortable arm range.
pulldown.safety: Keep fingers clear of the stack. If the bar is out of reach, use the machine’s intended access method; do not climb the seat.
pulldown.loadConvention: Log the displayed stack setting and units, machine identity and attachment. Settings from different machines are not equivalent loads.
pulldown.sourceNote: Mayo supports the front-of-chest pulldown. Seat and pad guidance is general: controls and available positions vary by machine. Follow its labels. Logging rules are app definitions.

terms.meaning: The pin that chooses how many weight plates move.

bar-squat.variant: Barbell back squat — upper-back bar position
bar-squat.summary: A barbell back squat carries the bar across the upper-back muscles. The bar and your trunk stay steady as hips and knees bend.
equipment: Stable rack with J-hooks and safeties
setup: Clear the rack floor. Set both J-hooks just below your standing shoulder height and lock them.
Set both safeties just below the bar’s lowest squat position. Test a full rep with an empty bar before loading.
Check the rack is stable. Center the bar; load both ends evenly and fit collars.
Face the bar. Grip it evenly, wider than shoulders, with thumbs around it.
Duck under and place it on the upper-back muscles below your neck. Draw shoulder blades together to make a firm resting area.
Put both feet under the bar, brace your abdomen and stand to clear the hooks without rising onto your toes.
Take two or three short steps back, staying over the safeties. Set feet about shoulder-width with toes slightly out.
Check that the bar feels centered and your whole feet are on the floor.
execution: Bend hips and knees together. Keep knees moving in the direction of your toes.
Let your torso lean as needed while keeping the bar balanced over the middle of your feet.
Stop at the deepest position you control, before heels lift or your back shape changes.
Press through the floor. Raise hips and shoulders together until standing.
finish: Stand steady, then walk forward until the bar touches both rack uprights.
Bend knees slightly to lower the bar into both hooks. Confirm support before stepping out.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before each descent. Exhale as you rise; reset at the top. Avoid prolonged breath-holding.
commonErrors: Bar presses on the neck.
Heels lift or knees fall inward.
Hips shoot up while chest stays down.
Bar reaches only one hook when reracking.
bar-squat.easierOption: Rehearse with a light training bar. A goblet squat is a separate exercise and log.
bar-squat.safety: Learn how to lower a failed rep onto these safeties in person before loaded work. Do not attempt a load you cannot control.
bar-squat.loadConvention: Enter the bar plus all plates, not weight per side. Keep bar position and depth convention consistent.
bar-squat.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

terms.meaning: Rack parts below the bar that catch it if you cannot finish a rep.

ohp.variant: Standing dumbbell shoulder press — two dumbbells
ohp.summary: A standing dumbbell shoulder press moves two weights overhead without using a knee dip.
setup: Check ceiling height and leave space on both sides.
Choose weights you can bring to your shoulders without throwing them.
Stand about hip-width apart with knees soft and feet planted.
Bend elbows to curl the light dumbbells to shoulder height without swinging. Turn palms mostly forward; keep thumbs around the handles.
Place elbows slightly in front of your body with forearms under the weights.
Brace your abdomen and keep your ribs above your hips.
execution: Press both dumbbells upward while keeping feet and knees still.
Let arms lengthen overhead through a comfortable path; do not force the weights to touch.
Stop before you must lean back to go higher.
Lower slowly until the weights return beside your shoulders.
finish: Lower both weights to shoulder level with control.
Bring them down to your sides, then bend hips and knees to set them down.
breathing: Exhale up; inhale down.
commonErrors: Knees dip to launch the weights.
Back arches and ribs lift.
Wrists bend far back or weights drift behind the head.
ohp.easierOption: Use lighter dumbbells and a comfortable range. A seated press requires its own record.
ohp.safety: Do not force overhead range that causes pain. If you cannot lower the weights under control, use less weight.
ohp.loadConvention: Log weight per dumbbell and reps for both arms together. Do not combine standing and seated records.
ohp.sourceNote: ACE’s cited article explicitly describes the standing two-dumbbell shoulder press. The guide does not adopt the article’s muscle-ranking claims. Logging rules are app definitions.

split.variant: Static split squat — rear toes on floor
split.summary: A static split squat keeps one foot forward and one behind for the whole set. The rear foot stays on its toes, not on a bench.
setup: Stand next to a fixed rail if you need balance support.
Place one foot forward and one back, about hip-width apart from side to side.
Keep your front foot flat and rear heel raised, with rear toes on the floor.
Make the stance long enough that both knees can bend without crowding your feet.
Face hips and chest forward; brace your abdomen. Hold the support lightly if used.
execution: Bend both knees to lower your body between your feet.
Let the rear knee move toward the floor without striking it.
Keep front heel down and front knee following the toes. Stop at a depth you control.
Press mainly through the front foot to rise. Keep both feet in the same places.
Finish that side before changing the lead leg.
finish: Stand fully before bringing your feet together.
Reset the stance before doing the other side.
breathing: Inhale lowering; exhale rising.
commonErrors: Feet form one narrow line, causing wobbling.
Front heel lifts or knee falls inward.
Rear knee drops onto the floor.
split.easierOption: Use a fixed support and a shorter descent.
split.safety: Stop for pain or loss of balance. Rear-foot-elevated and stepping lunges are separate variations.
split.loadConvention: Log reps per lead leg, not the sum of both legs. Record support used; this variant has no added load.
split.sourceNote: NSCA discusses related lunge patterns. REP explicitly describes the stationary split squat and bodyweight option, though its main demonstration is loaded. This guide uses bodyweight; logging rules are app definitions.

bridge.variant: Glute bridge — bodyweight, both feet on floor
bridge.summary: A floor glute bridge lifts your hips while your shoulders and both feet stay on the floor.
setup: Lay the mat flat and sit near its middle.
Lie on your back with knees bent.
Place feet flat about hip-width apart, close enough that shins are near upright when hips rise.
Rest arms by your sides with palms down.
Keep head and shoulders on the mat and gently brace your abdomen.
execution: Press through both feet and squeeze your glutes to lift the hips.
Stop when shoulders, hips and knees form a line; do not arch higher through the low back.
Keep knees pointing in the same direction as your feet.
Lower hips slowly until they touch the mat.
finish: Rest hips fully on the floor.
Roll onto your side and use your hands to sit up.
breathing: Exhale as hips rise; inhale as they lower.
commonErrors: Lower back arches to gain height.
Knees spread or fall inward.
Weight shifts onto the neck or heels lift.
bridge.easierOption: Lift through a smaller range with both feet planted.
bridge.safety: Support weight through shoulders and feet, not your neck. Stop for pain.
bridge.loadConvention: One lift and lowering equals one rep. This floor version uses no added load; bench hip thrusts need a separate record.
bridge.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

terms.meaning: The muscles around your buttocks that help straighten the hips.

band-row.summary: A seated row pulls a resistance band toward your lower ribs. This version uses an anchor made for resistance-band exercise.
setup: Inspect the band and handles for cracks or tears. Do not use a damaged band.
Fit the anchor exactly as its maker directs at about lower-chest height when seated. Do not attach it to loose furniture.
Pull gently to check it is secure. Keep people out of the band’s path.
Sit facing the anchor with knees slightly bent and feet supported.
Take one handle in each hand with palms facing each other. Sit far enough back for light tension with arms extended.
Sit tall and brace your abdomen; keep shoulders relaxed.
execution: Bend elbows and draw them back close to your ribs.
Bring handles toward your lower ribs without leaning backward.
Pause with shoulders steady; avoid pushing elbows far behind your body.
Straighten arms slowly, controlling the band as it shortens.
finish: Let arms extend while keeping a firm grip.
Move closer until the band is slack before setting handles down.
breathing: Exhale pulling; inhale as arms lengthen.
commonErrors: Leaning back to stretch the band farther.
Shrugging shoulders.
Releasing stretched handles or using a loose anchor.
band-row.easierOption: Use a lighter band or move nearer the anchor while keeping slight starting tension.
band-row.safety: Follow the band’s stretch limit and anchor instructions. Never release a stretched band toward yourself or others.
band-row.loadConvention: Record band brand/level, anchor height and starting distance. Band color is not a kilogram value.
band-row.sourceNote: Adaptation: ACE’s seated-row page describes a cable machine; its band guide supports band selection, anchoring and controlled return. Neither is an exact demonstration of this anchored seated-band setup. Logging rules are app definitions.

walk.summary: A brisk walk uses a purposeful pace that still lets you speak comfortably.
setup: Choose a clear, well-lit route with suitable footing.
Check weather and choose an indoor route if conditions are poor.
Tie your shoes and wear clothing that allows easy movement.
Start your timer where you can walk without looking down at it.
Stand upright with eyes on the route and shoulders relaxed.
execution: Begin with several minutes of easy walking.
Build gradually to your planned brisk pace.
Let arms swing naturally and take comfortable steps.
Slow down if speaking becomes difficult or footing needs more care.
finish: Walk more slowly for the last few minutes.
Stop the timer and record the minutes you actually walked.
breathing: Breathe naturally; you should still be able to speak comfortably.
commonErrors: Overstriding or forcing long steps.
Looking down at a phone while moving.
Keeping a fast pace despite difficult footing.
walk.easierOption: Walk more slowly or for less time on a flat route.
walk.safety: Stop for pain, dizziness, chest discomfort or unusual breathlessness; seek appropriate help for concerning symptoms.
walk.loadConvention: Log actual minutes; optionally record distance, route and terrain. No external weight is required.
walk.sourceNote: Mayo supports route choice, walking posture and a gradual warm-up and cool-down. Session duration and the logging convention belong to the app.

run.variant: Easy run / walk — follow the selected interval stage
run.summary: Follow the run and walk stages shown for this session. Easy running means a pace at which you can speak in short sentences.
setup: Read the session’s run/walk stages before starting; they may differ from the NHS plan.
Choose a clear route with even footing and room to slow down.
Check weather, tie shoes and carry water as conditions require.
Set the timer so stage alerts are easy to follow without staring at a screen.
Begin from standing with relaxed shoulders and eyes on the route.
execution: Complete the displayed walking warm-up.
When the running stage starts, ease into a comfortable jog with short, natural steps.
Keep effort conversational. Slow down or walk if you cannot speak comfortably.
At each walking stage, reduce speed smoothly and continue for its displayed time.
Follow the planned stage order; record any stages you shorten or replace with walking.
finish: Complete the displayed cool-down walk.
Record total actual minutes, including walking, and note any changed intervals.
breathing: Let breathing settle during walking stages. No fixed step-to-breath pattern is required.
commonErrors: Starting the first run too fast.
Skipping walks to chase distance.
Adding missed minutes at the end despite pain or poor control.
run.easierOption: Use more walking or repeat a manageable stage; record what you actually did.
run.safety: Stop for pain, dizziness, chest discomfort or unusual breathlessness. A timer does not establish readiness for a harder stage.
run.loadConvention: Log total actual session minutes including walks; record run/walk intervals and distance separately when available. Load is not a weight entry.
run.sourceNote: NHS supports gradual run/walk practice and walking warm-ups and cool-downs. The app’s selected sequence may be app-authored and is not presented as the NHS Couch to 5K schedule.

skill.variant: Coach-selected sport skill practice — logging placeholder
skill.summary: This is a sport-practice tracker. The exact drill must come from your coach’s plan before technique instructions can be supplied.
equipment: Equipment listed in the selected drill
setup: Open the coach’s drill plan and record its name.
Check which equipment, area and partners that exact drill requires.
Use the drill’s stated equipment placement and starting positions.
Check the listed reps or time, rest, and when to stop.
If those details are missing, leave the drill unstarted until the coach supplies them.
execution: Start the timer only when the named practice begins.
Follow the selected drill’s movement sequence and coaching cues.
Record completed practice and any changes to the drill.
Do not count unperformed work or use this tracker as a technique score.
finish: End the timer when practice ends.
Record actual minutes and the drill name; add other results in notes.
breathing: Use breathing guidance from the selected drill; this placeholder supplies no drill-specific breathing pattern.
commonErrors: Logging a drill without naming it.
Treating elapsed time as proof of skill.
Replacing missing instructions with an invented drill.
skill.easierOption: Use a simpler version only when your coach has selected and described it.
skill.safety: This entry cannot determine whether you can safely perform an unspecified sport skill.
skill.loadConvention: This tracker uses minutes. Log actual practice time and drill name; put reps, distance or external load in notes when relevant. Completion does not certify skill.
skill.sourceNote: USA Volleyball provides sport-specific coaching resources, not a universal drill for this entry. No exact drill is specified or verified; this guide only explains the tracker.

deadlift.variant: Barbell deadlift — conventional stance from floor
deadlift.summary: A conventional barbell deadlift lifts a bar from the floor to standing. Feet stay inside the hands; each rep starts from a settled bar.
equipment: Full-diameter light technique plates if needed
setup: Clear both ends of the bar. Use level flooring so it cannot roll.
Load equal plates on each side and secure collars. Use a start height you can reach with a controlled back position.
Stand about hip-width apart with the bar over the middle of your feet and close to your shins.
Push hips back and bend knees to reach the bar. Grip just outside your legs, both palms toward you and thumbs around it.
Keep arms long. Bring shins near the bar without pushing it forward.
Set your back in its natural shape, look at the floor ahead and brace your abdomen.
Gently take tension through your arms until bar and plates feel connected; do not jerk.
execution: Push through the floor and straighten knees and hips together.
Keep the bar close to your legs and arms straight; the hands hold the bar rather than curl it.
Finish standing tall with hips under your shoulders. Do not lean back or shrug.
Push hips back to lower the bar down your thighs.
Once the bar passes your knees, bend knees further and set both ends on the floor.
Let plates settle and reset before each rep.
finish: Lower the final rep fully to the floor.
Release your grip only after the bar is still, then stand and step away.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before each rep; exhale as you stand. Reset breathing when the bar is settled. Avoid prolonged breath-holding.
commonErrors: Jerking the bar from the floor.
Hips rise before the bar moves.
Bar drifts away from the legs.
Leaning back at the finish or bouncing the next rep.
deadlift.easierOption: Use less weight. If floor height is beyond your controlled range, use a separately logged raised-start variation with stable lifting blocks.
deadlift.safety: Learn an unfamiliar loaded deadlift in person. If grip or back control changes, lower the bar and end the set.
deadlift.loadConvention: Enter total bar plus plates. Record conventional stance and start height; sumo, trap-bar and Romanian deadlifts need separate records.
deadlift.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

terms.meaning: A deadlift stance with feet inside the hands.
The controlled lowering phase of this lift.

leg-curl.variant: Machine leg curl — lying face down
leg-curl.summary: A lying leg curl bends both knees while the front of your body rests on the machine pad.
setup: Check the machine’s diagram for its pad and roller adjustments; keep the stack resting while adjusting.
Choose a light stack setting and push the selector pin fully in.
Lie face down with hips and chest supported. Line the sides of your knees up with the machine’s pivot, where its arm turns.
Adjust the leg roller so it rests behind your lower legs just above the ankles, not on your heels.
Set the starting range so legs are nearly straight without forcing knees backward. Lock every adjustment.
Hold the handles lightly. Keep head in line with your back and hips on the pad.
execution: Bend both knees to move heels toward your buttocks.
Stop before hips lift or your low back arches.
Pause briefly without pulling hard on the handgrips.
Lower the roller slowly until legs return to the chosen start.
finish: Let the weight stack settle without slamming.
Free your lower legs from the roller and rise using the machine’s fixed supports.
breathing: Exhale curling; inhale lowering.
commonErrors: Hips lift to finish the curl.
Neck cranes upward.
Arms yank the handles or stack drops on return.
leg-curl.easierOption: Reduce stack weight and use the range you can control without moving your hips.
leg-curl.safety: Follow this machine’s labels. Do not use it if the knee and pivot cannot line up or a pad causes pain.
leg-curl.loadConvention: Log displayed stack setting and units, machine identity, pad and roller settings. Keep 'lying' distinct from seated curls; count one curl with both legs as one rep.
leg-curl.sourceNote: Mayo describes the lying curl; Precor confirms knee-pivot alignment and adjustable ankle support on its prone model. Exact adjustment controls vary by machine. Logging rules are app definitions.

leg-extension.summary: A seated leg extension straightens both knees while your back and thighs remain supported.
setup: Read the machine’s diagram. Make seat and roller changes while the stack rests.
Set a light stack load and insert the selector pin fully.
Sit back. Move the back pad so the sides of your knees line up with the machine’s pivot and the seat supports your thighs.
Adjust the roller onto the front of your lower legs just above the ankles, clear of the feet.
Set the starting angle to a comfortable bend, often near 90 degrees, using the machine’s range control if provided.
Lock the adjustments. Hold the side handles, sit tall and keep hips against the seat.
execution: Straighten both knees to lift the roller.
Stop with knees nearly straight; do not snap them into a hard lock.
Keep thighs on the seat and pause briefly.
Lower slowly to the same starting knee bend.
finish: Settle the stack gently.
Move your feet clear of the roller before standing.
breathing: Exhale extending; inhale returning.
commonErrors: Hips lift from the seat.
Knees do not line up with the machine pivot.
Kicking the roller or letting the stack slam.
leg-extension.easierOption: Use less weight and a comfortable machine-approved range.
leg-extension.safety: Do not force a painful knee range. If the machine cannot fit your legs, use another suitable setup.
leg-extension.loadConvention: Log the displayed stack setting and units, machine identity, seat and roller settings. Do not compare different machines as equal loads.
leg-extension.sourceNote: Mayo supports controlled seated knee extension. Precor confirms back-pad adjustment for knee-pivot alignment on its model. Controls differ by machine. Logging rules are app definitions.

incline-press.variant: Incline dumbbell chest press — both arms
incline-press.summary: An incline dumbbell press uses a raised backrest. Both weights move together while your head, upper back and hips stay supported.
equipment: Spotter for weights you cannot safely position
setup: Set the backrest to your chosen incline; 45 degrees matches the lower end of the ACE source range. Record the angle.
Seat every adjustment pin fully. Press on the bench to check it is stable before adding weight.
Sit with dumbbells resting upright on your thighs. Use weights you can bring into place with control.
Lean back onto the pad as you guide the weights toward your shoulders. Arrange a spotter’s handoff if needed.
Plant feet on the floor or a stable foot platform. Keep head, upper back and hips on the bench.
Turn palms forward. Set wrists over elbows and gently draw shoulder blades against the pad.
execution: Press both weights above your upper chest until arms are long.
Lower slowly toward the outer upper chest, keeping wrists above elbows.
Stop at a comfortable depth without letting shoulders roll forward.
Press upward along the same path without bouncing or colliding the dumbbells.
finish: Lower weights toward your shoulders. With light weights, bring them back to your thighs as you sit upright; use the arranged handoff if needed.
Keep your grip until the weights are fully supported, then return them to storage.
breathing: Inhale lowering; exhale pressing.
commonErrors: Back arches farther with each rep.
Weights tilt because wrists bend back.
Bench angle changes between logs without being recorded.
incline-press.easierOption: Use lighter dumbbells and rehearse getting in and out of position.
incline-press.safety: Choose weights you can safely position and finish with. Do not drop weights beside the bench or twist to reach the floor.
incline-press.loadConvention: Enter weight per dumbbell, not the combined pair. Record the bench angle because changing it changes the variation.
incline-press.sourceNote: ACE describes an incline of 45–60 degrees. This guide uses 45 degrees as a reproducible starting example, not a universal optimum. Log other bench angles distinctly; logging rules are app definitions.

lateral.summary: A dumbbell lateral raise lifts both arms out to the sides. The elbows stay slightly bent as shoulders move the weights.
setup: Leave enough room for both arms to reach out without hitting anything.
Hold one dumbbell in each hand with thumbs around the handles and palms toward your thighs.
Stand about hip-width apart with knees soft.
Keep a small elbow bend and wrists straight.
Brace your abdomen and let shoulders rest away from your ears.
execution: Raise both arms out and slightly forward, keeping the same elbow bend.
Let elbows and upper arms rise together; keep thumbs level or slightly up.
Stop around shoulder height or sooner if that is your comfortable range.
Lower smoothly to your sides without letting weights fall.
finish: Bring both dumbbells to a still position beside your thighs.
Bend hips and knees to set them down.
breathing: Exhale lifting; inhale lowering.
commonErrors: Knees dip or torso swings to start.
Shoulders shrug toward ears.
Hands tip down as if pouring water.
lateral.easierOption: Use lighter dumbbells and a shorter lift.
lateral.safety: Stop for shoulder pain; do not force a higher range.
lateral.loadConvention: Enter weight per dumbbell; one simultaneous lift and lowering equals one rep. Record standing versus seated variants separately.
lateral.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

curl.variant: Dumbbell biceps curl — standing, palms up
curl.summary: A standing dumbbell biceps curl bends both elbows while palms face forward and then upward.
setup: Check that both weights are secure and leave room beside you.
Stand about hip-width apart with knees soft.
Hold one dumbbell in each hand, thumbs around the handles.
Let arms hang beside your body with palms facing forward.
Keep wrists straight, shoulders relaxed and abdomen firm.
execution: Bend both elbows to raise the weights toward your shoulders.
Keep upper arms close to your sides instead of swinging elbows forward.
Stop before the wrists bend or the shoulders help lift.
Lower slowly until arms are long again without forcing the elbows backward.
finish: Let weights settle at your sides.
Use bent hips and knees to put them down with control.
breathing: Exhale curling; inhale lowering.
commonErrors: Torso leans back to start the curl.
Elbows travel forward.
Wrists bend to bring the weights closer.
curl.easierOption: Use lighter dumbbells. Record a seated or alternating version separately.
curl.safety: Stop if you cannot hold the weights without swinging or if the movement causes pain.
curl.loadConvention: Enter weight per dumbbell. Reps are per arm; simultaneous curls count once per pair, not twice. Note alternating or seated versions separately.
curl.sourceNote: Based on the linked instructions for this variation. The guide has not had an independent technique review. Logging instructions describe how to record it here.

triceps.variant: Cable triceps pushdown — high pulley, two arms
triceps.summary: A high-cable triceps pushdown straightens both elbows while the upper arms remain beside the torso.
setup: Set the pulley above your head with the stack resting. Lock the height pin.
Clip on the chosen bar or rope and check the clip closes fully. Use the same attachment for comparable logs.
Choose a light stack setting and insert the selector pin fully.
Face the machine with feet hip-width apart or one slightly forward.
Grip a bar palms down or hold the rope ends palms facing each other; wrap thumbs securely.
Bring elbows beside your ribs with forearms bent. Stand tall, brace your abdomen and keep wrists straight.
execution: Straighten elbows to press the attachment toward your thighs.
Keep upper arms by your sides and torso still.
Pause with arms nearly straight without snapping the elbows backward.
Let elbows bend slowly until the attachment returns toward your lower chest, before elbows move forward.
finish: Guide the attachment up until the stack rests.
Release it only once the cable tension is settled.
breathing: Exhale pressing down; inhale returning.
commonErrors: Leaning body weight onto the attachment.
Elbows swing forward or out.
Wrists bend or stack slams.
triceps.easierOption: Lower the stack setting and keep a controlled range.
triceps.safety: Keep hands clear of cable and stack pinch points. Do not let the attachment snap upward.
triceps.loadConvention: Log stack setting, units, machine and attachment. Rope, bar and overhead extensions are distinct variations; settings do not transfer across machines.
triceps.sourceNote: ACE explicitly covers high-pulley bar and rope pushdowns. Record which attachment you used; the two setups are not interchangeable load records. Logging rules are app definitions.

core-floor-crunch.summary: Lift your shoulders with a small curl of your upper back. Your feet and hips stay on the floor.
setup: Spread the mat on a firm floor with room for your whole body.
Sit down, then lower onto your back.
Bend your knees and place both feet flat, about hip-width apart.
Rest your fingertips beside your ears with elbows open. Do not clasp your hands behind your neck.
Leave a small space between your chin and chest. Let your lower back rest comfortably on the mat.
execution: Tighten your belly and slowly curl your ribs toward your hips.
Lift until your shoulder blades just leave the mat; keep your hips and feet down.
Pause briefly, then lower your upper back and head gently. Count that full curl and return as one rep.
finish: After the last rep, rest your head and shoulders, then roll to your side to sit up.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl up; breathe in as you lower.
commonErrors: Pulling the head forward with the hands.
Sitting all the way up or bouncing off the mat.
core-floor-crunch.easierOption: Reach both hands toward your knees and make a smaller curl.
core-floor-crunch.safety: Stop if the movement causes neck or back pain.
core-floor-crunch.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; count each curl as one repetition.
core-floor-crunch.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE describes the floor crunch. The self-entry steps and app counting rule are added wording.

terms.meaning: One complete curl up and return.

core-dumbbell-crunch.summary: Do a small floor crunch while holding one dumbbell against your chest.
setup: Set the dumbbell beside the mat, clear of where your head will rest.
Sit with knees bent and feet flat; grip the dumbbell with both hands.
Hold it across your chest, then lower yourself onto your back without lifting the weight over your face.
Place feet hip-width apart and keep both soles on the floor.
Keep a firm two-hand grip, elbows near your sides, and a small gap under your chin.
execution: Curl your shoulders up by bringing your ribs toward your hips.
Keep the dumbbell against your chest and stop when your shoulder blades clear the floor.
Lower your upper back and head slowly. One curl and return is one rep.
finish: Finish with your shoulders down. Roll to your side while holding the weight, sit up, and place it on the floor.
breathing: Breathe out during the curl and in as you lower.
commonErrors: Moving the weight toward your face.
Throwing the arms forward to start the curl.
core-dumbbell-crunch.easierOption: Set the dumbbell aside and use the floor crunch.
core-dumbbell-crunch.safety: Use a weight you can hold securely through entry and exit; stop for neck or back pain.
core-dumbbell-crunch.loadConvention: Enter the total external load of the one dumbbell held at the chest, excluding bodyweight.
core-dumbbell-crunch.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE supports the crunch family only. This dumbbell-at-chest variant was not verified in an exact primary guide.

core-reverse-crunch.summary: Curl your hips a little off the floor while keeping your knees bent.
setup: Lay the mat on a firm floor and lie on your back.
Place arms a little away from your sides with palms down for balance.
Bend your knees, then lift one foot and the other.
Set knees above your hips with shins roughly level to the floor.
Rest your head and shoulders on the mat; gently tighten your belly before moving.
execution: Tip your pelvis toward your ribs so your tailbone starts to lift.
Let your knees move a little toward your chest without changing their bend or swinging your feet.
Lower your hips slowly until they rest on the mat, with knees back above hips. Count one curl and return as one rep.
finish: Set one foot down, then the other. Roll to your side before sitting up.
breathing: Breathe out as the hips curl up and in as they lower.
commonErrors: Kicking the legs to lift the hips.
Lowering the knees away from the body until the back arches.
core-reverse-crunch.easierOption: Make only a small pelvic tip, leaving most of your hips on the floor.
core-reverse-crunch.safety: Keep weight off your neck and stop if your back hurts.
core-reverse-crunch.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; count each controlled pelvic curl as one repetition.
core-reverse-crunch.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE describes the reverse crunch. The shorter range option and logging explanation are added wording.

terms.meaning: The ring of bones around your hips.

core-bicycle-crunch.summary: Alternate a bent knee and the opposite shoulder while slowly reaching the other leg away.
setup: Lie on your back on a mat with clear space beyond your feet.
Place fingertips lightly beside your head; keep elbows open.
Lift bent knees over your hips, with lower legs level to the floor.
Gently tighten your belly so your lower back stays supported.
Lift your head and shoulder blades slightly, leaving a gap under your chin.
execution: Bring your right knee inward and turn your left shoulder toward it; let your left leg reach away.
Keep the straightening leg high enough that your lower back does not lift. Your elbow need not touch the knee.
Return through the middle, then bring the left knee inward and turn the right shoulder toward it.
Move at a slow, even pace. Each side counts as one rep; right plus left is two.
finish: Bend both knees, lower your shoulders, then place your feet down.
breathing: Keep breathing as you alternate; use a small breath out with each turn.
commonErrors: Pulling the neck to make elbow and knee meet.
Pedaling fast while the hips rock.
core-bicycle-crunch.easierOption: Keep one foot on the floor while you lift the other knee and turn toward it.
core-bicycle-crunch.safety: Stop for neck or back pain; shorten the leg reach if the back lifts.
core-bicycle-crunch.loadConvention: Count each side reached as one repetition; left plus right equals two repetitions.
core-bicycle-crunch.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE gives the bicycle movement. Added setup and easier-option wording needs review.

core-standing-cable-crunch.summary: Curl your ribs toward your hips while a high cable pulls upward on a rope.
setup: With the stack resting, clip the rope to one high pulley and close the clip fully.
Insert the selector pin all the way into a light weight setting. Set any extra add-on weight to zero.
Grip one rope end in each hand, with hands above the end stops. Face the station and pull the rope beside your shoulders.
Step back, feet about shoulder-width apart, and bend your knees slightly.
Keep hands near your shoulders and elbows bent. Start with ribs above hips and enough cable tension to avoid slack.
execution: Keep your hips nearly still as you curl your upper body toward your thighs.
Let your elbows travel with your chest; do not pull them down by straightening your arms.
Stop before you need to sit back or bounce, then slowly uncurl. One curl and return is one rep.
finish: Step toward the pulley until the stack rests, then release the rope.
breathing: Breathe out on the curl and in on the return.
commonErrors: Bending only at the hips.
Moving the rope with the arms while the chest stays still.
core-standing-cable-crunch.easierOption: Use less stack weight or switch to a floor crunch.
core-standing-cable-crunch.safety: Keep the rope off your neck; stop if the cable pulls you off balance.
core-standing-cable-crunch.loadConvention: Enter the single stack display, not a per-hand value; compare only the same pulley, attachment and stance.
core-standing-cable-crunch.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. Life Fitness shows a kneeling cable crunch with separate handles, facing away. It supports the family only, not this standing rope setup.

terms.meaning: The pin that chooses plates on a weight stack.
The wheel that guides the cable and sets its pulling direction.

core-kneeling-cable-crunch.summary: Curl your ribs toward your hips while a high cable pulls upward on a rope.
setup: With the stack resting, clip the rope to one high pulley and close the clip fully.
Insert the selector pin all the way into a light weight setting. Set any extra add-on weight to zero.
Grip one rope end in each hand, with hands above the end stops. Face the station and pull the rope beside your shoulders.
Kneel on padding, knees hip-width apart, far enough back that the rope clears your head.
Keep hands near your shoulders and elbows bent. Start with ribs above hips and enough cable tension to avoid slack.
execution: Keep your hips nearly still as you curl your upper body toward your thighs.
Let your elbows travel with your chest; do not pull them down by straightening your arms.
Stop before you need to sit back or bounce, then slowly uncurl. One curl and return is one rep.
finish: Move toward the pulley under control until the stack rests, then release the rope. Stand up after unloading the cable.
breathing: Breathe out on the curl and in on the return.
commonErrors: Bending only at the hips.
Moving the rope with the arms while the chest stays still.
core-kneeling-cable-crunch.easierOption: Use less stack weight or switch to a floor crunch.
core-kneeling-cable-crunch.safety: Keep the rope off your neck; stop if the cable pulls you off balance.
core-kneeling-cable-crunch.loadConvention: Enter the single stack display, not a per-hand value; record pulley, rope and kneeling position.
core-kneeling-cable-crunch.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. Life Fitness shows a kneeling cable crunch with separate handles, facing away. It supports the family only, not this kneeling rope setup.

terms.meaning: The pin that chooses plates on a weight stack.
The wheel that guides the cable and sets its pulling direction.

core-selectorized-crunch.summary: Use a weight-stack machine to curl your ribs toward your hips while seated.
setup: Read the machine picture to find its seat, foot supports, moving pads, and start position.
With the stack down, insert the pin fully into the lightest suitable setting; clear any add-on weight.
If the seat adjusts, take your weight off it, pull its lever or pin, move the seat, and release it into a locked hole.
Sit back. Set the seat so pads meet your upper chest or shoulders, as pictured, and feet reach the supports. Keep pads off your throat.
Set any start-range stop to a comfortable upright position. Grip the handles without shrugging.
Try one slow rep; stop and readjust if a pad slides onto your neck or you cannot keep your seat.
execution: Curl your ribs toward your hips, letting the machine arm move with your chest.
Keep your hips on the seat and avoid yanking the handles with your arms.
Return slowly to the start without dropping the stack. Count one curl and return as one rep.
finish: Let the stack settle fully before releasing the handles and stepping out.
breathing: Breathe out on the curl; breathe in as you return.
commonErrors: Using a seat setting that puts a pad on the neck.
Throwing your body forward to lift the stack.
core-selectorized-crunch.easierOption: Choose less weight or use a floor crunch.
core-selectorized-crunch.safety: Controls differ by model. If the picture does not match, use the model instructions before starting.
core-selectorized-crunch.loadConvention: Enter the selected stack display once; compare only the same machine and seat/pad settings.
core-selectorized-crunch.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. Manufacturer reference covers one Hammer Strength model, not every selectorized machine or its exact adjustment controls.

terms.meaning: A machine where a pin selects the plates you move.

core-plate-loaded-crunch.summary: Use a seated crunch machine with weight plates on its moving loading posts.
equipment: Retainers if the machine requires them
setup: Read the exercise picture and identify moving loading posts; fixed storage pegs do not add exercise load.
Start with the lever unloaded. Add small plates to loading posts, evenly if paired loading is required.
Fit required retainers. Keep hands out of the lever path.
If the seat adjusts, unload your body from it, pull its lever or pin, move it, then lock it. Lock any swivel seat facing forward.
Sit against the support, place feet on the marked supports, and grip the handles. Pads must not press on your throat.
Try the empty lever first; it may already feel heavy. Set any start stop so you can begin without a deep backward bend.
execution: Curl your ribs toward your hips, moving the handles with your chest.
Keep your seat on the pad and avoid pulling with your arms alone.
Slowly return until the lever rests at its start. One curl and return is one rep.
finish: Let the lever rest before leaving. Remove plates while the lever is supported.
breathing: Breathe out as you curl; breathe in as you return.
commonErrors: Loading storage pegs instead of moving posts.
Bouncing the lever or twisting the seat during a rep.
core-plate-loaded-crunch.easierOption: Use no added plates; if still too hard, use a floor crunch.
core-plate-loaded-crunch.safety: Follow the model picture for pad contact and loading. Stop for back or neck pain.
core-plate-loaded-crunch.loadConvention: Enter total plates loaded across all horns, excluding unknown lever starting resistance; use the same machine and settings.
core-plate-loaded-crunch.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. Manufacturer reference covers the PL-AB family example; controls and loading posts vary across machines.

terms.meaning: Clips or stops that hold plates on the loading posts.

core-hanging-knee-raise.summary: Hang from a fixed bar and lift both bent knees while keeping your body from swinging.
equipment: Stable step if needed to reach the bar
setup: Use an installed exercise bar rated for your bodyweight. Check that it does not shift under a gentle pull.
Clear the floor below and in front of the bar. Put a stable step where you can reach it when finished.
Stand on the floor or step and grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, palms forward and thumbs wrapped.
Transfer weight to your hands slowly. Keep arms long and shoulders supported without forcing them down.
Let your feet clear the floor and wait until your body is still. Start with knees bent enough that your feet stay clear.
execution: Lift both bent knees toward your chest in a smooth motion.
Near the top, curl your pelvis a little toward your ribs rather than only moving your thighs.
Lower slowly to stillness before the next rep. One lift of both legs and return is one rep.
finish: Stop before your grip fails. Place your feet on the step or floor before letting go.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
commonErrors: Kicking backward to start a swing.
Dropping the legs or hanging through shoulder pain.
core-hanging-knee-raise.easierOption: Use a captain's chair knee raise or a floor reverse crunch.
core-hanging-knee-raise.safety: Do not jump to an uncertain bar; stop if your grip slips or a shoulder hurts.
core-hanging-knee-raise.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; one simultaneous knee raise is one repetition. Requires a secure overhead bar.
core-hanging-knee-raise.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. NASM discusses hanging knee raises and names the straight-leg progression. Bar access and this full bent-knee setup remain draft wording.

terms.meaning: The ring of bones around your hips.

core-hanging-leg-raise.summary: Hang from a fixed bar and lift both straight legs while keeping your body from swinging.
equipment: Stable step if needed to reach the bar
setup: Use an installed exercise bar rated for your bodyweight. Check that it does not shift under a gentle pull.
Clear the floor below and in front of the bar. Put a stable step where you can reach it when finished.
Stand on the floor or step and grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, palms forward and thumbs wrapped.
Transfer weight to your hands slowly. Keep arms long and shoulders supported without forcing them down.
Let your feet clear the floor and wait until your body is still. Start with legs together and knees straight but not forced backward.
execution: Lift both legs forward together; start with a small range rather than trying to reach the bar.
As the legs rise, tip the front of your pelvis slightly toward your ribs without swinging your chest.
Lower slowly to stillness before the next rep. One lift of both legs and return is one rep.
finish: Stop before your grip fails. Place your feet on the step or floor before letting go.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
commonErrors: Kicking backward to start a swing.
Dropping the legs or hanging through shoulder pain.
core-hanging-leg-raise.easierOption: Use a bent-knee hanging raise or a supported knee raise.
core-hanging-leg-raise.safety: Do not jump to an uncertain bar; stop if your grip slips or a shoulder hurts.
core-hanging-leg-raise.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; one simultaneous leg raise is one repetition. Requires a secure overhead bar.
core-hanging-leg-raise.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. NASM discusses hanging knee raises and names the straight-leg progression. Bar access and this full straight-leg setup remain draft wording.

terms.meaning: The ring of bones around your hips.

core-captain-chair-knee-raise.summary: Support your body on forearm pads and lift both bent knees in front of you.
equipment: Captain's chair or vertical knee-raise station
setup: Check that the station is steady and its pads, handles, and steps are secure.
Face away from the back pad and climb onto the built-in steps using the handles.
Place your forearms along the pads, elbows under your shoulders, and hands around the grips.
Rest your back against the support without forcing a large arch. If pads adjust, set and lock them while your feet are supported.
Press into both forearm pads, then lift your feet from the steps. Let your legs hang, then bend your knees.
execution: Lift both bent knees toward your chest without throwing your head back.
Curl your hips slightly toward your ribs near the top, keeping firm forearm support.
Lower slowly until the legs hang still. Count one lift of both legs and return as one rep.
finish: Place your feet on the steps before taking weight off the forearm pads; then climb down using the handles.
breathing: Breathe out during the lift and in during the return.
commonErrors: Shrugging and sinking between the pads.
Bouncing the back against the pad to lift the legs.
core-captain-chair-knee-raise.easierOption: Lift the knees a shorter distance or use a floor reverse crunch.
core-captain-chair-knee-raise.safety: Stop for shoulder or back pain; do not continue once you cannot support yourself on the pads.
core-captain-chair-knee-raise.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; count each simultaneous knee raise as one repetition. Record the support station.
core-captain-chair-knee-raise.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. Life Fitness verifies station supports; ACE describes its bent-knee movement. The expanded mounting steps are draft wording.

core-captain-chair-leg-raise.summary: Support your body on forearm pads and lift both straight legs in front of you.
equipment: Captain's chair or vertical knee-raise station
setup: Check that the station is steady and its pads, handles, and steps are secure.
Face away from the back pad and climb onto the built-in steps using the handles.
Place your forearms along the pads, elbows under your shoulders, and hands around the grips.
Rest your back against the support without forcing a large arch. If pads adjust, set and lock them while your feet are supported.
Press into both forearm pads, then lift your feet from the steps. Let your legs hang straight with feet together.
execution: Raise both legs forward with knees straight but not locked backward.
Stop at or below hip height if going higher makes you rock or peel your back off the pad.
Lower slowly until the legs hang still. Count one lift of both legs and return as one rep.
finish: Place your feet on the steps before taking weight off the forearm pads; then climb down using the handles.
breathing: Breathe out during the lift and in during the return.
commonErrors: Shrugging and sinking between the pads.
Bouncing the back against the pad to lift the legs.
core-captain-chair-leg-raise.easierOption: Bend your knees to shorten the lift.
core-captain-chair-leg-raise.safety: Stop for shoulder or back pain; do not continue once you cannot support yourself on the pads.
core-captain-chair-leg-raise.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; count each simultaneous leg raise as one repetition. Record the support station.
core-captain-chair-leg-raise.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. Life Fitness verifies station supports; ACE describes its bent-knee movement. The straight-leg variant has family support only.

core-kneeling-ab-wheel.summary: Roll a wheel forward from your knees, then pull it back without letting your lower back sag.
equipment: Firm floor with a clear rolling path
setup: Check that the wheel turns freely and both handles are secure.
Set knee padding on the floor; keep loose fabric out of the wheel path.
Kneel hip-width apart and place the wheel just ahead of your knees.
Grip both handles, arms long and shoulders above the wheel.
Tighten your belly and buttocks. Start with a short reach you can reverse without falling forward.
execution: Roll the wheel forward slowly as your hips move forward with your shoulders.
Keep the distance between your ribs and hip bones steady. Stop before your belly drops or your back arches.
Pull the wheel toward your knees while bringing your shoulders and hips back together.
Return to the start with the wheel below your shoulders. One out-and-back is one rep.
finish: Bring the wheel close, put your hands on the floor, and sit back before standing.
breathing: Take a small breath in as you roll out and breathe out as you return; avoid holding your breath.
commonErrors: Reaching so far that you cannot roll back.
Sitting the hips back first while the wheel stays far away.
core-kneeling-ab-wheel.easierOption: Shorten the roll or use a kneeling forearm plank.
core-kneeling-ab-wheel.safety: Stop for back, wrist, or shoulder pain; do not try to catch a runaway wheel with an arched back.
core-kneeling-ab-wheel.loadConvention: Bodyweight leverage exercise; do not enter bodyweight as lifted load. Record wheel and rollout range.
core-kneeling-ab-wheel.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE covers the barbell rollout; NASM names ab-wheel rollouts. These support the family, not a wheel-specific setup guide.

core-kneeling-barbell-rollout.summary: Roll a barbell forward from your knees and bring it back while holding your middle steady.
setup: Choose equal round plates that roll smoothly; avoid hexagonal plates.
Fit plates on both ends and lock collars against them. Check the floor is level and clear.
Put padding behind the bar for your knees, outside the plates' path.
Kneel and grip the bar about shoulder-width apart with palms down and thumbs wrapped.
Set shoulders above the bar, arms long, belly and buttocks gently tight. Plan a short first roll.
execution: Roll the bar forward as your shoulders and hips travel forward together.
Keep your lower back from dipping; stop while you can still reverse the movement.
Draw the bar back toward your knees without jerking or sitting back first.
Finish with shoulders above the bar. One roll out and return is one rep.
finish: Bring the bar close, place hands on the floor, and sit back. Park the bar where it cannot roll.
breathing: Breathe in gently during the forward roll and out during the return.
commonErrors: Using loose or different-sized plates.
Rolling farther after the lower back starts to sag.
core-kneeling-barbell-rollout.easierOption: Use a shorter reach or choose a kneeling plank.
core-kneeling-barbell-rollout.safety: Keep fingers clear of plates. More plate weight is not the same as lifting that weight.
core-kneeling-barbell-rollout.loadConvention: Enter barbell plus all plates as setup context, not weight lifted. Load multiplier is zero because the bar rolls; compare the same plate diameter and rollout range.
core-kneeling-barbell-rollout.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE describes the kneeling barbell rollout. Plate checks and the app-specific load rule are added wording.

terms.meaning: Clamps that keep plates from sliding along the bar.

core-forearm-plank.summary: Hold your body above the floor on your forearms and toes while you keep breathing.
setup: Put a mat on a firm, non-slip floor and set a timer where you can hear it.
Start on hands and knees, then lower your forearms to the mat.
Place elbows directly below shoulders with forearms pointing forward.
Step one foot and then the other back, toes tucked under, feet about hip-width apart.
Straighten your legs and raise your knees. Tighten your belly and buttocks so hips line up between shoulders and heels.
execution: Press your forearms into the mat and look at the floor between your hands.
Hold your chest, hips, and legs in the same line without lifting your hips high or letting them dip.
Start counting seconds once settled. End the hold when you cannot keep that line while breathing.
finish: Lower both knees to the mat first, then lower your hips or sit back.
breathing: Take small, steady breaths throughout; do not hold your breath to extend the time.
commonErrors: Letting the belly drop and back arch.
Moving elbows far ahead of shoulders.
core-forearm-plank.easierOption: Keep your knees on the floor in a kneeling forearm plank.
core-forearm-plank.safety: Stop if shoulders or lower back hurt. Record only controlled seconds.
core-forearm-plank.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; record seconds held with control, excluding time after position is lost.
core-forearm-plank.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. NASM describes the forearm plank. Entry, timer placement, and logging wording are added.

core-high-plank.summary: Hold the top of a push-up with straight arms, using your hands and toes for support.
setup: Clear enough floor space to stretch your body out and put the timer within hearing.
Start on hands and knees.
Place palms below your shoulders, fingers spread and pointing forward or slightly outward.
Step your feet back one at a time, about hip-width apart.
Keep arms straight without forcing the elbows backward. Tighten belly and buttocks until hips line up with shoulders and heels.
execution: Press through your whole hands so your chest does not sink between your shoulders.
Look at the floor and hold your hips steady, without pushing your bottom high or dipping your belly.
Count seconds only after settling into position; end when you cannot hold it and breathe.
finish: Set both knees on the floor before taking weight off your hands.
breathing: Breathe steadily through the hold, with small breaths if needed.
commonErrors: Placing hands far in front of the shoulders.
Letting the hips sag while watching the timer.
core-high-plank.easierOption: Place hands on a fixed counter or a heavy bench secured against movement, and walk feet back.
core-high-plank.safety: Choose the forearm version if hand loading hurts; stop for shoulder or back pain.
core-high-plank.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; record seconds held with control.
core-high-plank.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. NASM describes the straight-arm plank. The elevated option and detailed entry wording are added.

core-kneeling-plank.summary: Hold your middle off the floor with your forearms and knees supporting your weight.
setup: Spread a mat on a non-slip floor and place the timer where you can hear it.
Begin on hands and knees; lower both forearms onto the mat.
Set elbows directly beneath shoulders and forearms pointing forward.
Move knees back until your body can form a straight slope from shoulders through hips to knees.
Keep knees about hip-width apart and shins resting on the mat. Gently tighten your belly and buttocks.
execution: Press your forearms down and lift your belly away from the mat.
Keep shoulders, hips, and knees on one straight line. Look down without dropping your chin to your chest.
Hold for the planned seconds only while the hips stay in place and you can breathe.
finish: Move your knees closer beneath your hips, then sit back to remove weight from your elbows.
breathing: Keep taking steady breaths through the entire hold.
commonErrors: Leaving hips folded so your bottom sits above the knees.
Letting your belly fall while the chest stays up.
core-kneeling-plank.easierOption: Use a shorter hold with rest between attempts, or place forearms on a firm elevated support.
core-kneeling-plank.safety: Use enough knee padding for comfort; stop for joint or back pain.
core-kneeling-plank.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; record seconds held with control.
core-kneeling-plank.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. NASM supports the forearm-plank family. This knees-down variant is an adaptation, not an exact-variant source check.

core-side-plank.summary: Hold your hips off the floor while resting on one forearm and your feet.
setup: Lie on one side on a mat, with enough room to turn over after the set.
Place the lower elbow directly under your shoulder and lay that forearm across the mat.
Extend both legs. Stack your feet or put the top foot just in front of the lower one for balance.
Keep your chest facing the wall in front of you, with one shoulder above the other.
Place your upper hand on your hip. Set the timer before lifting.
execution: Press the lower forearm and feet into the floor to raise your hips.
Hold a straight line from shoulders through hips to ankles; avoid rolling your chest toward the floor or ceiling.
Count controlled seconds for this side. End the hold when your hip drops or you cannot breathe steadily.
finish: Lower your hip gently to the mat.
Rest, then turn onto the other side and repeat; log the two sides separately.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift, then keep breathing during the hold.
commonErrors: Supporting elbow placed far away from the shoulder.
Rolling the upper hip backward.
core-side-plank.safety: Stop for shoulder pain; do not sink into the support arm.
core-side-plank.loadConvention: Record seconds for one side per set; log left and right separately, not as a combined duration.
core-side-plank.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. NASM describes the side plank and feet options. Entry and logging wording are added.

core-kneeling-side-plank.summary: Hold your hips off the floor while resting on one forearm and your bent knees.
setup: Lie on one side on a mat, with enough room to turn over after the set.
Place the lower elbow directly under your shoulder and lay that forearm across the mat.
Bend both knees about a right angle, with one knee resting on the other. Keep thighs in line with your trunk.
Keep your chest facing the wall in front of you, with one shoulder above the other.
Place your upper hand on your hip. Set the timer before lifting.
execution: Press the lower forearm and lower knee into the floor to raise your hips.
Hold a straight line from shoulders through hips to knees; avoid rolling your chest toward the floor or ceiling.
Count controlled seconds for this side. End the hold when your hip drops or you cannot breathe steadily.
finish: Lower your hip gently to the mat.
Rest, then turn onto the other side and repeat; log the two sides separately.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift, then keep breathing during the hold.
commonErrors: Supporting elbow placed far away from the shoulder.
Rolling the upper hip backward.
core-kneeling-side-plank.easierOption: Hold for fewer seconds with a rest between attempts.
core-kneeling-side-plank.safety: Stop for shoulder pain; do not sink into the support arm.
core-kneeling-side-plank.loadConvention: Record seconds for one side per set; log left and right separately.
core-kneeling-side-plank.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE describes a bent-knee side plank and timed holds. Entry and logging wording are added.

terms.meaning: Your body between your shoulders and hips.

core-plank-shoulder-tap.summary: From a high plank, lift one hand to touch the opposite shoulder without turning your hips.
setup: Start on hands and knees with clear floor space behind you.
Set palms directly under shoulders, fingers spread.
Step both feet back and place them wider than hip-width for balance.
Keep arms long and line up shoulders, hips, and heels.
Tighten your belly and settle your weight evenly before lifting a hand.
execution: Shift a little weight to your left palm, then lift the right hand and touch the left shoulder.
Keep both hip bones pointing toward the floor; make a quick, light touch without rushing.
Put the right palm back under its shoulder before lifting the left hand to the right shoulder.
Continue alternating. Each tap is one rep, so one left and one right tap equal two.
finish: Place both hands down, then lower your knees before sitting back.
breathing: Keep breathing; a short breath out during each tap may help you avoid holding your breath.
commonErrors: Rolling the hips to the side when a hand lifts.
Placing the hand farther forward after each tap.
core-plank-shoulder-tap.easierOption: Put hands on a fixed counter or a heavy secured bench and use a wide stance.
core-plank-shoulder-tap.safety: Stop for wrist, shoulder, or back pain; finish before balance becomes uncertain.
core-plank-shoulder-tap.loadConvention: Count each hand-to-opposite-shoulder tap as one repetition; left plus right equals two.
