core-plank-shoulder-tap.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. NASM covers the high-plank position; ACE shows taps within a push-up combination. The isolated tap variant has family support only.

core-dead-bug.summary: Lie on your back and reach one arm and the opposite leg away while your middle stays still.
setup: Lie on a mat with enough room for your arms to reach above your head.
Rest your head and shoulders on the floor.
Lift both arms toward the ceiling, hands above shoulders.
Bend hips and knees so knees are above hips and shins are level to the floor.
Breathe out gently and settle your lower back against the mat without pressing hard.
execution: Reach your right arm toward the floor beyond your head while straightening the left leg away.
Stop the reach before your lower back arches or your ribs lift; neither hand nor heel has to touch down.
Return that hand over the shoulder and knee over the hip.
Repeat with left arm and right leg. Each opposite arm-and-leg reach counts as one rep; both sides make two.
finish: Bring both knees back in. Lower one foot, then the other, and rest your arms.
breathing: Breathe out during the reach and in as you return; use a shorter reach if you cannot breathe.
commonErrors: Moving the arm and leg on the same side.
Reaching low enough that the back lifts from the mat.
core-dead-bug.easierOption: Leave arms pointing up and lower only one bent-leg heel toward the floor at a time.
core-dead-bug.safety: Stop for back pain; keep head down rather than straining to watch your legs.
core-dead-bug.loadConvention: Count each opposite arm-and-leg extension as one repetition; left plus right equals two.
core-dead-bug.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. NASM describes the opposite-limb dead bug. Entry, counting, and easier-option details are added wording.

core-bird-dog.summary: Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg backward from hands and knees.
setup: Put a mat on firm ground and leave clear space in front and behind you.
Kneel with knees beneath hips and hands beneath shoulders.
Spread fingers and press palms evenly into the floor.
Keep your back in a comfortable shape, with belly gently tight and no deep sag.
Look between your hands so your head follows the line of your back.
execution: Slide your right foot backward, then lift it as you reach the left arm forward.
Reach long, stopping at or below body height. Keep the two hip bones facing the floor.
Pause briefly without shifting your chest or turning your hip upward.
Bring hand and knee back under you, then switch sides. Each opposite arm-and-leg reach is one rep; left plus right is two.
finish: Return both hands and knees to the mat, then sit back or rise slowly.
breathing: Breathe out during the reach and in as you return. Keep breathing during any pause.
commonErrors: Lifting the leg high by arching the lower back.
Rolling the pelvis open or leaning far onto the supporting arm.
core-bird-dog.easierOption: Reach just one arm or one leg at a time, keeping the other three points on the floor.
core-bird-dog.safety: Stop for wrist, knee, or back pain. Extra height is not needed.
core-bird-dog.loadConvention: Count each opposite arm-and-leg reach as one repetition; left plus right equals two.
core-bird-dog.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE describes bird dog, including opposite limbs and limited reach. The app counting rule is added.

terms.meaning: The ring of bones around your hips.

core-hollow-hold.summary: Hold a shallow curved body shape on your back, with shoulders and feet lifted.
setup: Lie on a mat with room to extend arms and legs.
Bend your knees over your hips and reach your hands toward your thighs.
Breathe out and gently bring your ribs toward your hips so your lower back rests against the floor.
Lift your head and shoulder blades slightly, keeping a small gap under your chin.
Straighten your legs upward, then lower them only as far as your back stays supported. Reach arms overhead only if you can keep that position.
execution: Hold the chosen arm and leg position without rocking.
Keep your lower back touching the mat and shoulders just clear of it.
Count seconds once still. If the back arches, bring knees in or end the hold and stop the timer.
finish: Bend your knees, bring arms beside you, and lower your shoulders. Put feet down gently.
breathing: Keep taking small, steady breaths; do not strain with your breath held.
commonErrors: Lowering legs to a fixed height even though the back arches.
Pushing the chin forward or rocking to stay up.
core-hollow-hold.easierOption: Keep knees bent and hands reaching beside your thighs. Record this easier position with the time.
core-hollow-hold.safety: Stop for neck or back pain; the full arms-overhead shape is optional.
core-hollow-hold.loadConvention: Bodyweight only; record controlled hold time and note arm/leg position.
core-hollow-hold.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. CrossFit's primary guide describes the floor hollow position and tucked option. This gradual self-setup wording is adapted.

core-cable-pallof-press.summary: Resist a sideways pull while pressing your hands away from your chest.
setup: With the stack resting, clip one D-shaped handle to one adjustable pulley; close the clip fully.
Pull the pulley-height pin, move the pulley to chest height, and lock the pin into its hole.
Insert the stack pin fully into a light setting, with extra add-on weight at zero.
Stand sideways to the station and hold the handle in both hands at the middle of your chest.
Step away until the cable is taut. Set feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Face straight ahead with shoulders over hips. The cable should pull from your side and clear your body.
execution: Press both hands straight ahead at chest height until arms are nearly straight.
Keep your chest and hip bones facing forward as the resistance pulls sideways.
Pause briefly, then bring hands back to your chest slowly. One press out and return is one rep for this side.
finish: Bring hands to your chest and step toward the pulley until the stack rests before releasing.
Turn to put the other side nearest the anchor, reset the same stance, and log that side separately.
breathing: Breathe out while pressing forward and in while returning.
commonErrors: Turning the chest toward the anchor.
Leaning away from the pull or lifting the shoulders.
core-cable-pallof-press.safety: Never adjust a pin while the stack is lifted.
core-cable-pallof-press.loadConvention: Enter one stack display; repetitions are for one side per set. Log each side separately with identical pulley/setup.
core-cable-pallof-press.sourceNote: Draft description; needs expert review. ACE describes the standing cable anti-rotation press. Attachment and logging steps are added wording.

Face straight ahead with shoulders over hips. The cable should pull from your side and clear your body.
execution: Press both hands straight ahead at chest height until arms are nearly straight.
Hold there while keeping chest and hip bones facing forward; do not turn toward the pull.
Count controlled seconds on this side, ending when hands drift or your body starts to turn.
finish: Bring hands to your chest and step toward the pulley until the stack rests before releasing.
Turn to put the other side nearest the anchor, reset the same stance, and time that side separately.
breathing: Breathe steadily throughout the hold.
commonErrors: Turning the chest toward the anchor.
Leaning away from the pull or lifting the shoulders.

core-band-pallof-press.summary: Resist a sideways pull while pressing your hands away from your chest.
equipment: Band-compatible anchor on a solid upright
setup: Check the band for cracks and worn ends; use an intact band.
Fasten its matching anchor strap around a solid rack upright at chest height. Follow the strap fitting method; avoid sharp edges.
Attach the band and test with a gentle pull. Stay within its stretch limit.
Stand sideways. Grip the handle or free band end in both hands at your chest; do not wrap your wrists.
Step sideways until lightly stretched. Set feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, shoulders above hips.
Keep the band clear of your body. Note the anchor height and your distance from it.
execution: Press both hands straight ahead at chest height until arms are nearly straight.
Keep your chest and hip bones facing forward as the resistance pulls sideways.
Pause briefly, then bring hands back to your chest slowly. One press out and return is one rep for this side.
finish: Bring hands to your chest and step toward the anchor until the band is slack before releasing.
Turn to put the other side nearest the anchor, reset the same stance, and log that side separately.
breathing: Breathe out while pressing forward and in while returning.
commonErrors: Turning the chest toward the anchor.
Leaning away from the pull or lifting the shoulders.
core-band-pallof-press.easierOption: Use a lighter band or move closer to reduce tension.
core-band-pallof-press.safety: Stop if the anchor shifts or the band is damaged.
core-band-pallof-press.loadConvention: Do not enter an estimated band weight; record band identity, anchor height and distance. Log each side separately.

core-dumbbell-suitcase-carry.summary: Walk with one weight beside your body while keeping your trunk upright.
setup: Choose a clear route with room to turn; remove loose items and avoid stairs.
Place the weight just outside one foot, with its handle running forward to back.
Set feet about hip-width apart. Push hips back and bend knees to reach the handle without twisting.
Wrap fingers and thumb around the handle, then push through both feet to stand. Let the loaded arm hang beside you; leave the other arm relaxed.
Keep the weight clear of your legs. Look along the route and settle shoulders above hips before starting the timer.
execution: Walk with short, even steps and keep your chest facing along the path.
Avoid leaning toward or away from the weight.
Turn with several small steps. Record seconds for this carrying side; do the other side as a separate set.
finish: Stop walking, set feet evenly, then bend hips and knees to lower the weight beside your feet. Release only when supported.
breathing: Keep breathing with your steps rather than holding your breath.
commonErrors: Walking fast enough that the weights swing.
Continuing after the fingers begin to open.
core-dumbbell-suitcase-carry.easierOption: Use lighter weight and a shorter timed walk.
core-dumbbell-suitcase-carry.safety: Keep feet clear when setting down; end before grip or balance fails.
core-dumbbell-suitcase-carry.loadConvention: Enter the load of the single dumbbell. Log duration separately for each carrying side; exclude timed carries from lifted-volume totals.

core-stability-ball-crunch.summary: Curl your shoulders upward while an exercise ball supports your lower and middle back.
equipment: Stability ball rated for your bodyweight
setup: Check the ball for damage and use the maker's inflation size. Clear space around it.

lib-bar-bent-over-row.summary: Pull a barbell toward your lower ribs while holding a hip hinge.

Load both ends evenly and fit collars; grip slightly wider than shoulders with palms down.
Stand to lift the bar, then step clear and set feet hip-width apart.
Bend knees softly and push hips back until your trunk leans forward at a steady, comfortable angle.
execution: Pull elbows back to bring the bar toward your upper belly or lower ribs.
Keep the same trunk angle; do not stand up to finish the pull.
Lower until arms extend, keeping the bar close and the neck in line with the trunk.

lib-bar-hip-thrust.summary: Lift your hips under a padded barbell while your upper back rests on a bench.
setup: Secure a low bench so it cannot slide or tip; clear space for the bar.
Load evenly and fit collars. Use plates tall enough for the bar to roll over your legs.
Sit on the floor with your upper back against the bench edge, below the shoulder blades.
Roll the padded bar to your hip crease; keep both hands on it.
Bend knees and plant feet so shins are roughly upright when the hips rise.
execution: Push through whole feet and lift your hips, letting the upper back pivot on the bench.
Stop when shoulders, hips and knees form a near-straight line; keep ribs down.
Lower the hips slowly without letting the bar roll toward your belly.
finish: Rest hips and plates on the floor, straighten legs and roll the bar away before standing.

lib-bar-good-morning.summary: Bend forward from the hips with a light bar supported across your upper back.
setup: Set hooks below shoulder height and safeties just below the bar’s planned lowest position.
Begin with a light training bar; if adding plates, load evenly and fit collars.

Stand to lift it from the hooks, then take small steps back.
Set feet hip-width apart and bend knees slightly.

Stop within a small controlled range while the back of your thighs stretches.
Bring hips forward and stand without snapping the trunk upward or leaning back.

ref-Barbell_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Grip.summary: A flat bench press with a bar. The elbows bend as the weight lowers, then straighten to press it up.
setup: Set both rack hooks to the same height. Test the empty bar so you can lift it clear without reaching.
Set safety arms just below your chosen bottom position. Use a spotter if the rack cannot catch a missed rep.
Load both ends evenly and secure the plates with collars. Wrap your thumbs around the bar.
Place the flat bench on a firm floor. Check that the seat and back pad are locked.
Lie back with your head, shoulders, and hips on the pad. Plant both feet firmly on the floor.
Hold the bar a little wider than your shoulders. At the bottom, keep each wrist above its elbow.
Start with the weight held above your chest and arms straight. Draw your shoulder blades gently back against the pad.
execution: Bend your elbows and lower the weight slowly toward your middle chest. Keep your wrists over your elbows.
Stop at a depth you can control. Keep your shoulders on the pad and do not bounce the weight.
Press the weight up until your arms are straight. Keep your hips down and feet steady.
Pause to regain balance before the next rep.
finish: Finish with arms straight. Guide the bar back until both hooks support it.
Check both ends are secure before you let go.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you return. Keep breathing between reps.
commonErrors: Shoulders roll forward: shorten the lower part of the rep.
Hips lift or weight bounces: reduce the load and lower more slowly.
Wrists fold back: keep them stacked above your elbows.
ref-Barbell_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Grip.easierOption: Use a lighter load while keeping the same grip and bench angle.
ref-Barbell_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Grip.safety: Keep the weight under control from pickup to put-down. Stop for shoulder, elbow, or neck pain.
ref-Barbell_Bench_Press_-_Medium_Grip.loadConvention: Enter the total weight of the bar and all plates. Do not enter the weight on just one end. One full movement out and back is one rep.

ref-Dumbbell_One-Arm_Triceps_Extension.summary: An overhead elbow extension. The upper arm stays still while the elbow bends and straightens.
setup: Choose weights you can pick up and set down safely. Check the handles, plates and adjustment locks.
Sit with your back on the pad and both feet planted.
Bring the weight to shoulder height, then press it overhead. Use the free hand to help position it if needed.
Point your upper arms up close to your ears. Keep ribs down and avoid leaning back.
Face the palm forward. Rest your free hand lightly on the upper arm if you need help keeping it still.
execution: Keep your upper arms still as you bend the elbows. Lower the weight behind your head.
Stop at a comfortable elbow bend. Do not force your forearm onto your upper arm.
Straighten the elbows to lift the weight overhead. Keep your ribs and hips in place.
Pause at the top without snapping the elbows.
finish: Bring the weight down to shoulder height with both hands, then lower it close to your body.
Set it on a stable surface. Do not release it behind your head.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you return. Keep breathing between reps.
commonErrors: Upper arms swing: lower the load and keep the elbows in one place.
Back arches: brace your middle and shorten the range.
Elbows snap straight: slow the last part of the rep.
ref-Dumbbell_One-Arm_Triceps_Extension.easierOption: Use a lighter weight or less band tension. Keep the same arm position.
ref-Dumbbell_One-Arm_Triceps_Extension.safety: Keep a secure grip, especially with weight over your head. Stop for elbow or shoulder pain.
ref-Dumbbell_One-Arm_Triceps_Extension.loadConvention: Enter the weight of ONE dumbbell. Do not double this number. Enter reps PER SIDE. Complete the same number on both sides before marking the set done; enter that count once.

Try one row with a light weight. Check that your hands can move freely and any support stays in place.

Grip the bar with one palm toward you. Grip both hanging towel ends with the other hand.
Start with the arms long and a small backward lean. The towel hand helps support the lift.
Use a stable step to reach the bar. Wrap your thumbs around it and test your grip before taking your feet off.
Let the legs hang still. Gently tighten your middle so the body does not swing.
execution: Pull the chest toward the bar while using the towel hand for the help you need.
Lower both arms slowly without twisting. Change hands and repeat the same setup on the other side.
finish: Lower to a steady hang. Put both feet back on the step.
Let go only after your feet support your weight.
breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you return. Avoid holding your breath for the whole set.
commonErrors: Kicking to start the rep: reset to a still hang.

ref-Plate_Pinch.summary: A timed grip hold pinching two plates together with one hand.
setup: Choose two light plates with their smooth faces outward. Put them together on a stable low surface.
Pinch both plates together with the fingers on one outer face and thumb on the other. Keep feet clear below them.
Lift them a short distance and hold the arm long beside you.
execution: Squeeze steadily without letting one plate slide against the other.
Hold only while the grip stays secure. End before the plates begin to slip.

Lower slowly to the same bottom point and repeat.
finish: Bring the weight close to your body before changing position.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you return. Avoid holding your breath for the whole set.

Keep heels on the floor, arms long, and the body in one straight line from shoulders to heels. Choose an angle you can control.
execution: Bend the elbows and draw the shoulder blades together to bring the chest toward the bar or handles.
Keep hips in line with shoulders. Pause, then straighten the arms slowly to lower the body as one piece.
finish: Slowly return to long arms.

breathing: Breathe out as you lift and in as you return. Avoid holding your breath for the whole set.

finish: Finish the last curl with both dumbbells close to your shoulders. Keep your elbows bent and your feet planted.

ref-Barbell_Full_Squat.summary: A back squat with a bar held across the upper back.

Push through both feet. Lift your hips and chest together until you stand tall.
finish: Stand fully before walking toward the rack. Touch both uprights with the bar.
Bend your knees to lower the bar onto both hooks. Check that both ends are secure before letting go.

ref-Barbell_Full_Squat.safety: Keep the bar off your neck. Use the safety stops. Stop for joint pain or loss of balance.

ref-Butt_Lift_Bridge.summary: A floor glute bridge with both feet planted.
setup: Lie on your back on a mat. Bend both knees and plant your feet about hip-width apart.
Rest your arms on the floor with palms down. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed.
Place feet close enough that your lower legs are near upright when the hips rise.
execution: Press through your feet and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
Stop when shoulders, hips, and knees form a long line. Keep your ribs down.
Pause without arching your lower back or turning your hips.
Lower your hips slowly to the floor. Reset before the next rep.
finish: Lower your hips completely. Relax your legs, roll onto one side, and use your hands to sit up.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Back arches: stop lifting when hips line up with the trunk.
Hips twist: make a smaller movement.
Neck presses down: support your weight through shoulders and feet.
ref-Butt_Lift_Bridge.easierOption: Use a smaller range. For ball versions, use a separately logged bridge on the floor.
ref-Butt_Lift_Bridge.safety: Use a ball sized for you and rated for your weight. Stop if it slips or your back hurts.
ref-Butt_Lift_Bridge.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. One full movement out and back is one rep.

ref-Single_Leg_Glute_Bridge.summary: A single-leg floor bridge with the free knee drawn toward the chest.
setup: Lie on your back on a mat. Bend both knees and plant your feet about hip-width apart.
Rest your arms on the floor with palms down. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed.
Place feet close enough that your lower legs are near upright when the hips rise.
Lift one foot and draw that knee toward your chest. Keep the other foot flat.
execution: Press through the planted foot. Squeeze that glute to lift both hips evenly.
Stop when shoulders, hips, and knees form a long line. Keep your ribs down.
Pause without arching your lower back or turning your hips.
Lower your hips slowly to the floor. Reset before the next rep.
finish: Lower your hips completely. Relax your legs, roll onto one side, and use your hands to sit up.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Back arches: stop lifting when hips line up with the trunk.

ref-Single_Leg_Glute_Bridge.safety: Use a ball sized for you and rated for your weight. Stop if it slips or your back hurts.
ref-Single_Leg_Glute_Bridge.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. Count reps per side; complete the same number on each side.

ref-Physioball_Hip_Bridge.summary: A hip bridge with the upper back on an exercise ball and feet on the floor.
setup: Place an exercise ball on a non-slip floor. Sit on it, then walk your feet forward as you lean back.
Stop with your upper back and shoulders supported by the ball. Keep your head supported and hips free.
Plant both feet wider than hip-width for balance. Bend the knees and keep your middle firm.
execution: Press through your feet and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
Stop when shoulders, hips, and knees form a long line. Keep your ribs down.
Pause without arching your lower back or turning your hips.
Lower your hips a small distance without letting the ball roll away. Then repeat.
finish: Lower your hips with control. Walk feet back toward the ball as you sit upright, keeping a hand on it for balance.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Back arches: stop lifting when hips line up with the trunk.
Hips twist: make a smaller movement.
Neck presses down: support your weight through shoulders and feet.
ref-Physioball_Hip_Bridge.easierOption: Use a smaller range. For ball versions, use a separately logged bridge on the floor.
ref-Physioball_Hip_Bridge.safety: Use a ball sized for you and rated for your weight. Stop if it slips or your back hurts.

ref-Ball_Leg_Curl.summary: A hamstring curl with the heels on a ball and hips held above the floor.
setup: Lie on your back on a mat. Rest your heels and lower calves on top of an exercise ball.
Start with legs almost straight. Set the ball so it can roll toward you without hitting anything.
Spread your arms on the floor for balance. Tighten your middle and lift your hips.
execution: Keep your hips raised. Bend both knees to roll the ball toward your hips with your heels.
Stop before your hips drop or the ball moves sideways. Keep shoulders on the floor.
Pause, then straighten the knees slowly to roll the ball away.
Keep hips raised during the planned reps. The ball rolls; your shoulders stay in place.
finish: Straighten your legs slowly. Lower the hips, then bring your feet off the ball and onto the floor.
Roll onto one side and use your hands to sit up.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Back arches: stop lifting when hips line up with the trunk.
Hips twist: make a smaller movement.
Neck presses down: support your weight through shoulders and feet.
ref-Ball_Leg_Curl.easierOption: Use a smaller range. For ball versions, use a separately logged bridge on the floor.
ref-Ball_Leg_Curl.safety: Use a ball sized for you and rated for your weight. Stop if it slips or your back hurts.
ref-Ball_Leg_Curl.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. One full movement out and back is one rep.
ref-Ball_Leg_Curl.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Hyperextensions_Back_Extensions.summary: A back extension that moves at the hips over a fixed thigh pad.
setup: Set a back-extension bench so the front pad supports your upper thighs, just below the hip crease.
Step into the station. Secure your heels beneath its pads and keep feet pressed against the foot supports.
Cross your arms over your chest. Start with head, trunk, and legs in one line.
execution: Push your hips into the pad and fold forward from your hips. Keep your back in its natural shape.
Stop before your back rounds or your head nears the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your trunk until it lines up with your legs.
Pause in that straight line. Do not arch upward past it.
finish: Return to the supported start. Hold the frame while taking one foot and then the other out of the station.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Lower back arches: stop at the line of your body.
Movement swings: slow down and use less range.
Pad blocks the hip fold: adjust the support.
ref-Hyperextensions_Back_Extensions.easierOption: Use no added weight and a smaller hip movement.
ref-Hyperextensions_Back_Extensions.safety: Keep secure foot support throughout. Stop if you feel back pain or cannot control the return.
ref-Hyperextensions_Back_Extensions.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. One full movement out and back is one rep.
ref-Hyperextensions_Back_Extensions.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Hyperextensions_With_No_Hyperextensi.summary: A back extension over the end of a flat bench while a helper anchors the legs.
setup: Use a firm flat bench and a helper who can hold your lower legs securely. Check that the bench cannot tip.
Lie face down with your hips near the bench end and your legs supported along it.
Ask the helper to hold both legs before sliding your upper body over the edge. Cross your arms over your chest.
execution: Push your hips into the pad and fold forward from your hips. Keep your back in its natural shape.
Stop before your back rounds or your head nears the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your trunk until it lines up with your legs.
Pause in that straight line. Do not arch upward past it.
finish: Return your chest to the bench and grip its sides. Slide back until fully supported.
Tell the helper they can release your legs only after you are safely on the bench.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Lower back arches: stop at the line of your body.
Movement swings: slow down and use less range.
Pad blocks the hip fold: adjust the support.
ref-Hyperextensions_With_No_Hyperextensi.easierOption: Use no added weight and a smaller hip movement.
ref-Hyperextensions_With_No_Hyperextensi.safety: Keep secure foot support throughout. Stop if you feel back pain or cannot control the return.
ref-Hyperextensions_With_No_Hyperextensi.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. One full movement out and back is one rep.
ref-Hyperextensions_With_No_Hyperextensi.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Weighted_Ball_Hyperextension.summary: A weighted trunk extension with the front of the body supported by an exercise ball.
setup: Set an exercise ball on a non-slip floor. Kneel behind it and roll your stomach and hips onto it.
Plant both forefeet wide on the floor. Position your torso roughly level with the floor and keep the ball still.
Hold a light plate close below your chin against your upper chest. Keep it off your throat and the back of your neck.
execution: Let your chest lower a small amount over the ball while the feet stay planted.
Stop before your back rounds or your head nears the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your trunk until it lines up with your legs.
Pause in that straight line. Do not arch upward past it.
finish: Lower the chest onto the ball. Set the plate on the floor within reach.
Walk your hands forward enough to guide your knees back to the floor. Get off the ball before standing.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Lower back arches: stop at the line of your body.
Movement swings: slow down and use less range.
Pad blocks the hip fold: adjust the support.
ref-Weighted_Ball_Hyperextension.easierOption: Use no added weight and a smaller hip movement.
ref-Weighted_Ball_Hyperextension.safety: Keep secure foot support throughout. Stop if you feel back pain or cannot control the return.
ref-Weighted_Ball_Hyperextension.loadConvention: Record the held plate weight and ball size in notes. This balance-dependent variation does not use automatic load progression. One trunk lift and return is one rep.
ref-Weighted_Ball_Hyperextension.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Reverse_Hyperextension.summary: A reverse hyperextension: the trunk stays supported while the legs move at the hips.
setup: Use a reverse-hyperextension machine. Set its load and foot pads while it is still.
Hold the handles and lie face down on the top pad. Place the hip crease near the pad edge.
Place the feet between the lower pads or in the provided ankle attachment, as its label directs. Keep your chest supported.
execution: Let your legs move forward under the pad through a comfortable hip bend.
Squeeze the glutes to lift the legs backward. Keep your chest and stomach on the pad.
Stop before the legs rise above your trunk or your lower back arches.
Lower the legs and carriage slowly. Do not kick or build a swinging rhythm.
finish: Let the moving arm settle on its rest. Release the ankle attachment and lower both feet safely.
Hold the handles as you slide off the top pad.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Lower back arches: stop at the line of your body.
Movement swings: slow down and use less range.
Pad blocks the hip fold: adjust the support.
ref-Reverse_Hyperextension.easierOption: Use no added weight and a smaller hip movement.
ref-Reverse_Hyperextension.safety: Keep secure foot support throughout. Stop if you feel back pain or cannot control the return.
ref-Reverse_Hyperextension.loadConvention: Record the exact machine and its load setting in notes. Its loading type is not confirmed here. Do not compare stack labels, plate totals, or sled weights as equal loads. Automatic load progression is off. One full movement out and back is one rep.
ref-Reverse_Hyperextension.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Floor_Glute-Ham_Raise.summary: A kneeling hamstring lower with the ankles anchored. The hips stay straight as the knees open.
setup: Place a thick knee pad on the floor. Kneel with knees hip-width apart and toes pointing back.
Have a helper hold both ankles down, or use a purpose-built fixed ankle anchor. Check it cannot lift or slide.
Start upright from knees to head. Tighten your glutes and middle. Keep your hands ready in front of your chest.
execution: Keep shoulders, hips, and knees in one line as you lean forward slowly.
Let the knees straighten while the hamstrings slow your descent. Do not bend at the hips.
Catch your weight with your hands on the floor before control is lost.
Push lightly with your hands and pull through the hamstrings to return upright. Keep the ankles anchored.
finish: Return to an upright kneel. Put your hands on the support before releasing your ankles.
Tell the helper the set is over before they let go. Step down from the seat with support if using a machine.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Hips fold: reduce the distance you lower.
Body drops: use more hand help and stop sooner.
Ankles lift: improve the anchor before continuing.
ref-Floor_Glute-Ham_Raise.easierOption: Lower only a short distance and use both hands for more help.
ref-Floor_Glute-Ham_Raise.safety: This movement can be very demanding. Keep a clear hand-landing space and never rely on loose furniture to hold the ankles.
ref-Floor_Glute-Ham_Raise.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. One full movement out and back is one rep.

ref-Natural_Glute_Ham_Raise.summary: A kneeling hamstring lower with the ankles anchored. The hips stay straight as the knees open.
setup: Use the padded seat and leg restraint of a suitable lat-pulldown or preacher station. Check the unit cannot tip.
Kneel facing away from the station. Put your ankles firmly under its pads and both knees on the padded seat.
Place a stable box in front for hand assistance. Start upright from knees to head with hands ready.
execution: Keep shoulders, hips, and knees in one line as you lean forward slowly.
Let the knees straighten while the hamstrings slow your descent. Do not bend at the hips.
Catch your weight with your hands on the assistance box before control is lost.
Push lightly with your hands and pull through the hamstrings to return upright. Keep the ankles anchored.
finish: Return to an upright kneel. Put your hands on the support before releasing your ankles.
Tell the helper the set is over before they let go. Step down from the seat with support if using a machine.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Hips fold: reduce the distance you lower.

ref-Balance_Board.summary: A standing balance hold on a board that rocks. Time starts after you are steady.
setup: Place the board on the surface its maker recommends. Clear space around all sides.
Stand next to a rail or solid counter that you can hold without leaning far.
Hold the support. Put one foot, then the other, on the marked standing areas.
Set feet evenly and keep knees soft. Look at one still point ahead.
execution: Shift pressure gently between your feet to bring the board near level.
Use small ankle and hip changes. Keep your knees soft and torso tall.
Hold for the planned time. Touch the support whenever needed.
Stop the timer if you step off or need a full reset.
finish: Hold the support. Let one board edge settle, then place one foot on the floor.
Bring the other foot down before releasing your hand.
breathing: Breathe slowly throughout the hold. Do not hold your breath to stay still.
commonErrors: Knees lock: soften them.
Large body swings: make smaller corrections.
Looking at feet: look ahead once your feet are placed.
ref-Balance_Board.easierOption: Keep both hands on the support or use a board with less tilt.
ref-Balance_Board.safety: Do not add external weight. Stay within reach of support and step off before fatigue makes balance poor.
ref-Balance_Board.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. Log time in seconds.
ref-Balance_Board.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Downward_Facing_Balance.summary: A face-down balance hold on an exercise ball with hands on the floor and legs lifted.
setup: Kneel behind the ball. Place your stomach over its center and both palms on the floor.
Walk your hands forward slowly. Keep the ball under your stomach and hips, not your neck.
Spread fingers and place hands about shoulder-width apart. Keep elbows straight without forcing them.
Reach your legs back. Lift them only once your hands and ball are steady.
execution: Hold your body long from head to feet, with knees extended.
Keep your middle firm so the lower back does not sag. Keep your gaze on the floor.
Make small balance changes through the hands. Keep both legs at the same height.
Hold for the planned time without rolling farther forward.
finish: Lower your feet to the floor. Walk your hands backward to bring knees down behind the ball.
Keep one hand on the ball as you sit back and stand.
breathing: Take small, steady breaths while holding the position.
commonErrors: Back sags: lower the feet and reset.
Ball rolls sideways: widen hand placement slightly.
Head lifts: look down between the hands.
ref-Downward_Facing_Balance.easierOption: Keep both toes on the floor or use a shorter hold.
ref-Downward_Facing_Balance.safety: Check ball size and weight rating. Stop if your wrists hurt or the ball cannot stay under you.
ref-Downward_Facing_Balance.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. Log time in seconds.

ref-Flutter_Kicks.variant: Flutter Kicks — prone on a flat bench
ref-Flutter_Kicks.summary: Prone flutter kicks on a bench: one straight leg rises as the other lowers.
setup: Lie face down along a stable bench. Place your hip crease near its end so both legs can move freely.
Hold the bench edges in front of you. Keep chest and stomach supported.
Straighten both knees. Lift the legs just enough to bring them near the line of your trunk.
Keep your neck in line with your back. Look toward the bench or floor.
execution: Lift one straight leg a small distance while the other lowers slightly.
Switch the leg positions slowly, like a small swimming kick.
Move from the hips. Keep your pelvis heavy on the bench and avoid arching your back.
Use equal, small movements on both sides. Count each leg lift on that side.
finish: Stop both legs near level, then lower the feet to the floor together.
Keep hold of the bench while sliding your body back to a safe standing position.
breathing: Breathe steadily through the alternating kicks.
commonErrors: Large kicks arch the back: reduce their size.
Knees bend: reach the legs long.
Pelvis rocks: slow the changes between legs.
ref-Flutter_Kicks.easierOption: Keep one foot on the floor and lift the other a small distance. Log that as a supported variation.
ref-Flutter_Kicks.safety: Make sure the bench cannot tip. Stop for low-back discomfort or pressure at the hip crease.
ref-Flutter_Kicks.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. Count reps per side; complete the same number on each side.
ref-Flutter_Kicks.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Glute_Kickback.summary: A hands-and-knees glute kickback with the working knee kept bent.
setup: Kneel on a mat and place hands under shoulders. Spread your fingers for steady support.
Place knees under hips. Keep elbows straight without forcing them.
Look at the floor between your hands. Tighten your middle so your back keeps its natural shape.
Keep the working knee bent about a right angle.
execution: Lift the working thigh behind you by moving at the hip.
Stop when the thigh lines up with your trunk, before your back arches.
Keep hips level and the working knee bent. Pause with the foot above the knee.
Lower the knee under the hip slowly. Alternate legs for the planned reps.
finish: Place both knees on the mat. Sit back toward your heels, then use your hands to come up.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Back arches: lift the leg less.
Hip turns open: point both hip bones toward the floor.
Head lifts: keep your neck long.
ref-Glute_Kickback.easierOption: Use a smaller lift or place a pad under the knees.
ref-Glute_Kickback.safety: Stop if the wrists, knees, or lower back hurt. Keep pressure spread across both hands.
ref-Glute_Kickback.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. Count reps per side; complete the same number on each side.
ref-Glute_Kickback.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Leg_Lift.summary: A standing leg curl: bend one knee to bring the heel up behind you.
setup: Stand facing a solid rail or counter. Hold it lightly with both hands.
Place feet hip-width apart. Keep your shoulders above your hips.
Shift weight onto one leg and soften that knee. Keep the working thigh beside it.
For the base version, use no ankle weight. If used, fasten it securely above the ankle and note it separately.
execution: Bend the working knee to lift the heel behind you.
Keep the working thigh mostly vertical. Do not swing the whole leg backward.
Pause before the heel reaches the hip, using a comfortable range.
Lower the foot slowly to the floor. Complete reps before changing legs.
finish: Set both feet flat and stand evenly before releasing the support.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Thigh swings backward: keep knees beside each other.
Body leans forward: shorten the curl.
Foot drops: slow the return.
ref-Leg_Lift.easierOption: Bend the knee through a smaller range with no ankle weight.
ref-Leg_Lift.safety: Use a fixed support that cannot tip. Stop for knee pain or cramping.
ref-Leg_Lift.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. Count reps per side; complete the same number on each side.
ref-Leg_Lift.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Monster_Walk.summary: A monster walk with one loop band at the ankles and another above the knees.
setup: Check both bands for tears. Sit down to place one above the knees and the other around the ankles.
Stand near a support, then set feet shoulder-width apart. Both bands should have light tension.
Bend knees and hips slightly. Keep your middle firm and chest steady.
Clear a short forward and backward path before moving.
execution: Take one short step forward without letting the knees collapse inward.
Follow with the other foot while keeping space and tension between your legs.
Continue with small alternating steps. Keep toes and knees aimed the same way.
Reverse the pattern and walk backward to the starting point. Place each foot before shifting your weight.
finish: Stand still with both feet under control. Sit down before removing the ankle band.
breathing: Keep breathing steadily as you step.
commonErrors: Feet snap together: use a lighter band.
Torso sways: shorten each step.
Knees turn inward: keep the band gently stretched.
ref-Monster_Walk.easierOption: Use lighter bands or one band above the knees as a separately logged version.
ref-Monster_Walk.safety: Do not let bands roll over the knee joints. Watch the clear path when walking backward.
ref-Monster_Walk.loadConvention: Record both band brands, colors, and placements. No fixed load or automatic progression is used. Count steps per leg; forward and backward steps each count on the moving side.
ref-Monster_Walk.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Platform_Hamstring_Slides.summary: A floor hamstring slide with one heel on a towel and the hips resting on the floor.
setup: Check that the floor is smooth and clear. Put a towel or slider under one heel.
Lie on your back with both legs straight. Rest your arms beside you.
Keep the other heel on the floor and your hips down. Point both knees toward the ceiling.
Test a short slide so the towel moves smoothly without catching.
execution: Bend the working knee to draw the sliding heel toward your hips.
Keep the heel pressed gently into the towel. Let the knee rise without turning outward.
Stop at a comfortable knee bend. Keep the pelvis and other leg still.
Slide the heel away slowly until the leg is nearly straight. Finish reps before changing legs.
finish: Straighten the working leg and rest both heels. Roll onto one side to sit up.
Move the slider out of the walking area.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Hips lift: keep the pelvis on the floor for this version.
Towel catches: change the surface.
Knee turns out: guide it toward the ceiling.
ref-Platform_Hamstring_Slides.easierOption: Make a shorter slide with no added weight.
ref-Platform_Hamstring_Slides.safety: Use a clear floor. Avoid a surface that grips suddenly or makes the heel hard to control.
ref-Platform_Hamstring_Slides.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. Count reps per side; complete the same number on each side.
ref-Platform_Hamstring_Slides.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Prone_Manual_Hamstring.summary: A partner-resisted hamstring curl performed face down. Resistance is set by communication, not a weight stack.
setup: Lie face down with both legs straight. Keep hips on the mat and head comfortable.
Have your partner kneel beside the working leg, clear of the moving foot.
Ask them to place a hand on the back of your heel. Agree on a clear stop word.
Start with very light pressure. Keep the working thigh against the mat.
execution: Bend the knee to bring your heel toward your hips while the partner resists gently.
Ask for more or less pressure so the movement stays smooth.
Pause at a comfortable knee bend. The partner then guides resistance as you lower.
Straighten the knee slowly without forcing it backward. Repeat, then change legs.
finish: Set the foot down. Ask the partner to remove all pressure before you turn or get up.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Partner pushes too hard: stop and reduce pressure.
Hip lifts: shorten the curl.
Foot is twisted: keep resistance in line with the lower leg.
ref-Prone_Manual_Hamstring.easierOption: Use no partner pressure and rehearse the knee bend first.
ref-Prone_Manual_Hamstring.safety: Keep talking throughout. Stop for pain, cramping, or sudden changes in pressure.
ref-Prone_Manual_Hamstring.loadConvention: Log the movement without an external load value. Record any support or assistance in notes. Automatic load progression is off. Count reps per side; complete the same number on each side.
ref-Prone_Manual_Hamstring.sourceNote: Based on the exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Seated_Band_Hamstring_Curl.summary: A seated hamstring curl with a low band pulling forward from the ankles.
setup: Secure the band to a firm anchor close to the floor. Inspect it and test the attachment.
Place a stable bench facing the anchor a few feet away. It must not slide toward the anchor.
Sit near the bench edge. Place the band behind both ankles, above the heels.
Start with legs nearly straight and light band tension. Hold the bench sides and sit tall.
execution: Bend both knees to pull your heels back toward the bench.
Keep your thighs still. Lean back only a little if needed to keep feet clear of the floor.
Pause at a comfortable knee bend without letting the band roll onto the feet.
Straighten the knees slowly and let the band lengthen. Keep tension controlled.
finish: Bring both feet onto the floor. Move closer to the anchor until the band is slack.
Remove it from your ankles while seated, then stand.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.

ref-Cable_Seated_Lateral_Raise.summary: A seated, bent-forward cable rear lateral raise with crossed low cables.
setup: Set two opposite pulleys low. Center a stable flat bench between them and choose equal light loads.
Sit near the bench edge. Put feet flat in front of your knees and lean your chest over your thighs.
Take the left handle in the right hand and the right in the left. Have a helper pass them if you cannot reach easily.
Let cables cross below the knees, clear of your feet. Start with arms hanging and elbows softly bent.
execution: Raise the arms out to the sides in a wide arc. Keep the elbows at the same slight bend.
Stop when the elbows reach about shoulder height. Keep the arms across the body rather than behind the hips.
Pause without lifting your chest or shrugging toward your ears.
Lower slowly until the arms hang beneath the shoulders again.
finish: Lower the handles and let both stacks settle. Set the handles down before sitting upright.

ref-Cable_Internal_Rotation.summary: A seated cable internal rotation using the arm nearest the pulley.
setup: Set a cable pulley at elbow height and attach a single handle. Choose a very light setting.
Sit side-on next to the low pulley with the working arm nearest it. Sit on the floor with legs forward, or use a bench if the pulley adjusts to elbow height.
Bend the working elbow to a right angle. Keep the elbow at your side, with a folded towel between elbow and ribs.
Start with the forearm pointing outward toward the pulley. Keep wrist straight and shoulders level.
execution: Keep the upper arm still at your side. Turn the forearm inward across your stomach.
Move only through a comfortable shoulder range. Do not twist your trunk or lift the elbow.
Pause without squeezing hard or forcing farther.
Turn the forearm back slowly. Keep the elbow bent and in the same place.
finish: Return the handle until the stack rests. Set it down, then use the free hand to help you stand.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Elbow drifts away: keep the towel in place.

ref-External_Rotation.summary: A side-lying dumbbell external rotation with the upper elbow held against the ribs.
setup: Lie on one side on a flat bench. Support your head with the lower arm or a small pad.
Hold a very light dumbbell in the upper hand. Keep that upper arm along your ribs.
Bend the working elbow to a right angle. Start with the forearm across your stomach and near horizontal.
Keep hips and shoulders stacked, with the wrist straight. Use a folded towel under the elbow if helpful.
execution: Keeping the elbow by your side, turn the forearm upward in an arc toward the ceiling.
Move only through a comfortable shoulder range. Do not twist your trunk or lift the elbow.
Pause without squeezing hard or forcing farther.
Turn the forearm back slowly. Keep the elbow bent and in the same place.
finish: Lower the dumbbell to the start. Use both hands to place it safely on the floor or a nearby low surface.
Roll upright before changing sides.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Elbow drifts away: keep the towel in place.

ref-External_Rotation_with_Band.summary: A shoulder external rotation with the elbow held by the ribs.

Start with the forearm across the front of your stomach. Keep wrist straight and shoulders level.

Move only through a comfortable shoulder range. Do not twist your trunk or lift the elbow.
Pause without squeezing hard or forcing farther.
Turn the forearm back slowly. Keep the elbow bent and in the same place.
finish: Return slowly, then step toward the anchor until the band is slack. Release it and change sides.

ref-Barbell_Rear_Delt_Row.summary: A bent-over barbell rear-delt row with a wide grip and elbows flared outward.
setup: Load a barbell evenly and lock its collars. Pick it up with a wide overhand grip.
Stand with feet hip-width apart. Soften knees and push hips back until the torso is nearly level.
Let arms hang below the shoulders. Keep the back in its natural shape and neck in line.
Turn the elbows outward so the upper arms will move across the body.
execution: Bend elbows out to the sides and pull the bar toward the upper chest.
Keep your torso fixed and the bar level. Stop before the shoulders shrug or back angle changes.
Pause with upper arms across the body, roughly in a T shape.
Lower the bar slowly until the arms hang. Keep the hip hinge through the set.
finish: Lower the bar to a hang. Bend hips and knees to place it on the floor before standing.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.

Sit with feet on the footplates and knees slightly bent. Grip both rope ends and scoot back until arms reach forward.
Sit tall with your back in its natural shape. Keep feet planted and rope level with the upper chest.
Lift elbows out to the sides while keeping shoulders away from the ears.

Reach both arms forward slowly as the cable returns. Keep balance without leaning backward.

ref-Face_Pull.summary: A standing face pull from a high pulley with the rope ends separating beside the face.

Step back until arms reach forward with light cable tension. Set feet hip-width apart or in a steady split stance.
Keep your ribs over your hips and knees soft. Look toward the pulley.
execution: Pull the rope toward your face as you separate the hands. Let the elbows travel out to the sides.
Keep upper arms around shoulder height and wrists straight. Stop before the neck shrugs.
Pause with hands beside your face and torso still.
Reach both arms forward slowly as the cable returns. Keep balance without leaning backward.
finish: Return the rope slowly. Step toward the pulley until the stack rests, then release the rope.

ref-Barbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise.summary: An incline shoulder raise with straight arms. The shoulder blades move; this is not a full press.

setup: Lock an incline bench at a comfortable moderate angle. Plant both feet and rest your head and back on the pad.
Set a bar in the bench rack within easy reach. Load evenly, lock collars, and use safety arms or a helper for the handoff.
Grip slightly wider than shoulders and lift the bar above the shoulders.
Hold arms nearly straight with wrists stacked over elbows. Keep ribs down and your neck relaxed.
execution: Keep elbows at the same angle. Reach the shoulders upward so the shoulder blades move around the rib cage.
Let the weights rise only a few inches. The arms stay pointed toward the ceiling.
Pause without lifting your head, hips, or lower back from the bench.
Let the shoulder blades settle back onto the pad slowly. This small reach and return is one rep.
finish: Bring the bar to both rack hooks and lower it onto them. Check it holds before letting go.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.

ref-Barbell_Incline_Shoulder_Raise.safety: Keep the weights above the shoulders and away from your face. Stop if the small reach hurts.

ref-Anti-Gravity_Press.summary: A chest-supported anti-gravity press with a bar moving forward at floor level, rather than vertically overhead.
setup: Lock the bench at a low incline with space beyond its head end. Use a very light bar.
Place the bar on the floor beyond the head end where you can reach without twisting.
Lie face down with chest supported and feet planted. Take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Bend elbows to bring the bar near your chest. Keep your neck in line with the trunk.
execution: Press the bar forward beyond your head by straightening the elbows.
Keep the arms roughly parallel to the floor and the chest on the pad.
Stop when the elbows are straight without forcing them. Keep the bar level.
Bend elbows to draw the bar back toward the chest along the same path.
finish: Lower the bar onto its floor supports with both hands. Keep your chest supported until it rests.
Use your hands on the bench to push yourself upright.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.

ref-Battling_Ropes.summary: Alternating battle-rope waves made by raising one arm as the other lowers.
setup: Secure the middle of the rope to a rated anchor about 15–20 feet in front of you.
Stand facing the anchor and hold one end in each hand. Leave a little slack in both rope lengths.
Set feet shoulder-width apart. Bend hips and knees slightly and keep your middle firm.
Let arms hang by your sides with palms facing inward. Keep the rope clear of your feet.
execution: Raise one hand quickly toward shoulder height while the other lowers.
Reverse the hands to send alternating waves toward the anchor.
Keep the elbows soft and torso steady. Let the arms move without shrugging hard.
Continue for the planned time. Keep the same squat depth and smooth rhythm.
finish: Make the waves smaller, then stop. Let the rope settle before placing both ends on the floor.
Step away without crossing over a moving rope.
breathing: Breathe in a steady rhythm throughout the interval. Do not hold your breath.
commonErrors: Torso bounces: slow the waves.
Shoulders shrug: use smaller arm motion.
Rope tangles: stop and reset the slack.
ref-Battling_Ropes.easierOption: Use smaller waves, a lighter rope, or a shorter interval.
ref-Battling_Ropes.safety: Test the anchor before each set. Stop when your grip or balance no longer stays steady.

ref-Car_Drivers.summary: A plate hold at shoulder height while turning it left and right like a steering wheel.
setup: Choose a plate with secure edges or grip holes. Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Hold the plate at its left and right sides, like 9 and 3 on a clock. Face palms toward each other.
Lift it in front of your chest to about shoulder height. Keep elbows soft rather than forced straight.
Keep ribs over hips and shoulders relaxed. Check the plate is clear of your face.
execution: Turn the plate to one side as though turning a steering wheel.
Keep the center of the plate in front of your chest. Let both hands move around that center.
Turn back through the middle and toward the other side. Use a comfortable wrist and shoulder range.
Return to the middle. A left turn, right turn, and return completes one cycle.
finish: Bring the plate down toward the waist with both hands.
Bend hips and knees to place it on a low rack or the floor.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Torso twists: keep hips and ribs facing ahead.
Plate drops in height: use a lighter plate.
Wrists bend sharply: turn less.
ref-Car_Drivers.easierOption: Use a lighter plate or hold it closer to your chest.
ref-Car_Drivers.safety: Stop for wrist or shoulder pain. Keep both hands secure; do not rotate to the limit of your grip.

ref-Cuban_Press.summary: A Cuban press: shoulder rotation from a scarecrow position, followed by an overhead press.
setup: Choose very light matching dumbbells. Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Lift both upper arms out to the sides to about shoulder height.
Bend elbows to right angles and let forearms point down. Keep wrists straight.
Hold the torso tall with ribs down. Use only a shoulder position that feels comfortable.
execution: Keep upper arms in place as you rotate the forearms forward and up.
Stop with wrists above elbows and forearms roughly vertical. Do not force the rotation.
Press both dumbbells overhead until arms are straight and the weights stay above the shoulders.
Lower to the raised-forearm position, then rotate forearms down to the start.
finish: Lower the upper arms to the sides. Set the dumbbells down with a steady bend of hips and knees.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Back arches: use less weight.
Elbows drift: shorten the rotation.
Rotation pinches: stop rather than forcing through.

ref-Cuban_Press.safety: This combines a demanding shoulder rotation with a press. Keep the load very light and stop at pain.

ref-Double_Kettlebell_Jerk.summary: A double-kettlebell split jerk with a split-foot overhead catch.
setup: Clear a lifting area with room overhead and on both sides. Choose two matching light kettlebells.
Place the bells between your feet. Hinge, grip both handles, then drive through hips and legs to bring them close to your shoulders.
Keep wrists straight with bells outside the forearms. Set elbows near the ribs and feet hip-width apart.
Brace your middle and check that both bells rest securely in the rack.
execution: Make a small upright dip by bending both knees. Keep heels down and chest tall.
Drive strongly through the legs. Use that upward force to press both bells overhead.
As the bells rise, move one foot forward and one back. Catch the bells overhead with arms straight and knees softly bent.
Keep the bells overhead while bringing feet back under you. Stand tall, then lower the bells to the shoulders.
finish: Lower the bells to the shoulders or a controlled hang.
Bend hips and knees to place both bells on the floor. Keep feet clear and release only once the bells stop.
breathing: Breathe and brace before the dip or squat. Breathe out during the upward drive. Reset your breath after the catch.
commonErrors: Back arches overhead: reduce the load.
Bells hit forearms: keep the path close and slow the practice.

ref-Handstand_Push-Ups.summary: A wall-supported handstand push-up with the back facing the wall.

Face away from the wall, bend down, and plant hands shoulder-width apart a short distance from it.
Spread fingers and use a practiced controlled kick-up to place heels against the wall. Have a skilled spotter help when learning.
Hold arms straight with ribs drawn in and legs together. Keep the neck neutral and gaze between the hands.
execution: Bend elbows slowly to lower the body. Let elbows point slightly forward rather than straight sideways.
Stop before placing bodyweight on the head. Use only a depth you can reverse under control.
Press through both hands to straighten the elbows and raise the body.
Keep the heels lightly on the wall. Pause to regain balance before the next rep.
finish: Keep hands planted. Lower one leg in a controlled arc until its foot reaches the floor, then bring the other foot down.

ref-Iron_Cross.variant: Iron Cross — dumbbell squat to standing cross
ref-Iron_Cross.summary: A dumbbell iron cross: squat with arms forward, then stand while opening the arms out to the sides.
setup: Choose two very light dumbbells. This long-arm movement needs much less load than a press.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out. Hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Raise both arms in front to shoulder height with palms facing each other and thumbs upward.
Keep elbows softly bent and ribs over the pelvis. Leave space for a wide arm sweep.
execution: Bend hips and knees into a controlled squat while keeping the arms forward.
Stop when your feet stay flat and back stays steady. Do not force the depth shown in a photo.
Stand through both feet. As you rise, open the arms out to the sides to form a cross at shoulder height.
Bring the arms forward again as you begin the next squat. Keep the weights at a controlled height.
finish: Stand upright, bring arms forward, then lower both dumbbells to your sides.
Bend hips and knees to put the weights down.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Arms drop: use lighter weights.
Back arches: keep ribs down and reduce arm height.
Knees fall inward: align them with toes.
ref-Iron_Cross.easierOption: Practice without weights or use a shallower squat.

setup: Pick up a light kettlebell with both hands. Turn it upside down and hold the two sides of the handle, called the horns.
Keep the bell body above your hands and close to the upper chest. Check both hands have a firm grip.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and eyes ahead.
Tighten your glutes and middle so your ribs stay over your pelvis.
execution: Move the bell slowly up beside one ear. Keep it close enough to control without touching your head.
Guide it behind the head while keeping your neck, ribs, and hips still.
Continue around the other ear and return the bell to the front of the chest.
Complete equal circles in each direction.
finish: Bring the bell back to the chest. Turn it to a secure two-hand hold.
Bend hips and knees to set it on the floor.
breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift. Keep your abdomen firm.
commonErrors: Head ducks: use a lighter bell and a wider comfortable arc.
Back arches: keep ribs down.

ref-Kettlebell_Halo.easierOption: Use a lighter bell. Practice a plain halo separately before adding the extension.

ref-Kettlebell_Pirate_Ships.summary: A kettlebell pirate ship: a two-hand side-to-side swing with a controlled turn of the body.

Stand wider than shoulder-width. Hold the handle with both hands and let the bell hang near the waist.
Keep arms long but not rigid. Soften the knees and brace your middle.
Test a slow side-to-side path before adding momentum.

Keep the bell away from your face. Stop at a height you can control without leaning backward.
Let it descend as you turn toward the other side. Allow the feet and hips to turn together rather than twisting fixed knees.
Guide it up on that side. Keep the swing smooth and use the same controlled height both ways.

Bend hips and knees to place it on the floor with both hands.
breathing: Breathe steadily, letting air out as the bell rises.

Place the left knee under your hip. Lift the left hand and come to a half-kneel, right foot forward.

Step the left foot back and lower that knee. Place the left hand on the floor, lift the hips, and sweep the left leg forward.

finish: Use both hands to lower the bell to your chest. Roll onto the bell side and set it on the floor.
Move the bell to the other side while it rests; do not pass it over your face.
breathing: Take small breaths at each stable position. Keep the middle firm during transitions.
commonErrors: Bell drifts: pause and stack the wrist over the shoulder.
Steps rush: stop at each support position.

Place fingertips beside your head. Keep the elbows open and the neck relaxed.

Rise toward upright without pulling on your head or jerking with your arms.
Lower slowly about three-quarters of the way. Stop before your shoulders touch down.

Hold the handles with elbows bent. Sit evenly on the seat.

Move both parts smoothly. Avoid pulling hard with the arms or kicking with the legs.
Pause briefly, then let the pads and torso return together.
Keep the resistance under control; do not let the moving parts slam.

Drive the hips forward and return upright. Keep the top arm steady through the whole rep.

Lift your knees over your hips and bend them. Raise your shoulder blades slightly.
Set your lower back on the mat. Keep space below your chin.
execution: Reach one leg away as the other knee comes toward your chest.
Turn your ribs so the opposite shoulder moves toward the bent knee.
Return through the middle, then switch legs and turn the other way.

ref-Alternate_Heel_Touchers.summary: You hold a small crunch and bend from side to side to reach toward your heels. Both heel reaches make one rep.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, set a little wider than your hips.
Place your arms beside you, palms facing your thighs.
Lift your head and shoulder blades slightly. Keep the chin away from the chest.
execution: Slide the right hand toward the right heel by bending your trunk to that side.
Pause briefly, then move through the middle.
Reach the left hand toward the left heel, then return to the middle.
Keep both feet planted. The reach may stop short of the heel.
finish: Lower your shoulders and head gently. Relax the arms and feet.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Twisting the chest toward the ceiling: keep it facing up.
Craning the neck to reach farther: move the feet closer and use a smaller reach.
ref-Alternate_Heel_Touchers.easierOption: Bring your heels closer to your hips or rest your head between pairs.
ref-Alternate_Heel_Touchers.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.

ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout.variant: Barbell Ab Rollout — straight-leg barbell pike from a high plank
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout.summary: This source version rolls a bar toward the feet while the hips rise. It is a pike motion, rather than the kneeling rollout used in the next variation.
setup: Load a bar with equal round plates and secure collars. Check that it rolls freely.
Clear a level lane and grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders.
Step into a high plank on your toes, with shoulders above the bar.
Keep your legs long and belly firm. Check that the plates cannot skid sideways.
execution: Raise your hips and roll the bar slowly toward your feet.
Keep your arms straight and your legs as long as your range allows.
Stop before balance or grip changes. Do not force the bar to reach your toes.
Roll forward again until your body reaches a straight plank. Do not sink below that line.
finish: Return to plank, then lower both knees. Let the bar stop rolling before releasing it.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Treating this as a standing forward rollout: follow the pike path.
Letting the low back dip on return: stop at a firm plank.
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout.easierOption: Use the separately logged kneeling barbell rollout with a short reach.
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout.loadConvention: Log reps only. Note bar and plate setup separately; rolling mass is not a direct measure of abdominal resistance.
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. Preserves the source pike-style motion. The source cue to arch the back is replaced with a firm trunk position.

ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout_-_On_Knees.variant: Barbell Ab Rollout - On Knees — kneeling barbell rollout on the floor
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout_-_On_Knees.summary: A rolling bar lets the hands move away from the knees. Your trunk must stay firm during the reach and return.
setup: Fit equal round plates to both ends of the bar. Secure both collars.
Check the bar rolls smoothly on a clear, level floor.
Kneel on a mat and set the bar just ahead of your knees.
Hold the bar about shoulder-width apart with straight arms.
execution: Tighten your abs and glutes before moving.
Roll the bar forward slowly, letting the shoulders reach as the hips open.
Stop while you can still keep the ribs and hips aligned. Do not let the back sag.
Pull the bar back and bring hips and shoulders toward the start together.
finish: Return the bar close to the knees. Let it stop. Sit back on your heels before releasing your grip.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Using a long reach before learning the return: stop closer.
Sitting back first: move the hips and shoulders together.
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout_-_On_Knees.easierOption: Use a short rollout from the floor. A wall can mark a firm travel limit.
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout_-_On_Knees.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout_-_On_Knees.loadConvention: Log reps only. Record bar and plate setup in notes; bar mass is not a direct measure of rollout resistance.
ref-Barbell_Ab_Rollout_-_On_Knees.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Barbell_Rollout_from_Bench.variant: Barbell Rollout from Bench — kneeling barbell rollout from a bench
ref-Barbell_Rollout_from_Bench.summary: A rolling bar lets the hands move away from the knees. Your trunk must stay firm during the reach and return.
setup: Fit equal round plates to both ends of the bar. Secure both collars.
Check the bar rolls smoothly on a clear, level floor.
Lock a stable bench in place. Kneel near its end with both knees fully supported.
Grip the bar on the floor below the end. Start with arms straight and hips close to the knees.
execution: Tighten your abs and glutes before moving.
Roll the bar forward slowly, letting the shoulders reach as the hips open.
Stop while you can still keep the ribs and hips aligned. Do not let the back sag.
Pull the bar back and bring hips and shoulders toward the start together.
finish: Return the bar close to the knees. Let it stop. Step down from the bench with care.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Using a long reach before learning the return: stop closer.
Sitting back first: move the hips and shoulders together.

ref-Barbell_Side_Bend.variant: Barbell Side Bend — bar across upper back, side bends
ref-Barbell_Side_Bend.summary: A bar held across the upper back adds load while the trunk bends gently to each side. The hips stay near the middle.
setup: Use a light bar and clear space for both ends.
Take the bar from a rack set below shoulder height. Rest it on the upper-back muscles, below the neck.
Hold it securely with a wide grip. Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart.
Keep knees soft and face forward.
execution: Bend a short way to one side without turning your chest.
Pause, then return to tall standing.
Bend to the other side, then return again.
Use a range that keeps both feet pressed into the floor and the bar level with your shoulders.
finish: Stand square, walk back into the rack, and place the bar on both hooks before letting go.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Resting the bar on the neck: lower it onto the upper-back muscles.
Leaning forward while bending sideways: reduce the range and keep the chest facing ahead.

ref-Barbell_Side_Bend.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Barbell_Side_Bend.loadConvention: Log total barbell weight, including plates. A bend left and a bend right, each returning to center, equals one rep.
ref-Barbell_Side_Bend.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Bent-Knee_Hip_Raise.variant: Bent-Knee Hip Raise — bent knees with a small hip curl
ref-Bent-Knee_Hip_Raise.summary: You bring bent knees toward your chest, then curl the pelvis just off the floor. The knee bend stays nearly the same.
setup: Lie on your back and set your arms beside you, palms down.
Bend your knees and lift your feet a little off the mat.
Keep your head and shoulders down. Tighten your abs before the first rep.
execution: Move your thighs toward your chest without kicking the lower legs.
As the knees come in, tip the pelvis back and lift the tailbone a little.
Pause with your weight on the upper back, never on the neck.
Lower the hips first. Then move the thighs away only while your low back stays controlled.
finish: Set the hips down, bend the knees further, and lower one foot at a time.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Throwing the feet upward: use a slow pelvic curl.
Lowering until the back arches: stop with the feet higher.
ref-Bent-Knee_Hip_Raise.easierOption: Keep the knees closer to your chest and use a smaller hip lift.
ref-Bent-Knee_Hip_Raise.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Bent-Knee_Hip_Raise.loadConvention: No external load is logged. One full movement and controlled return is one rep.
ref-Bent-Knee_Hip_Raise.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Bent_Press.summary: The bent press moves your torso under a kettlebell as the arm straightens. It combines a side hinge, rotation, and an overhead hold.
setup: Clear space beside and above you. Use a light bell you can control.
Clean it to one shoulder, with the elbow close to your ribs.
Set the feet in a wide, stable stance. Turn them slightly away from the loaded side.
Keep the wrist straight and the eyes on the bell when comfortable.
execution: Shift the hips back and hinge away from the bell.
Turn the torso and bend the knees as needed while the arm straightens upward.
Let your body move under the weight. Do not jerk it up with a sideways press.
Stop at your controlled depth. Stand back up with the bell over the shoulder, then bring it to the rack position.
finish: Bring the bell from overhead to the shoulder with control. Hinge at the hips to set it down before changing sides.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Trying to reach the floor at all costs: use less depth.
Losing the overhead line: lower the load and practice the pattern unloaded.
ref-Bent_Press.easierOption: Learn the hinge and overhead hold with a light object before using a kettlebell.
ref-Bent_Press.safety: This is a complex loaded skill. Use it only when you can control the rack, hinge, and overhead positions. Stop if balance or shoulder control is lost.
ref-Bent_Press.loadConvention: Enter the weight of the single implement. Enter reps for each side. Complete both sides before marking the set done.
