ref-Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Ben.variant: Bosu Ball Cable Crunch With Side Bends — two low cables on a BOSU, then heel reaches
ref-Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Ben.summary: This sequence starts with cable crunches over a BOSU dome. It ends with small side reaches while the hips stay lifted.
setup: Set two low pulleys to equal height and light settings. Clip on two handles.
Place the BOSU dome up, centered in front of the machine. Check that its base grips the floor.
Sit, take one handle in each hand, and lower your low back onto the dome.
Plant feet wide. Hold arms straight in front, with hands between the knees.
execution: Curl the ribs toward the hips while keeping the arms fixed.
Lower over the dome only as far as your trunk stays controlled. Do the planned crunch reps.
For the second phase, lift the hips so the trunk stays level. Bring arms beside you.
Bend a small way right and left, reaching toward each heel. Keep both feet planted.
finish: Lower the hips. Sit up while controlling the handles. Let both stacks settle before releasing them.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Letting the cables pull the back into a deep arch: shorten the return.
Continuing after balance is lost: stop the sequence and lower the handles.
ref-Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Ben.easierOption: Practice a ball crunch without cables before adding the BOSU-and-cable sequence.
ref-Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Ben.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Ben.loadConvention: Log one stack setting when both stacks match; two stacks move. Log the main crunch reps. Note the number of right-plus-left heel-reach pairs separately.
ref-Bosu_Ball_Cable_Crunch_With_Side_Ben.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source calls for failure before side bends. This guide uses planned reps and stops when control fades.

ref-Bottoms_Up.variant: Bottoms Up — tuck, leg extension, and hip curl
ref-Bottoms_Up.summary: This floor sequence brings the knees in, straightens the legs upward, and adds a small pelvic curl.
setup: Lie on your back with legs long and arms beside you.
Keep the head and shoulders resting on the mat.
Press the hands lightly down and tighten the abs.
execution: Bend the knees and draw them toward your chest.
Straighten the legs toward the ceiling, keeping a little knee bend if needed.
Tip the pelvis back and lift the hips a small distance. Keep weight off the neck.
Lower the hips, bend the knees, then extend the legs only as far as the low back stays controlled.
finish: Set the hips down. Bend the knees and place both feet on the mat.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Kicking the legs up to throw the hips: slow each stage.
Dropping the legs too low: stop before the back arches.
ref-Bottoms_Up.easierOption: Leave the knees bent during the hip curl and use less lift.
ref-Bottoms_Up.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Bottoms_Up.loadConvention: No external load is logged. One tuck, leg extension, hip curl, and return sequence equals one rep.
ref-Bottoms_Up.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Butt-Ups.summary: The hips rise from a forearm plank, then return to a straight body line. Your forearms and toes stay on the floor.
setup: Kneel and set both forearms on the mat, elbows below shoulders.
Step the feet back and tuck the toes under.
Make a straight line from head to heels. Tighten the abs and glutes.
execution: Lift your hips toward the ceiling as the ribs move toward the pelvis.
Keep the forearms planted and the neck in line with the trunk.
Pause in a high pike that you can control.
Lower the hips slowly back to plank. Stop before the belly sinks toward the floor.
finish: Return to plank, then lower the knees and sit back.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Lowering below a straight plank: stop earlier.
Pushing the head between the arms: let the neck follow the trunk.
ref-Butt-Ups.easierOption: Move the hips a smaller distance or practice a short forearm plank.
ref-Butt-Ups.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Butt-Ups.loadConvention: No external load is logged. One full movement and controlled return is one rep.
ref-Butt-Ups.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source asks for a slight back arch at setup. This guide starts with a firm, straight plank.

ref-Cable_Crunch.variant: Cable Crunch — kneeling high-pulley rope crunch
ref-Cable_Crunch.summary: The cable resists a trunk curl. Your arms hold the attachment in place while your abs move the ribs toward the hips.
setup: Set the pulley before adding tension. Clip the attachment fully closed and choose a light stack setting.
Keep the cable path clear of your head and clothing.
Kneel facing a high pulley, with the rope beside your temples.
Start with a small hip bend. Keep the hands in place and the knees comfortable.
execution: Keep your hips still and curl the ribs down toward your pelvis.
Let the elbows travel toward the thighs as the trunk shortens.
Pause, then slowly open the trunk to the starting shape. Do not lean into a deep back arch.
Use the same controlled range on each rep. Let the stack settle only after the set.
finish: Return upright with control. Move toward the pulley until the stack rests, then release the rope.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Pulling down with the arms: keep the hands fixed beside the head or shoulders.
Rocking the hips or arching far back: reduce the load and shorten the return.
ref-Cable_Crunch.easierOption: Use a lighter setting or a short, separately logged floor crunch.
ref-Cable_Crunch.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Cable_Crunch.loadConvention: Log the displayed stack setting on this machine. One curl and return is one rep.
ref-Cable_Crunch.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source includes a deep backward arch or optional variations. This guide uses only the stated variation and a controlled return.

ref-Cable_Judo_Flip.variant: Cable Judo Flip — low-cable rope turn over one shoulder
ref-Cable_Judo_Flip.summary: You turn away from a low cable and draw the rope over a shoulder, then crunch slightly forward. The feet share the turn.
setup: Set a low pulley and attach a rope. Select a light setting.
Stand side-on in a wide stance. Hold both rope ends near the side closest to the machine.
Keep the cable clear of your neck. Test a small turn before the first rep.
execution: Turn your hips and chest away from the pulley.
Guide the rope over the shoulder while your feet pivot with the turn.
Shift weight toward the front foot and curl the trunk a small way forward.
Undo the curl and turn slowly back. Keep tension controlled throughout the return.
finish: Turn back toward the pulley and let the stack settle. Change your stance for the other side.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Turning on fixed feet: let the heels pivot with the hips.
Whipping the rope across the neck: reduce speed and keep a clear path.
ref-Cable_Judo_Flip.easierOption: Use a light setting and a shorter turn before adding the forward curl.
ref-Cable_Judo_Flip.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Cable_Judo_Flip.loadConvention: Log the machine stack setting. Enter reps per side; do both sides before Done.
ref-Cable_Judo_Flip.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. Keeps the source turn-and-crunch motion, but does not require training to failure.

ref-Cable_Reverse_Crunch.variant: Cable Reverse Crunch — ankle-strapped low-cable reverse crunch
ref-Cable_Reverse_Crunch.summary: The cable pulls against your legs as you bring the knees toward your chest and curl the hips off the floor.
setup: Clip a matched ankle-strap attachment to a low pulley. Select a light stack setting.
Sit facing the machine on a mat. Fasten the cuffs snugly above the ankles.
Lie back, bend both knees to roughly a right angle, and lift the feet.
Align the cable with the lower legs. Place hands beside you for support.
execution: Draw the bent knees toward the chest without changing the knee angle much.
Curl the tailbone up a little. Keep the head and shoulders on the mat.
Lower the hips first, then move the thighs back to the start.
Stop the return before the cable pulls the low back into an arch.
finish: Set your hips down. Bring the feet toward the machine until the stack rests. Sit up before removing cuffs.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Loose ankle cuffs: stop and refasten before moving.
Kicking against the cable: lower the load and start with a small hip curl.
ref-Cable_Reverse_Crunch.easierOption: Practice a bent-knee reverse crunch without the cable.
ref-Cable_Reverse_Crunch.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Cable_Reverse_Crunch.loadConvention: Log the one stack setting. One knee draw, hip curl, and return equals one rep; do not double the setting for two ankles.
ref-Cable_Reverse_Crunch.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source places hands behind the head and asks for failure. Hands beside the body and planned reps support a controlled setup.

ref-Cable_Russian_Twists.variant: Cable Russian Twists — cable rotation while supported on a ball
ref-Cable_Russian_Twists.summary: Your upper back rests on a ball while straight arms carry a cable handle through a small turn. The hips stay lifted.
setup: Set a handle at about chest height when you lie on the ball. Use a light setting.
Sit on a correctly inflated ball, hold the handle with both hands, and walk the feet forward.
Rest the upper back and head on the ball. Set feet wide and lift hips to a level bridge.
Extend the arms over the chest. The cable should pull from the side without rubbing the ball.
execution: Turn the chest away from the pulley, moving both hands together.
Let the upper back roll a small way over the ball. Keep the hips level and the feet planted.
Pause before balance changes, then turn back with control.
Use a small range first; do not chase a full quarter-turn.
finish: Turn to the start. Walk closer to release cable tension, then sit upright before letting go.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Sagging hips or rolling off the ball: shorten the turn.
Pulling with bent elbows: lower the load and keep the arms long.
ref-Cable_Russian_Twists.easierOption: Practice the ball-supported turn with empty hands first.
ref-Cable_Russian_Twists.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Cable_Russian_Twists.loadConvention: Log the single stack setting and reps per side. Complete both directions before Done.
ref-Cable_Russian_Twists.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source gives a quarter-turn and failure target. This guide limits range by balance and control.

Sit on a stable bench with your back toward a high pulley.
Hold the rope ends over the shoulders. Plant both feet and keep your seat on the bench.

Let the elbows travel toward the thighs as the trunk shortens.

ref-Cocoons.variant: Cocoons — floor tuck with overhead arm sweep
ref-Cocoons.summary: Both ends of the body curl inward at once. The knees tuck in as the arms sweep from overhead toward the legs.
setup: Lie on a mat with your legs long and arms reaching behind your head.
Keep enough space for the arms to sweep forward.
Set your head down and lightly tighten the abs before moving.
execution: Bring the knees toward the chest and tip the pelvis back a little.
At the same time, lift the shoulders and sweep the arms forward beside the knees.
Pause in the tucked shape without squeezing the chin down.
Open the arms and legs slowly. Stop before the low back arches off the mat.
finish: Bend the knees and set the feet down. Rest the shoulders and head on the mat.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Throwing the arms to lift the chest: slow the arm sweep.
Reaching the legs too low on return: keep them higher or bend them.
ref-Cocoons.easierOption: Start with the arms beside you and use a small tuck.
ref-Cocoons.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Cocoons.loadConvention: No external load is logged. One full movement and controlled return is one rep.

ref-Cross-Body_Crunch.variant: Cross-Body Crunch — alternating opposite shoulder and knee
ref-Cross-Body_Crunch.summary: A small trunk curl works the abs. This version uses alternating opposite shoulder and knee. The motion comes from your ribs moving toward your hips.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Rest fingertips beside the head without linking them tightly.
Keep a small gap between your chin and chest. Set your gaze above your knees.
execution: Lift one shoulder toward the opposite knee as that knee moves in.
Turn the ribs across the body; the elbow does not need to touch the knee.
Lower the shoulder and foot, then repeat on the other side.
Let your abs start each rep. Keep your head in line with your chest as you move.
finish: Lower your shoulders and head to the support. Set down any held weight before sitting up.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Pulling the head forward: keep the hands light and let the chest rise first.
Swinging up or sitting all the way up: slow down and use the stated small curl.
ref-Cross-Body_Crunch.easierOption: Use a smaller curl. Rest between reps if your neck starts doing the work.
ref-Cross-Body_Crunch.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Cross-Body_Crunch.loadConvention: No external load is logged. Enter reps for each side. Complete both sides before marking the set done.

Reach both arms beyond your head with palms together or crossed.
Keep a small gap between your chin and chest. Set your gaze above your knees.
execution: Curl the shoulder blades a short way off the mat.
Keep the upper arms beside your ears as the trunk rises.
Pause, then lower the shoulders without swinging the arms forward.
Let your abs start each rep. Keep your head in line with your chest as you move.

ref-Crunch_-_Legs_On_Exercise_Ball.variant: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball — lower legs resting on an exercise ball
ref-Crunch_-_Legs_On_Exercise_Ball.summary: A small trunk curl works the abs. This version uses lower legs resting on an exercise ball. The motion comes from your ribs moving toward your hips.
setup: Lie on your back and place both lower legs on a ball.
Bend knees to about a right angle. Set the ball where it stays still.
Place fingertips beside the head, with no pull on the neck.
Keep a small gap between your chin and chest. Set your gaze above your knees.
execution: Curl your ribs toward your hips. Lift your shoulder blades only a little.
Pause, then lower your shoulders slowly. Keep your lower back supported.
Let your abs start each rep. Keep your head in line with your chest as you move.
finish: Lower your shoulders and head to the support. Set down any held weight before sitting up.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.

ref-Iron_Crosses_stretch.variant: Iron Crosses (stretch) — prone alternating cross-body leg reach
ref-Iron_Crosses_stretch.summary: Lying face down, you bend one knee and move that foot across behind the body. This is a moving hip-and-trunk stretch.

Leave room on both sides for the moving leg.
Keep the head comfortable, with the face turned only as needed to breathe.

Move it slowly across toward the opposite side, allowing the hip to turn.
Stop before either shoulder is pulled up or the low back feels pinched.
Return the leg and repeat on the other side. The foot need not reach the floor.
finish: Complete the last return with control. Pause in the setup pose before you get up.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.

ref-Iron_Crosses_stretch.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source says to move quickly. This guide retains the alternating reach with a controlled pace.

ref-Isometric_Neck_Exercise_-_Front_And_.variant: Isometric Neck Exercise - Front And Back — gentle hand-resisted hold forward and backward
ref-Isometric_Neck_Exercise_-_Front_And_.summary: An isometric hold uses neck muscle effort without moving the head. Your own hand supplies gentle resistance.
setup: Sit or stand tall. Let the shoulders relax and look straight ahead.
Keep the ears above the shoulders, with the chin neither raised nor tucked hard.
Place your palm or palms across the forehead, away from your eyes.
execution: Gently press the head into the hand as the hand matches the pressure.
Keep the head still; do not tilt, turn, or lean your trunk.
Hold for the short time in your plan while breathing normally.
Release the pressure slowly. Rest, then place the hands behind the head and press gently backward without moving it.
finish: Ease off the hand pressure before moving the head. Lower the arms and rest.
breathing: Keep breathing softly through the hold. Do not hold your breath to reach farther.
commonErrors: Letting the head move: use less hand pressure.

ref-Isometric_Neck_Exercise_-_Front_And_.safety: Stop for neck pain, headache, dizziness, tingling, or symptoms into an arm. Get individual advice before using neck resistance after injury.
ref-Isometric_Neck_Exercise_-_Front_And_.loadConvention: Log hold seconds per direction, excluding rest. Complete front and back before Done. Hand pressure is not a measurable weight; load and automatic progression are off.

ref-Jackknife_Sit-Up.variant: Jackknife Sit-Up — simultaneous long-leg and trunk lift

ref-Kettlebell_Figure_8.summary: A kettlebell passes between and around the legs while you hold a hip hinge. The bell traces a figure eight around the thighs.
setup: Place one light bell between your feet. Clear the floor so a dropped bell cannot hit anything.
Stand wider than the hips and soften the knees.
Push the hips back with the chest long. Reach down and pick up the handle.
execution: Reach the empty hand behind one thigh and take the handle between the legs.
Guide the bell around the outside of that thigh and back through the middle.
Pass to the other hand behind the opposite thigh, then guide it around that leg.
Keep the bell low. Make the handoff secure before the first hand lets go.
finish: Bring the bell to the middle and lower it to the floor with both feet planted.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Looking down by rounding the back: keep the neck in line with the trunk.
Rushing the handoff: slow down and use a lighter bell.

ref-Kettlebell_Figure_8.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Kettlebell_Figure_8.loadConvention: Log the one kettlebell weight. A full circuit around both legs, returning to the starting hand, equals one rep.

ref-Kettlebell_Pass_Between_The_Legs.variant: Kettlebell Pass Between The Legs — hand-to-hand W-path pass
ref-Kettlebell_Pass_Between_The_Legs.summary: A kettlebell passes between and around the legs while you hold a hip hinge. The source calls this a W path.

Stand wider than the hips and soften the knees.
Push the hips back with the chest long. Reach down and pick up the handle.

Guide the bell out beside that leg, then bring it back through the gap for the return handoff, making the source’s W-shaped path.

Reverse the path smoothly. Keep the feet still and stop if you must round the back to reach.
finish: Bring the bell to the middle and lower it to the floor with both feet planted.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Looking down by rounding the back: keep the neck in line with the trunk.

ref-Kettlebell_Windmill.variant: Kettlebell Windmill — one overhead kettlebell with free-hand reach
ref-Kettlebell_Windmill.summary: This side hinge combines hip motion with an overhead hold. The top bell stays over the shoulder while your trunk moves below it.

Keep the wrist over the shoulder. Turn both feet slightly away from the raised arm.
Let the free hand rest on the inside of the front thigh.

Hinge at the hips and turn your chest slightly upward. Watch the raised bell if your neck is comfortable.
Slide the free hand down the inner leg. The hand does not need to touch the floor.
Drive the hips forward and return upright. Keep the top arm steady through the whole rep.
finish: Stand fully before lowering the top bell to your shoulder. Set each bell on the floor with a hip hinge. Change sides only with the weights down.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.

Letting the bell drift forward: use less weight and reset the overhead hold.

ref-Knee_Circles.variant: Knee Circles — small standing knee circles

ref-Knee_Hip_Raise_On_Parallel_Bars.variant: Knee/Hip Raise On Parallel Bars — supported straight-leg raise on a captain’s chair

Grip the handles and rest the back against the rear pad.
Press down through the forearms, then lift the feet clear of the steps.

Keep the back against the pad and the shoulders away from the ears.
Pause without swinging, then lower until the legs hang still.

Pivot the feet so the knees turn with the toes.
Raise the bar through the middle and guide it toward the other side.

breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.

setup: Use only a Smith machine whose maker permits this setup. Set safety stops just below the lowest bar position.
Lock a flat bench in place and center it under the bar. Check that your head and trunk fit on the pad.
Set a very light load. With a helper controlling the hooks, place both soles squarely under the bar.
Keep a small bend in the knees and hold stable frame grips. Release the bar only when both feet are secure.
execution: Keep the knee angle nearly still and tip the pelvis back.
Lift the hips a small distance from the pad by curling the lower trunk.
Pause with head and shoulders supported, then lower the hips slowly.
Keep both feet centered under the bar and stop if either sole shifts.
finish: Lower the hips and have the helper secure both hooks. Confirm the bar is supported before removing either foot.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Turning this into a knee press: keep the knee bend nearly fixed.
Trying to hook or unhook the bar with the feet: use the planned helper and safety stops.
ref-Smith_Machine_Hip_Raise.easierOption: Use a floor bent-knee hip raise with no bar.
ref-Smith_Machine_Hip_Raise.safety: Do not improvise this setup on a machine that cannot be safely released and secured. Never rely on the soles alone as the only protection under a loaded bar.
ref-Smith_Machine_Hip_Raise.loadConvention: Log the machine’s documented resistance convention: added plates plus documented carriage resistance, or the machine’s stated load. Keep the same convention; automatic progression is off.
ref-Smith_Machine_Hip_Raise.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source omits a safe release and re-rack method and suggests holding the frame. This guide adds stops and a helper; compatibility remains machine-specific.

ref-Spell_Caster.summary: Two dumbbells move together near the hips as the chest turns side to side. The feet pivot with the hips.
setup: Choose two light dumbbells and clear space beside both hips.
Stand with feet wide, knees soft, and palms facing down or inward as your wrists allow.
Hold arms long in front without locking the elbows.
Start with both weights close to one hip and the chest turned slightly that way.
execution: Turn the hips and trunk to move both dumbbells toward the other hip.
Let the feet pivot so the knees turn with the toes.
Keep the sweep low and smooth. Do not fling the weights behind the body.
Reverse under control and return to the first side.
finish: Bring both weights to the middle and let them stop. Hinge at the hips to set them down.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Whipping the weights using a back twist: use less load and a smaller arc.
Turning over locked knees: soften the knees and pivot the feet.
ref-Spell_Caster.easierOption: Practice the path empty-handed, then use very light dumbbells.
ref-Spell_Caster.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Spell_Caster.loadConvention: Log the weight of one dumbbell; both equal dumbbells are used. One sweep to the far side and back equals one rep.
ref-Spell_Caster.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source uses a swinging motion. This guide retains the sweep but limits speed by control.

ref-Spider_Crawl.variant: Spider Crawl — low-plank alternating knee-to-elbow reach
ref-Spider_Crawl.summary: You hold the bottom part of a push-up while one knee moves toward the same-side elbow. The hands remain in place.
setup: Set hands just wider than the shoulders and step feet back together.
Bend the elbows to a low push-up position that you can hold steadily.
Keep the trunk in one line and the neck long. Brace the abs before lifting a foot.
execution: Lift one foot and turn that knee out to the side.
Draw the knee toward the same-side elbow without rolling the hips.
Return the leg until the toes are back on the floor.
Repeat on the other side while the chest stays at a steady height.
finish: Set both feet down, lower the knees, and rest the chest.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Dropping the belly as the leg moves: use a higher arm position.
Rocking side to side to reach the elbow: shorten the knee reach.
ref-Spider_Crawl.easierOption: Use straight arms in a high plank and a smaller knee reach.
ref-Spider_Crawl.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Spider_Crawl.loadConvention: Log reps per side. Each knee reaching and returning is one rep for that side. No external load is logged.
ref-Spider_Crawl.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. Despite the crawl name, the source keeps the hands fixed; this guide preserves that stationary knee-to-elbow version.

terms.meaning: Tighten the muscles around your middle while you keep breathing.

ref-Spinal_Stretch.variant: Spinal Stretch — seated turn with a small forward lean
ref-Spinal_Stretch.summary: This chair-based mobility sequence combines a gentle trunk turn with a small forward lean. Both feet remain planted.
setup: Sit toward the front of a firm chair that cannot roll.
Set feet flat and apart enough to support you.
Rest hands lightly beside the head with elbows open. Keep the neck long.
execution: Turn the upper chest a little toward one side, then return to center.
Repeat a few gentle turns without forcing a larger range.
Turn once more and lean forward a small way toward the inside of that knee.
Return upright before changing sides. The elbow does not need to reach the floor.
finish: Return to upright sitting and let the arms rest.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Pulling the chin down with the hands: keep hands light.
Trying to force the elbow to the floor: use a small comfortable lean.
ref-Spinal_Stretch.easierOption: Cross the arms at the chest and do only the seated turn.
ref-Spinal_Stretch.safety: Use mild stretch tension. Stop for sharp pain, tingling, or numbness. Do not force extra range.
ref-Spinal_Stretch.loadConvention: Log one gentle turn-and-lean sequence per side as one rep. No external load is logged.
ref-Spinal_Stretch.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source repeats end-range twists and reaches the elbow to the floor. This guide keeps the sequence but limits both motions by comfort.

ref-Split_Squats.summary: The source version jumps between split stances, switching which leg is forward. It is a moving jump drill rather than a held stretch.
setup: Use a nonslip floor and enough space above and around you.
Start in a short split stance with one foot forward and the other behind.
Keep the feet on separate hip-width tracks. Bend both knees slightly.
Set the arms where they help balance and keep the chest lifted.
execution: Push through both feet for a small jump.
Switch the front and rear legs while in the air.
Land softly in the new split stance, bending both knees to absorb the landing.
Regain balance before the next switch. Keep the front knee following its toes.
finish: Land, let the body become still, then step the feet together.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Landing with feet on one narrow line: widen the stance.
Bouncing again before control returns: pause and reset.
ref-Split_Squats.easierOption: Step between split stances without jumping.
ref-Split_Squats.safety: Use the stepping option if you cannot land quietly and keep balance. Stop for joint pain or loss of landing control.
ref-Split_Squats.loadConvention: Log landings per lead leg. A landing with the left leg forward is one left rep; do the same count with the right leg forward. No external load is logged.
ref-Split_Squats.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source name is Split Squats but its cues describe jumping leg switches. This guide preserves that specific moving version.

ref-Standing_Biceps_Stretch.variant: Standing Biceps Stretch — standing biceps and front-shoulder opening
ref-Standing_Biceps_Stretch.summary: A held stretch for standing biceps and front-shoulder opening. Settle into mild tension, then stay still while you breathe.
setup: Warm up with a few minutes of easy movement before stretching.
Stand tall and link the hands behind your back.
Keep the arms low and softly straight. Use a towel between the hands if they do not meet.
Let the shoulders settle away from the ears.
execution: Turn the palms gently downward if comfortable.
Lift the linked hands a little away from the body while keeping the ribs over the hips.
Stop at the first mild stretch. Hold for 15–30 seconds, or the shorter time in your plan.
Keep the position steady. Do not bounce or pull harder as the hold goes on.
finish: Ease out of the hold. Return to the setup pose and rest.
breathing: Keep breathing softly through the hold. Do not hold your breath to reach farther.
commonErrors: Arching the back or shrugging to lift higher: use less lift.
Pulling farther with each breath: hold the same gentle stretch.
ref-Standing_Biceps_Stretch.easierOption: Hold a towel with a wider grip and keep the hands low.
ref-Standing_Biceps_Stretch.safety: Use mild stretch tension. Stop for sharp pain, tingling, or numbness. Do not force extra range.
ref-Standing_Biceps_Stretch.loadConvention: No external load is logged. Enter hold time in seconds, excluding rest and setup.
ref-Standing_Biceps_Stretch.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here.

ref-Standing_Cable_Lift.variant: Standing Cable Lift — standing low-to-high cable lift
ref-Standing_Cable_Lift.summary: Both hands move a cable handle diagonally across the body. The hips and feet turn with the trunk.
setup: Set a single handle at the lowest pulley and choose a light setting.
Stand side-on with feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the handle in both hands.
Step away until the cable is taut. Start with hands near the hip closest to the machine and knees partly bent.
Keep arms long but not locked and check that the cable clears your body.
execution: Move the handle up and across toward the opposite shoulder as the legs straighten.
Turn the hips and chest together. Let the rear foot pivot so the knee follows the toes.
Stop before the arms pull the trunk out of balance.
Reverse the path slowly, returning the hands and legs to the setup position.
finish: Return to the starting side and step toward the machine until the stack rests. Then switch stance.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Twisting against fixed feet: let the feet share the turn.
Yanking with bent elbows: use a lighter setting and move smoothly.
ref-Standing_Cable_Lift.easierOption: Use less weight and a shorter diagonal path.
ref-Standing_Cable_Lift.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.
ref-Standing_Cable_Lift.loadConvention: Log the machine stack setting and reps per side. Complete both sides before Done.
ref-Standing_Cable_Lift.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source prescribes training to failure. This guide stops the set when the diagonal path or balance cannot be controlled.

ref-Standing_Elevated_Quad_Stretch.variant: Standing Elevated Quad Stretch — front thigh with the rear foot elevated

Rest the top of one foot on the support behind you.
Keep the standing knee soft and hold a fixed rail or chair if needed.
execution: Keep the trunk tall and gently bring the pelvis under the ribs.
Bend the standing knee a little until the front of the rear thigh feels a mild stretch.
Stop at the first mild stretch. Hold for 15–30 seconds, or the shorter time in your plan.
Keep the position steady. Do not bounce or pull harder as the hold goes on.
finish: Ease out of the stretch and return to the starting position before changing sides.
breathing: Keep breathing softly through the hold. Do not hold your breath to reach farther.
commonErrors: Using a high support that arches the back: choose a lower surface.
Pulling farther with each breath: hold the same gentle stretch.
ref-Standing_Elevated_Quad_Stretch.easierOption: Use a lower step or a regular standing quad stretch.
ref-Standing_Elevated_Quad_Stretch.safety: Use mild stretch tension. Stop for sharp pain, tingling, or numbness. Do not force extra range.

ref-Standing_Gastrocnemius_Calf_Stretch.variant: Standing Gastrocnemius Calf Stretch — straight-knee calf with the heel on a step

Keep the other foot on the floor and bend that knee a little.

execution: Hinge forward slightly and reach toward the raised forefoot.
Gently draw the toes toward the shin while keeping the raised knee softly straight.
Stop at the first mild stretch. Hold for 15–30 seconds, or the shorter time in your plan.
Keep the position steady. Do not bounce or pull harder as the hold goes on.
finish: Ease out of the stretch and return to the starting position before changing sides.
breathing: Keep breathing softly through the hold. Do not hold your breath to reach farther.

setup: Warm up with a few minutes of easy movement before stretching.
Loop a strap around one forefoot and step that foot a short way forward.
Keep the front heel down and lift its toes.
Bend the back knee and hold a support if needed for balance.
execution: Hinge the hips back over the rear leg.
Keep the front knee softly straight and use light strap tension to draw its toes toward the shin.
Stop at the first mild stretch. Hold for 10–20 seconds, or the shorter time in your plan.
Keep the position steady. Do not bounce or pull harder as the hold goes on.
finish: Ease out of the stretch and return to the starting position before changing sides.
breathing: Keep breathing softly through the hold. Do not hold your breath to reach farther.

ref-Standing_Hip_Circles.variant: Standing Hip Circles — supported standing hip circles
ref-Standing_Hip_Circles.summary: One bent knee draws a circle while the other leg supports you. A fixed hand support helps keep the trunk still.
setup: Stand beside a fixed rail and hold it lightly.
Keep the standing knee soft and the pelvis level.
Lift the other knee in front to a comfortable height below or near hip level.
execution: Move the knee outward to open the hip.
Continue the circle back and down, then bring the knee forward again.
Use a slow circle that does not tip the trunk or roll the standing foot.
Reverse direction after the planned reps, then change legs.
finish: Set both feet down and pause before changing legs.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Making a large circle with a trunk lean: draw a smaller circle.
Locking the standing knee: keep it soft.

Hold the small tuck while breathing. The knees may stay softly bent; do not squeeze into a hard back flattening.
Stop at the first mild stretch. Hold for 10–20 seconds, or the shorter time in your plan.
Keep the position steady. Do not bounce or pull harder as the hold goes on.

ref-Standing_Rope_Crunch.variant: Standing Rope Crunch — standing rope crunch with back to the pulley
ref-Standing_Rope_Crunch.summary: The cable resists a trunk curl. Your arms hold the attachment in place while your abs move the ribs toward the hips.
setup: Set the pulley before adding tension. Clip the attachment fully closed and choose a light stack setting.
Keep the cable path clear of your head and clothing.
Stand with your back to a high pulley. Bring the rope ends over the shoulders to the upper chest.
Set feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and hips steady.
execution: Keep your hips still and curl the ribs down toward your pelvis.
Let the elbows travel toward the thighs as the trunk shortens.
Pause, then slowly open the trunk to the starting shape. Do not lean into a deep back arch.
Use the same controlled range on each rep. Let the stack settle only after the set.
finish: Return upright with control. Move toward the pulley until the stack rests, then release the rope.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Pulling down with the arms: keep the hands fixed beside the head or shoulders.
Rocking the hips or arching far back: reduce the load and shorten the return.

ref-Standing_Rope_Crunch.safety: Stay within a range you can control. Stop for sharp pain or if you lose the setup position.

ref-Stomach_Vacuum.variant: Stomach Vacuum — gentle abdominal draw-in while standing
ref-Stomach_Vacuum.summary: You draw the lower belly inward while staying tall and breathing. This is a timed muscle-control hold, not a breath-holding drill.

Place hands on your hips or lower ribs.
Keep shoulders relaxed and the ribs above the pelvis.
execution: Take an easy breath in, then breathe out slowly.
Gently draw the belly inward, as if narrowing the waist.
Keep that light muscle effort while continuing small, normal breaths.

ref-Supine_One-Arm_Overhead_Throw.variant: Supine One-Arm Overhead Throw — one-arm supine sit-up throw
ref-Supine_One-Arm_Overhead_Throw.summary: A medicine ball starts behind your head while you lie down. You sit up and throw it forward into a clear area.

Keep the ball off your face and start with a short practice throw.

Release the ball into the clear lane in front of you as you reach a seated position.

Let the ball settle, or let the partner secure it, before resetting the next rep.
finish: Finish seated. Retrieve the ball only when the lane is clear, then lie back to reset.

ref-Supine_One-Arm_Overhead_Throw.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source asks for maximum distance and allows a wall bounce. This guide uses a controlled throw and a planned safe reset.

ref-Suspended_Fallout.summary: You lean forward into suspension handles as the arms reach overhead. The trunk stays in a straight line during the reach and return.

Face away from the anchor and hold both handles with straight arms.
Lean forward a little with feet planted. Tighten the belly and glutes.
execution: Let both arms reach forward and overhead as the whole body leans farther.
Keep the ribs and pelvis in line. Only the shoulder angle should change much.
Stop before the lower back sags or the straps go slack.
Press into the handles and draw the body back to the starting lean.

ref-Suspended_Reverse_Crunch.variant: Suspended Reverse Crunch — suspended feet with a knee tuck
ref-Suspended_Reverse_Crunch.summary: The feet rest in suspension cradles while the hands support a high plank. Both knees draw toward the chest together.

Set equal foot-cradle lengths about a foot above the floor.

Set hands below shoulders and extend the legs into a straight plank facing away from the anchor.
execution: Bend both knees and draw them toward the chest.
Let the pelvis curl gently under as the hips move forward. Keep shoulders above the hands.
Pause before the straps swing or the upper body loses support.
Extend both legs slowly back to plank, stopping before the belly sags.
finish: Lower the knees, shift to a stable kneeling or seated position, and remove one foot at a time.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.

ref-The_Straddle.variant: The Straddle — seated wide-leg forward hinge

Place hands on the floor in front of you.
execution: Tip forward from the hips and slide the hands ahead.
Keep the chest long and stop at mild inner-thigh or hamstring tension.
Stop at the first mild stretch. Hold for 10–20 seconds, or the shorter time in your plan.

finish: Ease out of the hold. Return to the setup pose and rest.

ref-Toe_Touchers.variant: Toe Touchers — legs raised with a reach toward the toes
ref-Toe_Touchers.summary: A small trunk curl works the abs. This version uses legs raised with a reach toward the toes. The motion comes from your ribs moving toward your hips.
setup: Lie on your back with legs together and lifted toward the ceiling.
Keep a soft knee bend. Raise both arms toward the feet.
Keep a small gap between your chin and chest. Set your gaze above your knees.
execution: Curl the shoulder blades up and reach the hands toward the toes.
Keep the pelvis down and the legs as still as possible. Toe contact is not needed.
Lower the shoulders slowly while leaving the arms aimed toward the feet.
Let your abs start each rep. Keep your head in line with your chest as you move.
finish: Lower your shoulders and head to the support. Set down any held weight before sitting up.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Pulling the head forward: keep the hands light and let the chest rise first.

ref-Toe_Touchers.easierOption: Use a smaller curl. Rest between reps if your neck starts doing the work.
ref-Toe_Touchers.safety: Use mild stretch tension. Stop for sharp pain, tingling, or numbness. Do not force extra range.

ref-Toe_Touchers.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. Although the source category is stretching, its cues describe repeated abdominal curls; this entry uses reps.

ref-Torso_Rotation.variant: Torso Rotation — standing turns with a ball held forward
ref-Torso_Rotation.summary: An exercise ball is held in front of the chest while the trunk turns side to side. The ball acts as a light reach cue.
setup: Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart and knees soft.
Hold an exercise ball with both hands, arms long but not locked.
Keep the ball below eye level and the shoulders relaxed.
execution: Turn the chest and ball a short way to one side.
Let the eyes follow the ball while the hips stay mostly facing forward.
Return through the middle and turn the other way.
Keep the movement slow enough that the ball does not pull you off balance.
finish: Return to the middle and lower the ball to the floor with control.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Arching the low back to hold the ball higher: lower the arms.
Swinging the ball while the chest stays still: shorten the turn and move them together.
ref-Torso_Rotation.easierOption: Hold the ball closer to the chest or practice with empty hands.
ref-Torso_Rotation.safety: Use mild stretch tension. Stop for sharp pain, tingling, or numbness. Do not force extra range.
ref-Torso_Rotation.loadConvention: No external load is logged for the light exercise ball. One left turn and one right turn equals one rep.
ref-Torso_Rotation.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source is a light moving mobility drill. This guide does not treat the exercise ball as a weighted medicine ball.

ref-Tricep_Side_Stretch.variant: Tricep Side Stretch — cross-body triceps and shoulder stretch
ref-Tricep_Side_Stretch.summary: A held stretch for cross-body triceps and shoulder stretch. Settle into mild tension, then stay still while you breathe.
setup: Warm up with a few minutes of easy movement before stretching.
Stand or sit tall with relaxed shoulders.
Bring one upper arm across your chest and bend the elbow so the hand passes toward the opposite shoulder.
Support the upper arm just above the elbow with the other hand.
execution: Guide the arm gently across the chest.
Keep the shoulder down and stop before the joint feels pinched.
Stop at the first mild stretch. Hold for 15–30 seconds, or the shorter time in your plan.
Keep the position steady. Do not bounce or pull harder as the hold goes on.
finish: Ease out of the stretch and return to the starting position before changing sides.
breathing: Keep breathing softly through the hold. Do not hold your breath to reach farther.

Pulling farther with each breath: hold the same gentle stretch.

Lower that leg as the other knee rises.

ref-Windmills.summary: Lying on your back, one leg rises and crosses toward the opposite side. The arms stay out to steady the trunk.
setup: Lie on a mat with both arms out to the sides.
Keep legs long with soft knees and both shoulders comfortable on the floor.
Leave room on each side for a leg to move across.
execution: Raise one leg, then guide it across the body toward the opposite side.
Let the pelvis turn a little while the opposite leg stays long.
Stop before the shoulder is pulled up or the back feels strained.
Return the leg to the middle and lower it. Repeat with the other leg.
finish: Bring both legs back to the middle and bend the knees before getting up.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Throwing the leg toward the opposite hand: use a smaller slow arc.
Forcing floor contact: let the foot stop in the air if needed.
ref-Windmills.easierOption: Bend the crossing knee and use a knee-across-body stretch.
ref-Windmills.safety: Use mild stretch tension. Stop for sharp pain, tingling, or numbness. Do not force extra range.
ref-Windmills.loadConvention: Log reps per leg. One leg crossing and returning is one rep for that side. No external load is logged.
ref-Windmills.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. The source says to cross quickly and reach the floor near the hand. This guide keeps the crossover with a controlled pace and comfortable endpoint.

ref-Worlds_Greatest_Stretch.variant: World's Greatest Stretch — three-part lunge, inside-elbow, and hamstring stretch
ref-Worlds_Greatest_Stretch.summary: This sequence has three holds on each side. It moves from a lunge to an inside-foot reach, then a front-leg hamstring stretch.
setup: Start with one foot in front and the rear toes planted in a long split stance.
Bend both knees and lower the rear knee near the floor. Use a pad if it rests down.
Keep the front heel planted and the trunk tall.
execution: First hold the low lunge for 10–20 seconds with mild tension at the rear hip.
Place the opposite hand on the floor. Reach the front-side elbow toward the inside of the front foot. Hold 10–20 seconds; use a block if the floor is too far.
Place both hands beside the front foot. Shift hips back, partly straighten the front knee, and raise those toes while the heel stays down.
Hold the hamstring position 10–20 seconds, then ease out and change sides.
finish: Bend the front knee again, bring the rear knee down, and return to kneeling before changing sides.
breathing: Keep breathing softly through the hold. Do not hold your breath to reach farther.
commonErrors: Forcing the elbow to the floor: use a block and shorten the reach.
Locking the front knee in the last hold: keep a small bend.
ref-Worlds_Greatest_Stretch.easierOption: Rest the rear knee on a pad and use blocks under the hands.
ref-Worlds_Greatest_Stretch.safety: Use mild stretch tension. Stop for sharp pain, tingling, or numbness. Do not force extra range.
ref-Worlds_Greatest_Stretch.loadConvention: Log the total held seconds across the three positions for one side. Repeat that total on the other side before Done. Exclude setup transitions and rest; no load is logged.
ref-Worlds_Greatest_Stretch.sourceNote: Based on the public-domain exercise record linked below. Logging instructions describe how to record the exercise here. Preserves all three source positions. The elbow and knee endpoints are limited by a comfortable range.

ref-Wrist_Circles.variant: Wrist Circles — wrist circles with arms held out

setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft, and chest upright.
Raise both arms out to the sides at or below shoulder height.
Keep elbows softly straight and palms down. Let the fingers stay loose.
execution: Circle both hands from the wrists with a small smooth motion.
Keep the forearms still instead of rotating the whole arm.
Complete the planned circles, then reverse direction.
Lower the arms if the shoulders tire or the neck starts to tense.
finish: Lower the arms and let the hands rest at your sides.
breathing: Breathe out with the effort and in as you return. Keep a steady rhythm.

ref-Clean.summary: A clean from the floor. The bar moves onto the fronts of your shoulders.
setup: Use a light bar, lock both collars and clear your space. Stand about hip-width.
Grip just outside your legs with both palms facing back. A hook grip wraps the fingers over the thumb.
Keep arms long, chest steady and whole feet down. Start with shoulders over or just ahead of the bar.
execution: Push the floor away. Let your hips and shoulders rise together as the bar passes your knees. Keep the bar close.
Drive your legs and hips tall to speed the bar upward. Keep it close; do not throw your hips forward into it.
Move down under the bar. Turn your elbows forward fast. Receive the bar across the fronts of your shoulders, with hands guiding it rather than holding all its weight.
Receive in your squat stance. Sit to a depth you can control, keeping the bar supported, then stand through both feet.
finish: Stand still with the bar secure on the front shoulders.
Lower a light bar close to the body, bending the knees to soften its return. For heavy lifts, use your practiced release onto a clear, drop-rated platform.
breathing: Breathe and brace before the pull. Breathe again once stable; reset before the next rep.
commonErrors: Bar swings away: keep it close.
Arms pull early: finish the leg drive first.
Catch feels loose: reduce the load and reset the stance.
ref-Clean.easierOption: Use a training bar and practice the pull and catch separately.
ref-Clean.safety: Learn the catch and safe release with a weightlifting coach before adding load. Use a clear, drop-rated platform and bumper plates. Never chase a falling bar.
ref-Clean.loadConvention: Enter the total weight of the bar and all plates. One full lift and return is one rep.
ref-Clean.sourceNote: Editorial rewrite of the exact Free Exercise DB exercise record (Unlicense) named in the first link. The added link gives movement-family guidance; it does not check this whole variation.

setup: Use a light bar, lock both collars and clear your space. Stand about hip-width.
Take a wide overhand grip so the bar sits near your hip crease when standing.
Keep arms long, chest steady and whole feet down. Start with shoulders over or just ahead of the bar.
execution: Push the floor away. Let your hips and shoulders rise together as the bar passes your knees. Keep the bar close.
Drive your legs and hips tall to speed the bar upward. Keep it close; do not throw your hips forward into it.
Move down under the bar as your elbows turn under. Push up firmly and receive it with straight arms above your middle.
Receive with one foot forward and the other back. Keep space between your feet from side to side. Bend both knees and hold your trunk steady.
Recover with small steps: front foot partway back, then rear foot forward, until your feet are level.
finish: Stand still with the bar secure overhead.
Lower a light bar close to the body, bending the knees to soften its return. For heavy lifts, use your practiced release onto a clear, drop-rated platform.
breathing: Breathe and brace before the pull. Breathe again once stable; reset before the next rep.
commonErrors: Bar swings away: keep it close.
Arms pull early: finish the leg drive first.
Catch feels loose: reduce the load and reset the stance.
ref-Split_Snatch.easierOption: Use a training bar and practice the pull and catch separately.
ref-Split_Snatch.safety: Learn the catch and safe release with a weightlifting coach before adding load. Use a clear, drop-rated platform and bumper plates. Never chase a falling bar.

ref-Clean_Deadlift.summary: A pull from the floor. It ends at standing, with no jump or catch.
setup: Load both ends evenly and lock the collars. Clear the floor so the bar can return without rolling.
Stand about hip-width and use a grip just outside your legs. Keep both palms facing back and your arms straight.
Start with the bar close to your shins. Bend your knees and hips; set your shoulders over or just ahead of the bar.
Brace your middle. Keep your neck in line with your back and pressure across your whole feet.
execution: Push the floor away. Raise your chest and hips together, keeping the bar close as it passes your knees.
Extend your hips and knees to stand tall. Keep the arms long; do not lean back or pull your shoulders behind your hips.
finish: Guide the bar down close to your legs. Bend your hips first, then your knees as the bar passes them.
Set it on the floor before releasing your grip. Let it settle before another rep.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Back changes shape: reduce the load and brace first.
Arms bend: keep your elbows long.
Leaning back at the top: finish with ribs over hips.
ref-Clean_Deadlift.easierOption: Use a training bar or a lighter load while keeping the same start height.
ref-Clean_Deadlift.safety: Keep these pulls controlled enough to keep the bar close. A heavier load is not useful if it changes the path or back position. Do not bounce it off the floor.

ref-Heaving_Snatch_Balance.summary: A light dip-and-catch drill. The bar starts on your upper back, and the feet stay in the squat stance.
setup: Set rack hooks just below shoulder height and clear the overhead space. Load both ends evenly and lock the collars.
Take a wide snatch grip and rest the bar across the upper back, clear of your neck.
Stand the bar out of the hooks and take a short step clear. Tighten your middle and set your feet about hip-width.
Set your feet in your squat stance before the dip. They stay in that stance during this heaving variation.
execution: Bend your knees for a short dip. Keep your chest upright and your whole feet in contact with the floor.
Drive up just enough to lighten the bar, then push yourself down under it with arms straight overhead.
Keep your feet in place as you sit into a squat.
Hold the bar over your base of support. Stand from the squat with your arms still straight.
finish: Stand still with the bar under control before ending the rep.
Lower a light bar close to your body, bending your knees to soften its return. With bumper plates on a cleared platform, use the release method you have learned. Never try to catch a falling bar.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Trunk tips during the dip: reduce its depth.
Bar drifts forward: keep the dip vertical and the middle firm.
Catch feels unstable: use a lighter bar and reset the feet.

ref-Rack_Delivery.summary: A light clean-turnover drill. It moves the bar from a high-elbow start onto the fronts of the shoulders.
setup: Use a stick or very light training bar and a clear floor.
Stand with feet about hip-width. Hold the bar close to the upper body, hands just outside shoulders.
Lift your elbows outward so the upper arms are near level and the forearms hang down. This is the scarecrow start.
Keep your chest up and your middle firm. Do not bend your wrists to hold a heavy bar here.
execution: Keep the bar close as you turn both elbows down, around and forward under it.
Let the bar settle on the fronts of your shoulders. The shoulders make its shelf; your fingers guide it.
Finish with elbows forward and wrists comfortable. Do not slam the bar into your throat.
Move slowly back to the light starting position and repeat with a clean turnover.
finish: Lower the bar to your thighs, then to the floor or rack with both hands.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Bar loops out: keep it near your shirt.

Bar strikes the throat: use a lighter bar and control the turnover.

setup: Set both hooks where slightly bent elbows can clear them. Set safeties below the press path but above the neck. Test with an empty bar.

execution: Bend the elbows and lower the bar under control. Keep your wrists stacked over your forearms; elbows angle away from your sides without flaring straight out.

Press up and slightly back toward the line over your shoulders. Keep hips down and feet planted.
Finish with straight elbows and a steady bar.

ref-Bench_Press_with_Chains.summary: A paused barbell bench press. Chains lift from the floor as the bar rises.
equipment: Matched lifting chains and rated connectors
setup: Set both hooks where slightly bent elbows can clear them. Set safeties below the press path but above the neck. Test with an empty bar.
Lie on a stable bench, with eyes near the bar. Keep your head, upper back and hips on the pad.
Grip evenly with thumbs wrapped, wrists above elbows at the bottom. Draw shoulders together and plant your feet.
Attach matched chains to both sleeves with rated links and equal leader lengths. Chain rests on the floor at the bottom; some links stay down at the top. Clear hands, feet and plates.
Ask for a lift-off if needed. Bring the bar clear of the hooks and hold it over your shoulders before lowering.
execution: Bend the elbows and lower the bar under control. Keep your wrists stacked over your forearms; elbows angle away from your sides without flaring straight out.
Stop when the bar touches your lower chest lightly. Pause without sinking or bouncing it.
Press up and slightly back toward the line over your shoulders. Keep hips down and feet planted.

Stop before your back rounds or your pelvis tucks under. Your range comes from the hips; the torso does not have to reach level with the floor.
Press through your feet and bring your hips forward to raise your torso. Stop when upright; do not lean back.
finish: Return fully to a steady start before ending the set.
Rack a back-held bar on both hooks. Set a hand-held bar down with hips and knees bent. For a band, remove tension before taking the loop off your back.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Back rounds or arches more: use less range and load.

ref-Barbell_Glute_Bridge.summary: A hip lift from the floor with a padded bar across the hips. The upper back stays on the floor.

Set your feet so the shins are near upright at the top. Keep your head and shoulders on the mat.
execution: Press through your feet and squeeze the hips upward.
Stop when shoulders, hips and knees make a roughly straight line. Keep ribs down rather than arching the low back.
Pause with the hips steady, then lower your hips to the floor slowly.
finish: Keep the hips on the floor while you remove the load.

execution: Push off the front leg and drive the other knee forward.
Travel forward and diagonally to the other side of the line.
Land on the opposite foot with the knee soft and hips steady.
Push off that foot and repeat to the other side.

ref-Chest_Push_with_Run_Release.summary: A chest throw on the second step followed by a short sprint.
setup: Set a clear lane and a separate clear ball-landing area. Stand in an athletic stance with the ball held near the thighs. Mark the sprint finish and slowing area.
Check the ball for damage and test its grip and bounce with a gentle attempt. Start with enough space to finish the throw without hitting anything.
execution: Take the first step while drawing the ball to the chest.
Take the second step and throw forward from the chest with both hands.
Sprint forward after the release while keeping clear of the ball and its bounce.
Slow beyond the finish mark and walk back.
finish: Wait until the ball is controlled or still before collecting it. Check the lane again before the next rep.
Stop the set when passes lose their line or the catch becomes rushed.
breathing: Breathe out as you throw. Take a fresh breath when the ball returns or while you reset; keep your middle firm during the pass.
commonErrors: Chasing the ball: keep your run lane clear of its path; do not try to catch your own throw.
Ball slips: dry it and use a lighter size you can hold.
Trunk folds or twists: reduce the effort and set the feet again.
ref-Chest_Push_with_Run_Release.easierOption: Use a lighter ball, shorter pass and a full pause between throws. For a linked run or fall drill, practice the throw alone first.
ref-Chest_Push_with_Run_Release.safety: Keep people out of the throwing lane. Use a ball and wall rated for this use. A partner must see the throw and be ready; do not throw toward an unready person.
ref-Chest_Push_with_Run_Release.loadConvention: Log active drill time in seconds and sprint distance in meters in the Distance field. Note ball weight and run setup.
ref-Chest_Push_with_Run_Release.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Medicine_Ball_Chest_Pass.summary: A standing two-hand chest pass and return catch.
setup: Face a ready partner or a throw-rated wall. Use a light ball and begin close enough for an easy chest-height pass.
Check the ball for damage and test its grip and bounce with a gentle attempt. Start with enough space to finish the throw without hitting anything.
execution: Hold the ball near the chest with elbows bent.
Push it forward by extending both arms toward the target; a small step can help.
Stay balanced after release and bring both hands up ready for the return.
Catch near chest height, letting elbows bend and the ball move toward the body.
finish: Wait until the ball is controlled or still before collecting it. Check the lane again before the next rep.
Stop the set when passes lose their line or the catch becomes rushed.
breathing: Breathe out as you throw. Take a fresh breath when the ball returns or while you reset; keep your middle firm during the pass.
commonErrors: Throw is too hard to catch: shorten the distance and reduce effort.
Ball slips: dry it and use a lighter size you can hold.
Trunk folds or twists: reduce the effort and set the feet again.

ref-Medicine_Ball_Chest_Pass.safety: Keep people out of the throwing lane. Use a ball and wall rated for this use. A partner must see the throw and be ready; do not throw toward an unready person.
ref-Medicine_Ball_Chest_Pass.loadConvention: Enter the weight of the single ball. Count each throw once; a return catch does not add a rep.

ref-Medicine_Ball_Scoop_Throw.summary: A backward scoop throw with straight arms and a small jump.
setup: Face away from a fully clear throwing area. Stand in a shallow squat with the ball near the feet, held in both hands.
Check the ball for damage and test its grip and bounce with a gentle attempt. Start with enough space to finish the throw without hitting anything.
execution: Drive the hips and knees tall and let the feet leave the ground.
Swing the long arms upward and over the head as the body rises.
Release into the clear area behind you without twisting.
Bring the feet back beneath you and land softly before turning around.
finish: Wait until the ball is controlled or still before collecting it. Check the lane again before the next rep.
Stop the set when passes lose their line or the catch becomes rushed.
breathing: Breathe out as you throw. Take a fresh breath when the ball returns or while you reset; keep your middle firm during the pass.
commonErrors: Arms bend into a chest pass: keep a long scoop path with a light ball.
Ball slips: dry it and use a lighter size you can hold.

ref-Overhead_Slam.summary: A two-hand overhead slam into the floor in front of the feet.
setup: Use a ball specifically rated for slams and check how much it bounces. Clear the floor and overhead space. Stand about shoulder-width.
Check the ball for damage and test its grip and bounce with a gentle attempt. Start with enough space to finish the throw without hitting anything.
execution: Raise the ball overhead without arching the low back.
Drive the ball down in front of you as hips and knees bend.
Release with hands clear and keep your face away from its rebound path.
Pick up a dead-bounce ball after it stops, or catch a low predictable rebound with both hands.
finish: Wait until the ball is controlled or still before collecting it. Check the lane again before the next rep.
Stop the set when passes lose their line or the catch becomes rushed.
breathing: Breathe out as you throw. Take a fresh breath when the ball returns or while you reset; keep your middle firm during the pass.
commonErrors: Bending over the bounce: stay clear until you know where the ball will return.
Ball slips: dry it and use a lighter size you can hold.

ref-Return_Push_from_Stance.summary: A catch-and-return pass after moving out of an athletic starting stance.
setup: Work with a partner using a light ball. Agree on a short route, signal and chest-height throw before starting in a two- or three-point stance.
Check the ball for damage and test its grip and bounce with a gentle attempt. Start with enough space to finish the throw without hitting anything.
execution: On the signal, rise and move into the agreed receiving space.
Set the feet and catch the pass with both hands near the chest.
Let the elbows bend briefly, then push the ball back toward the partner.
Finish in balance and reset the start stance before another route.
finish: Wait until the ball is controlled or still before collecting it. Check the lane again before the next rep.
Stop the set when passes lose their line or the catch becomes rushed.
breathing: Breathe out as you throw. Take a fresh breath when the ball returns or while you reset; keep your middle firm during the pass.
commonErrors: Pass arrives before balance: shorten the route and slow the first throw.

ref-Standing_Two-Arm_Overhead_Throw.summary: A standing two-arm throw from behind the head toward a partner or rated wall.
setup: Stand about shoulder-width facing a clear target. Hold a light ball in both hands with enough overhead room.
Check the ball for damage and test its grip and bounce with a gentle attempt. Start with enough space to finish the throw without hitting anything.
execution: Bring the ball behind the head within a comfortable shoulder range.
Bend the knees slightly, then drive forward through the legs and arms.
Release forward over the head and let the arms follow through.
Stay balanced; catch a gentle return only when both hands and feet are ready.
finish: Wait until the ball is controlled or still before collecting it. Check the lane again before the next rep.
Stop the set when passes lose their line or the catch becomes rushed.
breathing: Breathe out as you throw. Take a fresh breath when the ball returns or while you reset; keep your middle firm during the pass.

Ball slips: dry it and use a lighter size you can hold.

ref-Supine_Chest_Throw.summary: A light chest throw while lying on the back, followed by a two-hand catch.
setup: Use a light soft medicine ball you can catch easily. Lie on a mat with knees bent and feet flat. Hold the ball above the chest, clear of the face.
Check the ball for damage and test its grip and bounce with a gentle attempt. Start with enough space to finish the throw without hitting anything.
execution: Push the ball a short distance straight up by extending both elbows.
Keep both hands ready under its path and watch it throughout.
Catch it above the chest with both hands, then bend the elbows to soften the catch.
Let it settle before another small throw; do not aim for maximum height.
finish: Catch and lower the ball to the chest after the last small toss. Roll to the side and sit up with the ball controlled.
breathing: Breathe out as you throw. Take a fresh breath when the ball returns or while you reset; keep your middle firm during the pass.
commonErrors: Throw drifts toward the face: use less force and stop to reset the line.
Ball slips: dry it and use a lighter size you can hold.
Ball drifts sideways: stop, set it back over the chest and reduce the throw.
ref-Supine_Chest_Throw.easierOption: Use a lighter soft ball and a smaller toss, or practice a standing chest pass as a separate exercise.
ref-Supine_Chest_Throw.safety: A missed catch can hit the face or chest. Use only a soft, very light ball and a small toss. Stop if the throw drifts; a standing chest pass is an easier separate option.
ref-Supine_Chest_Throw.loadConvention: Enter the weight of the single ball. Count each throw once; a return catch does not add a rep.

ref-Heavy_Bag_Thrust.summary: A quick two-hand or one-hand push into a hanging heavy bag, followed by control of its return.
setup: Check the mount and bag for damage. Make sure the whole swing path is clear.
Stand beside the bag with a comfortable staggered stance and knees soft.
Place a hand on the bag near chest height with the wrist straight. Begin with a small push to learn the swing.
execution: Turn through the hips and trunk together as you push the bag away.
Let the feet turn with the body so the knees do not twist against planted feet.
Keep the push short and smooth; do not strike with a locked elbow.
Meet the returning bag with a soft elbow and let the hips turn back to slow it.
finish: Stop the bag gently before leaving its path. Do not walk under or behind a moving bag.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Feet stick while the trunk turns: let the heels turn with the hips.
Elbow locks on return: soften the arm.
Bag swings too far: use less force.
ref-Heavy_Bag_Thrust.easierOption: Use a smaller push and stop the bag fully between reps.
ref-Heavy_Bag_Thrust.safety: Use a secure bag that is meant for pushing and striking. Keep your face out of its return path and stop if the mount moves.
ref-Heavy_Bag_Thrust.loadConvention: Count one push and controlled return as one rep. Note the bag and side used; its full mass is not a lifted load.
ref-Heavy_Bag_Thrust.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Isometric_Chest_Squeezes.summary: A chest isometric: the palms press together while the arms stay still.
setup: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed and feet supported.
Bring open palms together in front of the chest. Bend the elbows about a right angle and point fingers forward.
Keep wrists comfortable and the neck long. Set a timer you can see without turning.
execution: Press the palms together gently and build to a firm, comfortable squeeze.
Keep the hands near the chest without lifting the shoulders or holding your breath.
Hold the same pressure for the planned time. Ease it if the wrists or shoulders feel strained.
finish: Gradually release the pressure and let the arms relax. Rest before another hold.
breathing: Breathe normally for the whole hold; do not hold your breath.
commonErrors: Shoulders rise toward ears: ease the force and lower them.
Breath stops: use less effort so you can breathe normally.
Wrists bend painfully: adjust the hand angle.
ref-Isometric_Chest_Squeezes.easierOption: Use a gentler squeeze for a shorter time, with the forearms in a comfortable position.
ref-Isometric_Chest_Squeezes.safety: This is a hold, not a maximum-force contest. Stop if there is pain, tingling or dizziness.
ref-Isometric_Chest_Squeezes.loadConvention: Log the seconds held with steady pressure. No added load or rep count is needed.
ref-Isometric_Chest_Squeezes.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Carioca_Quick_Step.summary: A sideways carioca step with a quick rear-foot cross and knee lift.
setup: Stand tall beside a clear level lane, knees soft, facing across the direction of travel.
Warm up with easy movement first. Test the route at walking speed and remove loose objects before moving quickly.
execution: Step sideways with the lead foot.
Cross the trailing foot behind it, then lift that knee forward and up as you uncross.
Use short quick steps while the arms swing to balance the body.
Keep looking in your original direction. Stop and repeat toward the other side.
finish: Reduce speed before stopping. Take a full reset between bouts so the next start is controlled.
For a supported or kneeling drill, come out of the position slowly and change sides only when balanced.
breathing: Keep breathing in a steady rhythm. Avoid holding your breath while the feet or arms move quickly.
commonErrors: Turning the whole body down the lane: keep the chest facing across it.
Arms and shoulders tense: loosen the hands and reduce speed.
Feet lose their rhythm: slow down and rebuild the pattern.
ref-Carioca_Quick_Step.easierOption: Use a slower pace and a shorter bout. Learn the same foot or arm pattern before adding speed.
ref-Carioca_Quick_Step.safety: Do not sprint into a wall, person or stopping point. Keep room to slow down. End the bout when foot placement or trunk control gets worse.
ref-Carioca_Quick_Step.loadConvention: Log active drill time in seconds. Add traveled distance in meters in the Distance field and note the route.
ref-Carioca_Quick_Step.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Kneeling_Arm_Drill.summary: A kneeling arm-swing drill that practices running rhythm while the lower body stays still.
setup: Use a firm pad. Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat ahead and trunk upright.
Warm up with easy movement first. Test the route at walking speed and remove loose objects before moving quickly.
execution: Swing one arm forward as the other moves back, keeping the hands relaxed.
Start with easy long swings, then bend the elbows more into a running shape.
Move faster while the hands pass beside the hips and the torso stays still.
Change the front leg and repeat the same arm rhythm.
finish: Reduce speed before stopping. Take a full reset between bouts so the next start is controlled.
For a supported or kneeling drill, come out of the position slowly and change sides only when balanced.
breathing: Keep breathing in a steady rhythm. Avoid holding your breath while the feet or arms move quickly.
commonErrors: Hands cross the chest: send each hand forward and back beside the body.
Arms and shoulders tense: loosen the hands and reduce speed.
Feet lose their rhythm: slow down and rebuild the pattern.

ref-Linear_3-Part_Start_Technique.summary: A sprint start from a staggered three-point stance.
setup: Mark a start line and a short clear lane with extra slowing space. Place one foot ahead, the other a short step back, and the opposite hand on the line.
Warm up with easy movement first. Test the route at walking speed and remove loose objects before moving quickly.
execution: Bend the hips and knees and lean forward with weight through the front foot and support hand.
Hold the free arm behind you with shoulders steady.
Push into the ground and drive forward out of the stance when ready.
Use short forceful first steps and rise gradually as speed builds.
finish: Reduce speed before stopping. Take a full reset between bouts so the next start is controlled.
For a supported or kneeling drill, come out of the position slowly and change sides only when balanced.
breathing: Keep breathing in a steady rhythm. Avoid holding your breath while the feet or arms move quickly.
commonErrors: Standing straight up on the first step: drive forward before rising.

ref-Linear_Acceleration_Wall_Drill.summary: A supported acceleration drill with quick alternating knee drives.
setup: Use a wall that will not move. Place hands at shoulder height and walk the feet back until the body leans forward in one straight line.
Warm up with easy movement first. Test the route at walking speed and remove loose objects before moving quickly.
execution: Raise one knee while the other leg supports you. Keep toes up and hips level.
Drive that foot down under the hip and pause.
Repeat on the other side, then use short alternating switches once the shape stays steady.
Keep hands fixed and avoid pumping the low back.
finish: Reduce speed before stopping. Take a full reset between bouts so the next start is controlled.
For a supported or kneeling drill, come out of the position slowly and change sides only when balanced.
breathing: Keep breathing in a steady rhythm. Avoid holding your breath while the feet or arms move quickly.
