ref-Mountain_Climbers.summary: Fast alternating knee drives from a high plank.
setup: Place hands on firm ground beneath the shoulders. Extend the legs back with toes down and hips near the shoulder line.
Warm up with easy movement first. Test the route at walking speed and remove loose objects before moving quickly.
execution: Bring one knee toward the chest without lifting the hips high.
Switch the feet so that leg extends back as the other knee comes forward.
Keep pushing the floor away and keep the shoulders above the hands.
Use a pace that lets the trunk stay still rather than bouncing side to side.
finish: Reduce speed before stopping. Take a full reset between bouts so the next start is controlled.
For a supported or kneeling drill, come out of the position slowly and change sides only when balanced.
breathing: Keep breathing in a steady rhythm. Avoid holding your breath while the feet or arms move quickly.

ref-Moving_Claw_Series.summary: A moving sprint-form drill that brings the heel up, then the foot down beneath the body.
setup: Choose a clear level lane. Start with a slow run or marching rhythm so you can control where each foot lands.
Warm up with easy movement first. Test the route at walking speed and remove loose objects before moving quickly.
execution: As the leg moves behind, bend the knee so the heel travels toward the hips.
Bring that knee forward, then bring the foot down under the body.
Use the opposite arm with each leg, moving hands forward and back near the hips.
Build a quicker rhythm only while the steps stay light and do not reach far ahead.
finish: Reduce speed before stopping. Take a full reset between bouts so the next start is controlled.
For a supported or kneeling drill, come out of the position slowly and change sides only when balanced.
breathing: Keep breathing in a steady rhythm. Avoid holding your breath while the feet or arms move quickly.
commonErrors: Reaching the foot out in front: place it closer beneath the hips.

ref-Single-Cone_Sprint_Drill.summary: A quick-foot drill that circles a single cone with short running steps.
setup: Place a soft cone on a level open surface. Leave room for a wide circle and a safe exit. Start beside it with arms in a running position.
Warm up with easy movement first. Test the route at walking speed and remove loose objects before moving quickly.
execution: Take short quick steps around the cone rather than pivoting on one foot.
Let the arms work forward and back to match the legs.
Keep the hips controlled and eyes on the route ahead.
Finish the planned time, slow down, then repeat in the other direction.
finish: Reduce speed before stopping. Take a full reset between bouts so the next start is controlled.
For a supported or kneeling drill, come out of the position slowly and change sides only when balanced.
breathing: Keep breathing in a steady rhythm. Avoid holding your breath while the feet or arms move quickly.
commonErrors: Turning on a planted foot: use several small steps around a wider circle.

ref-Atlas_Stone_Trainer.summary: A stone-style lift with a purpose-built plate-loaded trainer, using a lap before standing.
setup: Use a load you can hold close. Clear the path and drop area.
Check the trainer, collar and plates. Use a purpose-built implement with secure fittings.
Stand with the object between your feet. Bend your hips and knees and reach around it with both arms.
execution: Pull the object close to your trunk and push through the feet to lift it past your knees. Keep the load near you rather than curling it out in front.
Sit back a little and settle it securely on your thighs. This lap position lets you reset your grip.
Hug it high against your chest and drive the hips and knees to stand. Keep the hands clear of any place the object can pinch them.
Finish as tall as you can while holding the trainer close. Keep ribs over hips instead of leaning far back.
finish: Make sure the object is supported before letting go. Step clear of its possible fall path.
Use a planned, controlled return or have the platform reset by trained helpers. Do not stand below a load being rolled off.
breathing: Brace for the pickup. Breathe again in the lap and take breaths during any carry.
commonErrors: Load hangs away: hug it closer.
Hands get trapped: change grip in the lap and clear the fingers.
Back leans far back: reduce load or platform height.
ref-Atlas_Stone_Trainer.easierOption: Use fewer plates and keep all fittings secure.
ref-Atlas_Stone_Trainer.safety: Learn the lap and release with a strongman coach. Awkward loads can slip. Keep feet out of the drop zone and never catch a falling object.
ref-Atlas_Stone_Trainer.loadConvention: Enter the total mass of the trainer and its plates. Count each completed lift from floor to standing as one rep.

terms.meaning: Rest the object across the thighs while sitting back to change the grip.

ref-Atlas_Stones.summary: A lift from the floor to a platform, using a lap and a close chest hold.
setup: Use a load you can hold close. Clear the path and drop area.
Check the stone for cracks and sharp spots.
Use a platform that supports the whole object without tipping or rolling. Start next to it before adding a carry.
Stand with the object between your feet. Bend your hips and knees and reach around it with both arms.
execution: Pull the object close to your trunk and push through the feet to lift it past your knees. Keep the load near you rather than curling it out in front.
Sit back a little and settle it securely on your thighs. This lap position lets you reset your grip.
Hug it high against your chest and drive the hips and knees to stand. Keep the hands clear of any place the object can pinch them.
If a carry is part of the set, use short steps to reach the platform. Keep the object close and eyes on the path.
Extend the hips and knees enough to guide the object onto the platform. Push it fully onto the top, keeping fingers out from underneath.
finish: Make sure the object is supported before letting go. Step clear of its possible fall path.
Use a planned, controlled return or have the platform reset by trained helpers. Do not stand below a load being rolled off.
breathing: Brace for the pickup. Breathe again in the lap and take breaths during any carry.
commonErrors: Load hangs away: hug it closer.
Hands get trapped: change grip in the lap and clear the fingers.
Back leans far back: reduce load or platform height.
ref-Atlas_Stones.easierOption: Use a lighter, smaller object and a lower platform; start without a carry.

ref-Keg_Load.summary: A keg pickup, carry and load onto a platform.
setup: Use a load you can hold close. Clear the path and drop area.
Check the keg edges, handles and fill closure. Loose fill can shift.
Use a platform that supports the whole object without tipping or rolling. Start next to it before adding a carry.
Tilt the keg slightly to take the near handle and the far bottom rim. Keep both hands clear of the edge as it rolls toward you.
execution: Pull the object close to your trunk and push through the feet to lift it past your knees. Keep the load near you rather than curling it out in front.
Sit back a little and settle it securely on your thighs. This lap position lets you reset your grip.
Hug it high against your chest and drive the hips and knees to stand. Keep the hands clear of any place the object can pinch them.
If a carry is part of the set, use short steps to reach the platform. Keep the object close and eyes on the path.
Extend the hips and knees enough to guide the object onto the platform. Push it fully onto the top, keeping fingers out from underneath.
finish: Make sure the object is supported before letting go. Step clear of its possible fall path.
Use a planned, controlled return or have the platform reset by trained helpers. Do not stand below a load being rolled off.
breathing: Brace for the pickup. Breathe again in the lap and take breaths during any carry.
commonErrors: Load hangs away: hug it closer.
Hands get trapped: change grip in the lap and clear the fingers.
Back leans far back: reduce load or platform height.

ref-Backward_Drag.summary: A backward sled drag held in the hands.
setup: Choose a flat lane with grip and space to slow down. Check that the surface permits sled use. Load plates evenly and secure them.

execution: Sit back a little while keeping the chest lifted.
Take short backward steps, extending one knee at a time to pull the sled. Keep steady tension without yanking the straps.
Stay in the marked lane; use a helper to watch for obstacles behind you.
finish: Shorten the steps and stop the sled under control at the end of the lane.
Let the sled take the full load before releasing handles or removing a harness. Step out of the strap without crossing a moving sled.
breathing: Keep breathing through the steps. For the press, breathe out as the hands move forward; reset without a long breath hold.
commonErrors: Load stops every step: remove plates and keep a smooth pull.
Back sags: shorten the body lean and tighten the middle.

ref-Backward_Drag.safety: Use fittings rated for the sled. Do not wrap ropes around the hands or neck. Keep bystanders outside the lane and stop if the sled catches or your shoes slip.
ref-Backward_Drag.loadConvention: Enter the total sled-and-plate mass if known; use the same sled and surface for comparisons. Log active time in seconds and distance in meters in the Distance field. Surface drag changes the effort, so mass alone does not describe difficulty.

ref-Farmers_Walk.summary: A walk with a separate weight held in each hand.
setup: Use a level, clear route. Choose the end point before lifting and leave room to set the load down without trapping feet.
Check all collars, pins, handles and attachments. Load the implement evenly and confirm its empty weight before logging load.
Stand between matched handles. Bend hips and knees, take each grip in its center, and brace with arms long.
execution: Push through both feet to raise the implement. Stand steady before taking the first step.
Take short controlled steps along the lane. Keep the load steady and look where you are going.
Keep ribs over hips and shoulders steady. Breathe through the carry; stop before grip or posture fails.
finish: Slow down and stop with the load still balanced.
Bend the hips and knees to lower it onto its feet or starting support. Keep toes clear and hold until the implement is fully supported.
breathing: Take a breath and brace for the pickup. Keep taking breaths during the walk; do not hold one breath for the whole carry.
commonErrors: Long rushed steps make the load swing: shorten the stride.
Shoulders or trunk tip to one side: reduce the load and check equal loading.
Breath is held for the whole walk: use smaller breaths while keeping the middle firm.
ref-Farmers_Walk.easierOption: Use less load and a shorter route. Begin with a still hold before adding walking.
ref-Farmers_Walk.safety: Do not run with an unstable carry or try to catch a tipped frame. Keep others clear of the path and use a load you can put down before your grip gives out.
ref-Farmers_Walk.loadConvention: Enter the mass of one fully loaded handle when both match; both hands carry that load, so total carried mass is twice the entered value. Log time in seconds and distance in meters in the Distance field.

Pick up the weights with arms near the body. Check that you can lower them safely before starting the timer.
execution: Raise both arms out to the sides until near shoulder height.
Hold the intended arm angle without shrugging, bending sideways or leaning back.
Keep wrists in line with the forearms and take steady breaths.
End the hold when the arm height drops or posture changes.
finish: Lower both weights slowly toward the sides. Set them down with hips and knees bent.
breathing: Breathe normally during the hold. Ease the load if you cannot keep breathing.

ref-Chain_Handle_Extension.summary: A lying elbow extension using chains attached to two handles. More links lift from the floor as the hands rise.

ref-Circus_Bell.summary: A two-hand clean to one shoulder followed by a one-arm circus-dumbbell push press.
setup: Check the thick handle, heads and any loading closure. Use a light implement while learning its balance.
Place it between the feet. Bend hips and knees and take the handle with both hands.
Clear the platform and learn how to release a missed lift before attempting the full movement.
execution: Drive the legs and hips to bring the bell close and up to one shoulder.
Set one head securely behind the shoulder as the handle settles in the working hand. Remove the helping hand once the bell is stable.
Dip the knees with a firm trunk, then drive upward and press with the working arm.
Finish with a straight arm and the weight balanced above the shoulder; do not force a large side bend.
finish: Guide a manageable bell back to the shoulder and then down with both hands, bending the legs.

ref-Log_Lift.summary: A log clean followed by a push press using the log’s inside neutral-grip handles.

Tip the log toward the body and drive the hips to roll it up onto the upper chest.
Settle it on the chest with elbows forward and trunk firm. Move the head only enough to clear the log.
Dip at the knees, then drive the legs tall and press to straight arms overhead.
Hold the log balanced over the body before lowering.
finish: Guide a manageable log to the chest while bending the knees to soften contact, then return through the lap to the floor.
For a missed lift, use a practiced release on a clear platform. Do not reach for the falling log.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Log stays away in the clean: lap it close before rolling.
Low back bends far backward: reduce load and stack ribs over hips.
Press begins before rack is stable: pause at the chest.
ref-Log_Lift.easierOption: Use a lighter log and practice the lap-to-chest clean before adding the press.
ref-Log_Lift.safety: The log can block your view and roll toward the face. Learn the rack and release with coaching, and do not lower a heavy log onto the neck.
ref-Log_Lift.loadConvention: Enter the total log-and-plate mass. One clean from the floor plus one overhead press and return is one rep; note any extra presses separately.
ref-Log_Lift.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

terms.meaning: Tighten the muscles around your middle to keep the trunk steady.
Rest the object across the thighs while sitting back to change the grip.

ref-Power_Stairs.summary: A strongman lift that places a handled implement onto successive raised steps.
setup: Check the handle and all load fittings. Use a light implement with room for both hands.
Use steps made for the load, with enough tread depth for the whole implement. Clear the sides and the route down.
Stand with feet wide enough for the implement between them. Bend hips and knees and take a centered two-hand grip.
execution: Push through the feet and extend hips and knees to raise the implement close to the body.
Guide it onto the next step with the arms long enough to avoid curling the load.
Set its full base down and check it is stable before moving your feet.
Step up in balance, reset the grip and repeat to the next planned step.
finish: Stop when the implement is fully supported. Use a planned equipment reset; do not drag it backward down stairs toward your feet.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Swinging far from the body: use less load and a lower step.
Only the edge lands on the step: stop and place the whole base securely.
Hands or toes enter the gap: move clear before lowering.
ref-Power_Stairs.easierOption: Practice one lift onto a low, broad platform before using a staircase.
ref-Power_Stairs.safety: Falling loads can crush hands or feet. Use purpose-built steps and learn the event with coaching. Do not use an unstable stack of boxes.
ref-Power_Stairs.loadConvention: Enter the total implement mass. Count each stable placement onto the next step as one rep. Record step height and number of steps in notes.
ref-Power_Stairs.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Tire_Flip.summary: A tire lift and push that rolls a large tire onto its opposite side.
setup: Inspect the tire for wire, sharp edges and slippery tread. Use a tire you can start without bending your arms into a curl.
Clear the whole fall area on the far side. Stand close with feet slightly back, chest against the tread and hands under a firm lower edge.
Bend hips and knees, keep arms long and set the back in a steady position.
execution: Drive forward into the tire and up through the legs and hips.
As it rises toward upright, step closer and use a knee against the tread only as a controlled support.
Change the hands from the low lifting grip to a higher pushing position without putting fingers under the falling edge.
Push the tire past its balance point, then move back and let it fall into the clear lane.
finish: Wait until the tire stops moving before setting up again. Walk around to the starting side without stepping into its fall path.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Trying to curl the tire: keep arms long and drive with legs.
Standing too far away: bring the chest to the tread.
Chasing the falling tire: let go and step clear.
ref-Tire_Flip.easierOption: Use a lighter tire and practice the change from lift to push with a coach.
ref-Tire_Flip.safety: Never try to catch a tire tipping toward you or another person. Stop if grip slips or the start pulls sharply on the elbows. Keep people off the far side.
ref-Tire_Flip.loadConvention: Enter the known tire mass if available. One complete flip onto the other side is one rep. Note tire size; equal mass does not mean equal difficulty.
ref-Tire_Flip.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Split_Jerk.summary: A jerk from the front shoulders to an overhead split stance.
setup: Set hooks just below shoulder height. Place the bar across the front shoulders, hands under it and elbows a little forward.
Stand the bar clear of the rack and step into open space. Set feet about hip-width and brace.
Choose the lead foot before the rep. Practice the split without load, keeping width between the feet from side to side.
execution: Dip a short way by bending the knees while the trunk stays upright.
Drive straight up with the legs, then push yourself under the rising bar.
Move one foot forward and the other back. Catch with arms straight, both knees bent and the rear heel raised.
Hold the bar steady over the body. Move the front foot partway back, then the rear foot forward until the feet are level.
finish: Stand still with the bar under control before ending the rep.
Lower a light bar close to your body, bending your knees to soften its return. With bumper plates on a cleared platform, use the release method you have learned. Never try to catch a falling bar.
breathing: Take a breath and brace before the lift. Breathe out as you finish, then reset.
commonErrors: Front foot lands on the same narrow line as the back foot: keep some width.
Rear knee locks: receive with a soft back knee.
Bar moves forward: keep the dip vertical and reduce the load.
ref-Split_Jerk.easierOption: Use a stick or training bar and practice the split and recovery separately.
ref-Split_Jerk.safety: Learn the catch and how to let go of a missed lift with a weightlifting coach before adding load. Use a platform and plates made for this task. Keep others out of the drop area. Do not chase a falling bar.
ref-Split_Jerk.loadConvention: Enter the total weight of the bar and all plates. One full lift and return is one rep.
ref-Split_Jerk.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

terms.meaning: Tighten the muscles around your middle to keep the trunk steady.
Either the bar stand, or the position where the bar rests on your shoulders.

ref-Jogging_Treadmill.summary: A jog on a powered treadmill. Speed moves the belt; incline changes the slope.
setup: Check that the belt is still and the space behind the machine is clear. Tie laces and keep loose items away from the belt.
Find the normal stop control and emergency stop. Clip the safety cord to your clothing if the treadmill has one.
Use the rails to get into the manufacturer’s starting position. Choose manual mode and start at a slow walking speed.
Begin walking in the middle of the belt before raising speed or incline. Change one control at a time.
execution: Build gradually to a comfortable jog. Keep eyes ahead and shoulders relaxed.
Use steps that land close beneath you. Let the arms swing naturally rather than pulling your body along with the rails.
Stay near the middle of the belt and adjust speed down if you drift toward its back.
Reduce the pace before reaching for water or changing a setting that distracts you.
finish: Lower speed to an easy walk to finish. Press stop and wait until the belt is fully still.
Use the rails to step off, then remove the safety clip. Never jump onto or off a fast belt.
breathing: Breathe in a steady rhythm. Choose a pace where breathing stays under control; lower the speed if you cannot keep that rhythm.
commonErrors: Holding the rails for the whole workout: lower speed or incline until you can move steadily.
Looking down at the feet: look ahead and keep the pace manageable.
Long reaching steps: shorten the stride.
ref-Jogging_Treadmill.easierOption: Use a slower walk and flatter incline for a shorter bout.
ref-Jogging_Treadmill.safety: Stop the belt if you feel faint, lose balance or have pain. Keep children, pets and loose items away from the moving belt and its rear edge.
ref-Jogging_Treadmill.loadConvention: Log minutes of movement. Add distance in meters in the Distance field if useful, and record speed and incline in notes. No lifting load is logged.
ref-Jogging_Treadmill.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Bicycling_Stationary.summary: Seated pedaling on a stationary upright bike.
setup: Find the resistance and stop controls before pedaling. Check that the machine is steady.
Adjust the seat while off the bike. At the farthest pedal position, keep a small bend in the knee without the hips rocking or reaching.
Set handlebar reach so shoulders can relax and elbows stay slightly bent. Use the fixed handle to help mount.
Lock the seat adjustment fully. Put the balls of the feet over the pedals and secure straps snugly if provided.
execution: Start pedaling with low resistance and a smooth, easy rhythm.
Keep the knees pointing with the feet and the hips still on the seat.
Add a little resistance only while you can turn the pedals smoothly without bouncing or pushing hard into the handles.
Keep the torso tall and relaxed and avoid reaching with the toes at the far point.
finish: Turn resistance down and pedal easily before stopping.
Wait until the pedals stop, release the foot straps and use the fixed handles to get off.
breathing: Breathe steadily through the ride. Use a pace you can sustain without holding your breath.
commonErrors: Hips rock side to side: check the seat height or distance.
Knees lock out: bring the seat closer or lower it.
Shoulders tense: relax the grip and reduce resistance.
ref-Bicycling_Stationary.easierOption: Use lower resistance and shorter bouts with the same well-fitted seat position.
ref-Bicycling_Stationary.safety: Do not adjust a loose seat while pedaling. On bikes with pedals that keep turning, use the bike’s braking method and wait before removing the feet.
ref-Bicycling_Stationary.loadConvention: Log minutes. Record bike model, resistance level and optional distance in notes or the Distance field in meters. Resistance levels are not kilograms or pounds.
ref-Bicycling_Stationary.sourceNote: Editorial rewrite of the exact Free Exercise DB exercise record (Unlicense) named in the first link. The added manufacturer page supports seat fit and locking on its model. Use the adjustment controls on the actual bike.

Adjust the seat while off the bike. At the farthest pedal position, keep a small bend in the knee without the hips rocking or reaching.
Set the seat distance so the back stays comfortably against the pad. Use the seat-side handle when getting in.
Lock the seat adjustment fully. Put the balls of the feet over the pedals and secure straps snugly if provided.
execution: Start pedaling with low resistance and a smooth, easy rhythm.
Keep the knees pointing with the feet and the hips still on the seat.
Add a little resistance only while you can turn the pedals smoothly without bouncing or pushing hard into the handles.
Keep the torso supported by the back pad and avoid reaching with the toes at the far point.
finish: Turn resistance down and pedal easily before stopping.
Wait until the pedals stop, release the foot straps and use the fixed handles to get off.
breathing: Breathe steadily through the ride. Use a pace you can sustain without holding your breath.

ref-Bicycling.summary: Outdoor bicycle riding with a steady pedaling rhythm.
setup: Choose a bicycle that fits and a route suited to your riding skills. Check tires, brakes, wheels and the seat clamp before leaving.
Set the saddle so the knee still has a small bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke without rocking the hips.
Wear a correctly fitted helmet and secure loose clothing. Check lights and visibility needs for the route.
Practice starting, turning and stopping in a clear safe area before entering traffic.
execution: Start in an easy gear and pedal smoothly with both hands ready on the controls.
Keep shoulders relaxed, elbows soft and eyes scanning ahead.
Change to an easier gear before a climb makes you strain or rock on the saddle.
Use the brakes smoothly and slow before turns, rough ground or busy crossings.
finish: Ease the pace before the end. Check the area and brake to a controlled stop.
Put a foot down only when stable, then dismount clear of traffic.
breathing: Keep breathing steadily. Choose an easier gear or slower pace when breathing becomes hard to control.
commonErrors: Seat too high makes the hips rock: adjust it before riding.
Gear too hard stalls the pedals: shift easier.
Looking only at the front wheel: look farther along the route.
ref-Bicycling.easierOption: Use a flat quiet route at an easy pace for a shorter ride.
ref-Bicycling.safety: Follow local road rules and give yourself space to stop. Keep attention on the route; stop safely before using a phone or changing equipment.
ref-Bicycling.loadConvention: Log riding time in minutes. Add distance in meters in the Distance field and note route or terrain. No lifting load is logged.
ref-Bicycling.sourceNote: Editorial rewrite of the exact Free Exercise DB exercise record (Unlicense) named in the first link. The original exact record has only a short seat-adjustment cue. NHTSA supplies general cycling-safety context; fit and riding steps are plain-language editorial guidance.

ref-Elliptical_Trainer.summary: A low-impact stepping cycle on an elliptical trainer, with feet staying on the pedals.
setup: Find the stop control and read the start directions on the machine. Check that pedals are still before mounting.
Hold the fixed rail and place one foot on the lower pedal, then the other on its pedal. Keep feet fully supported.
Choose low resistance and a low ramp setting if the model has one.
Start with the fixed handles until you know the pedal path. Use moving handles only when they can be reached without leaning.
execution: Push through one pedal, then the other, letting the linked pedals follow their oval path.
Keep the knees pointing with the toes and a small bend in the legs.
Stand tall with shoulders relaxed. Use a light hand grip and keep the hips centered.
Build pace smoothly; lower resistance if you bounce, rock or lean on the handles.
finish: Reduce pace and resistance gradually. Let the pedals come to a complete stop.
Hold the fixed rails while stepping off one foot at a time. Do not step from a moving pedal.
breathing: Keep a steady breathing rhythm. Slow the pedal pace if you cannot keep breathing comfortably.
commonErrors: Leaning heavily on the handles: reduce effort and stand tall.
Heels lift far on each stroke: check foot position and shorten the stride if adjustable.
Knees fall inward: slow down and follow the toe line.
ref-Elliptical_Trainer.easierOption: Use low resistance and fixed handles for a shorter bout.
ref-Elliptical_Trainer.safety: Pedals may keep moving after you stop pushing. Wait for them to settle before dismounting, and keep clothing away from the moving arms.
ref-Elliptical_Trainer.loadConvention: Log minutes. Note machine model, resistance and ramp setting. Console levels are not lifting weights.
ref-Elliptical_Trainer.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Rowing_Stationary.summary: A rowing-machine stroke that uses legs, then body, then arms to pull, and reverses that order to return.
setup: Check the seat track is clear. Sit down, place heels in the foot cradles and adjust them so the straps cross the broad part of each foot.
Tighten straps enough to hold the feet securely, without pain. Set a modest resistance and choose a simple time display.
Take the handle with a light overhand grip and straight wrists. Slide forward until shins are near upright.
Keep arms long, shoulders relaxed and the trunk tipped slightly forward from the hips.
execution: Push with the legs first while arms stay straight.
As the legs straighten, swing the trunk from a slight forward lean to a slight backward lean.
Finish by bending the elbows to draw the handle below the ribs. Keep wrists flat.
For the return, straighten arms, tip forward from the hips, then bend knees once hands have passed them.
Slide forward calmly and repeat in one smooth rhythm.
finish: Ease the effort for the last strokes and let the handle return under control.
Place it in its holder, loosen straps and step off once the seat is still.
breathing: Breathe out through the drive and breathe in during the easy return, or use another steady rhythm you can maintain.
commonErrors: Arms pull first: start the stroke with the legs.
Knees rise before hands pass: send arms forward first.
Large backward lean: keep the trunk swing small.
ref-Rowing_Stationary.easierOption: Use gentler strokes and practice the sequence slowly before adding force.
ref-Rowing_Stationary.safety: Keep fingers clear of the seat rollers and avoid a rounded or sharply arched back. Do not yank the handle against the return cord.
ref-Rowing_Stationary.loadConvention: Log rowing minutes. Add distance in meters in the Distance field and note machine setting. Do not enter the damper setting as a lifting load.
ref-Rowing_Stationary.sourceNote: Editorial rewrite of the exact Free Exercise DB exercise record (Unlicense) named in the first link. The exact record supplies the exercise identity. Concept2 supplies the drive and recovery order; setup and logging are editorial guidance.

ref-Stairmaster.summary: Alternating downward presses on a two-pedal stair stepper. This record describes pedals, not rotating stairs.
setup: Find the stop control before getting on. Wait for the machine to be still and use the fixed rails to mount.
Place both feet fully on the pedals. Choose a low setting and begin with short, controlled pedal strokes.
Keep your torso upright and your hands light on the rails. Check that clothing and laces are clear of moving parts.
execution: Shift your weight onto one foot, then the other to press the pedals down in a steady rhythm.
Keep knees pointing with toes and use the whole foot rather than only the toes.
Do not drive either pedal hard into its bottom stop. Keep both feet following the pedal path.
Lower the speed if you must hang from the rails or cannot place each foot well.
finish: Slow the machine and press stop while holding the fixed rails.
Wait for all motion to stop, then use the rails to step down onto the fixed floor.
breathing: Breathe steadily as you step. Lower the speed if you cannot keep the rhythm or must hold your breath.
commonErrors: Body hangs on rails: lower speed and stand more upright.
Only toes touch: place more of the foot on the step or pedal.
Feet rush or cross: slow down and keep each foot in its own path.
ref-Stairmaster.easierOption: Use a lower speed and shorter bout. Begin with the model’s smallest controlled step motion.
ref-Stairmaster.safety: Do not turn around, skip steps or use a phone on a moving stair machine. Keep the stop control within reach and get off only after motion stops.
ref-Stairmaster.loadConvention: Log minutes. Note the exact machine and speed or level; rotating stairs and pedal steppers are different tasks. No lifting load is logged.
ref-Stairmaster.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Step_Mill.summary: Climbing moving stairs on a step mill.

Place the whole foot on a step with enough room ahead of the toes. Begin at the slowest comfortable stair speed.
Keep your torso upright and your hands light on the rails. Check that clothing and laces are clear of moving parts.
execution: Shift your weight onto one foot, then the other to climb each arriving step.
Keep knees pointing with toes and use the whole foot rather than only the toes.
Lift each foot enough to clear the next step. Stay away from the bottom edge of the moving stairway.
Lower the speed if you must hang from the rails or cannot place each foot well.
finish: Slow the machine and press stop while holding the fixed rails.
Wait for all motion to stop, then use the rails to step down onto the fixed floor.
breathing: Breathe steadily as you step. Lower the speed if you cannot keep the rhythm or must hold your breath.

ref-Rope_Jumping.summary: Repeated small jumps over a rope turned by the hands.
setup: Choose a rope length that clears the head and feet without a large arm swing. Check handles and rope for damage.
Clear space overhead, behind and beside you. Avoid a slick floor or a surface with holes.
Hold a handle in each hand near the hips, elbows close to the sides. Start with the rope behind the heels.
execution: Turn the rope forward mostly with the wrists.
As it reaches the feet, make a small two-foot jump just high enough to clear it.
Land softly with knees unlocked and keep the feet near the same spot.
Repeat a quiet rhythm. If the rope catches, stop and reset rather than hopping through a tangle.
finish: Let the rope stop in front of you and place both feet firmly down.
Walk easily before another bout and move the rope out of any walkway.
breathing: Breathe steadily with the jump rhythm. Pause when you cannot keep both the breathing and foot timing controlled.
commonErrors: Large arm circles: keep elbows closer and turn with wrists.
High jumps: lower the jump to reduce hard landings.
Rigid knees: soften each landing.
ref-Rope_Jumping.easierOption: Turn the rope more slowly, or practice small rope-free hops before joining the movements.
ref-Rope_Jumping.safety: Stop when the feet slap loudly, balance changes or calf or foot pain begins. Keep others out of the rope’s full arc.
ref-Rope_Jumping.loadConvention: Log active jumping minutes. Note the rope type and any planned intervals. No lifting load is logged.

ref-Skating.summary: Cardio skating on roller or inline skates, using alternating pushes and glides.
setup: Check wheels, brakes and fastenings. Use skates that fit firmly without numbness.
Choose a dry smooth area away from traffic. Learn the stopping method for your skate type before building speed.
Put on protective gear and stand with knees soft and feet about hip-width. Keep eyes forward.
execution: Push one foot gently out and back, then glide on the other.
Bring the pushing foot back under the hips and change sides.
Keep knees bent enough to balance, with the trunk slightly forward and arms ready for balance.
Use short controlled pushes and wide easy turns until the route and stopping distance are clear.
finish: Reduce the push size and use your learned braking method well before the finish point.
Stop in a clear place before removing equipment. Do not aim for a wall or person as a brake.
breathing: Use a steady easy breathing rhythm. Reduce speed before fatigue affects balance or braking.
commonErrors: Knees lock: lower the hips a little.
Feet spread too far: bring each foot back beneath you.
Speed grows beyond braking skill: shorten the pushes and use a flatter area.
ref-Skating.easierOption: Practice short glides and stops on a flat clear surface before continuous skating.
ref-Skating.safety: Avoid wet surfaces, loose stones and steep slopes. Do not skate fast until you can turn and stop reliably in the same conditions.
ref-Skating.loadConvention: Log skating minutes. Add distance in meters in the Distance field if measured, and note the surface. No lifting load is logged.
ref-Skating.sourceNote: Based on the exercise linked below from Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). Setup, finish and logging instructions were added for this guide.

ref-Trail_Running_Walking.summary: Walking or running on a trail with pace adjusted to hills, footing and visibility.
setup: Choose a route that fits your current walking or running skill. Check weather, daylight, access and how you will return.
Use shoes with grip for the surface. Carry needed water and let someone know the route when appropriate.
Begin on an easy section. Scan ahead for roots, stones, holes, mud and other trail users.
execution: Use shorter steps as the trail gets steep or uneven.
Walk steep or rough sections when that gives better control; a walking section is part of the same outing.
On descents, reduce speed and keep knees soft rather than reaching far downhill with a stiff leg.
Keep looking a few steps ahead and choose a clear foot placement before shifting weight.
finish: Ease to a walk near the end and finish on stable ground.
Stop before checking a map, tying a shoe or drinking if doing so would distract you from footing.
breathing: Keep breathing under control. Walk or slow down on climbs when you need to recover a steady rhythm.
commonErrors: Long downhill steps: shorten the stride and slow down.
Eyes stay on the distant view: check nearby foot placements too.
Running every section: walk where footing needs more care.
ref-Trail_Running_Walking.easierOption: Choose a flatter, shorter, familiar trail and walk the full route.
ref-Trail_Running_Walking.safety: Turn back when weather, light or trail conditions exceed your preparation. Give yourself room to stop near edges and crossings; speed should follow the terrain.
ref-Trail_Running_Walking.loadConvention: Log active minutes. Add distance in meters in the Distance field and note terrain or elevation. No lifting load is logged.

lib-small-jump-reset.variant: Small two-foot jump with a full landing reset
lib-small-jump-reset.summary: A low bodyweight jump from two feet. Hold each landing before standing and starting the next rep. This is a landing practice drill, with no height target.
setup: Clear loose weights, mats and people from the landing area. Check that the floor and your shoes do not slide.
Stand with your feet about hip-width apart. Keep your toes facing forward or slightly out.
First bend your hips and knees a little, then stand without leaving the floor. Use this to check comfort and balance.
Keep your hands free. Start with small jumps only; do not hold weights or jump from a box.
execution: Bend your hips and knees a little. Let your arms move naturally beside you.
Push through both feet to make a small upward jump. Stay near your starting spot.
Land on both feet. Let your ankles, knees and hips bend to absorb the landing. Keep knees in line with your feet.
Hold the landing until steady. Then stand tall and fully reset before the next rep.
Count one jump and its steady landing as one rep. End the set if you cannot hold the landing.
finish: Stand still after the final landing. Walk clear once you feel steady.
Take the full planned rest before another set. Do not turn the drill into continuous jumps.
breathing: Breathe normally between reps. Avoid a long breath hold.
commonErrors: Trying to jump as high as possible. This drill uses a small jump.
Starting another rep before the landing is steady.
Letting the knees fall inward or landing with stiff knees.
lib-small-jump-reset.easierOption: Practice the small hip-and-knee bend and return to standing without leaving the floor. Record that separately as non-jumping practice.
lib-small-jump-reset.safety: Stop for pain, dizziness or loss of balance. New users and youth need qualified instruction and supervision. This drill does not establish readiness for depth jumps or sport competition.
lib-small-jump-reset.loadConvention: Bodyweight; record the total number of completed jumps with a steady landing. Do not enter body weight as external load. Optional notes can describe the surface and landing control.
lib-small-jump-reset.sourceNote: App-authored low-intensity practice variation. NSCA sources support movement mastery, appropriate instruction and accounting for other training. This exact drill wording, sets, reps and schedule limits are product choices; the sources do not validate this as an individualized prescription.
quickCues: Make a small jump from two feet.
Bend your hips and knees as you land.
Hold the landing, then fully reset.
